Cell image segmentation is a crucial task in biomedical image analysis, as it enables the quantification and analysis of cellular structures.
In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning architecture called Feedback U-net for cell image segmentation.
The proposed architecture incorporates a feedback mechanism that allows the model to iteratively refine its predictions.
This feedback mechanism is achieved by introducing skip connections between the encoder and decoder blocks of the U-net architecture.
Additionally, we introduce a novel loss function that combines both pixel-wise and boundary-aware terms to improve the accuracy of the segmentation.
We evaluate the performance of the Feedback U-net on several benchmark datasets and compare it with other state-of-the-art methods.

Overall, our study provides valuable insights into the behavior of particles in high dimensions and contributes to the understanding of complex systems in statistical physics.

Coherent averaging is a technique used in signal processing to improve the signal-to-noise ratio of a measured signal.
This paper presents a comprehensive review of coherent averaging, including its theoretical foundations, practical implementation, and applications in various fields such as radar, sonar, and medical imaging.
The paper discusses the basic principles of coherent averaging, including the concept of coherence and the effects of averaging on signal quality.
It also explores different methods for implementing coherent averaging, such as time-domain averaging, frequency-domain averaging, and adaptive averaging.
The paper further examines the limitations and challenges associated with coherent averaging, such as the trade-off between averaging time and signal resolution, and the impact of non-stationary signals.
Finally, the paper highlights the potential future developments and research directions in the field of coherent averaging.

This paper presents a method for computing valid p-values for image segmentation using selective inference.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision and involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions.
Traditional methods for computing p-values in this context often suffer from multiple testing issues, leading to inflated false positive rates.
The proposed method addresses this problem by leveraging selective inference, which allows for valid inference while controlling the false discovery rate.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments on various image segmentation datasets, showing improved accuracy compared to existing methods.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of image segmentation by offering a reliable and statistically sound method for computing p-values.

Automated weed detection in aerial imagery is an important task in precision agriculture, as it can help farmers identify and manage weed infestations more effectively.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for automated weed detection in aerial imagery that takes into account the context of the surrounding vegetation.
We first segment the aerial imagery into different regions based on color and texture features.
Then, we extract features from each region and train a deep learning model to classify them as either weed or non-weed.
To incorporate context information, we use a graph-based approach to model the relationships between the different regions.
Experimental results on a large dataset of aerial imagery demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving high accuracy in weed detection.

Skin lesion segmentation plays a crucial role in the early detection and diagnosis of skin diseases.
In this paper, we propose a deep convolutional encoder-decoder network with aggregated multi-resolution skip connections for accurate skin lesion segmentation.
The network architecture consists of an encoder network that extracts high-level features and a decoder network that reconstructs the segmentation mask.
We introduce skip connections at multiple resolutions to enable the network to capture both local and global contextual information.
Additionally, we aggregate the skip connections to enhance the segmentation performance.
Experimental results on a publicly available skin lesion dataset demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.

MultiResUNet is a novel architecture proposed for multimodal biomedical image segmentation, which aims to improve the performance of the U-Net architecture.
The U-Net architecture has been widely used for biomedical image segmentation tasks, but it has limitations in handling multimodal images due to its single-scale feature extraction.
MultiResUNet addresses this limitation by introducing a multi-resolution strategy, which incorporates multiple scales of features into the network.
This is achieved by using residual connections and a modified U-Net structure.
The proposed architecture is evaluated on two publicly available datasets for brain tumor segmentation and retinal vessel segmentation.
The results show that MultiResUNet outperforms the U-Net architecture in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability.

This paper presents a high-order adaptive Gegenbauer integral spectral element method for solving nonlinear optimal control problems.
The method combines the advantages of the Gegenbauer integral spectral element method and the adaptive mesh refinement technique to achieve high accuracy and efficiency in solving optimal control problems.
The Gegenbauer integral spectral element method is used to discretize the state and adjoint equations, while the adaptive mesh refinement technique is employed to adaptively refine the mesh in regions of high solution gradients.
The resulting method is capable of accurately solving optimal control problems with high-order accuracy and efficiency.
Numerical experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method.
The results show that the method is able to achieve high accuracy and efficiency in solving a variety of optimal control problems.

Compositionality refers to the ability to reason about the behavior of a system by analyzing the behavior of its components.
The paper argues that compositionality is a desirable property for QIF frameworks, as it allows for modular analysis and reasoning about complex systems.
The authors propose a formal definition of compositionality for QIF and present a compositional framework for reasoning about information flow.
They demonstrate the usefulness of their approach through several case studies and provide insights into the challenges and limitations of achieving compositionality in QIF.

This paper proposes a novel approach for training multi-organ segmentation networks using sample selection by relaxed upper confident bound.
The authors argue that current methods for training such networks often suffer from the problem of imbalanced training data, leading to poor performance on underrepresented organs.
To address this issue, they introduce a sample selection strategy based on the relaxed upper confident bound, which aims to select informative samples that can improve the network's performance on underrepresented organs.
The proposed method is evaluated on a large dataset of abdominal CT scans and compared with several state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves the segmentation accuracy for underrepresented organs, outperforming existing methods.
The authors conclude that the sample selection strategy based on relaxed upper confident bound is an effective approach for training multi-organ segmentation networks.

Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions.
Traditional methods for image segmentation often rely on handcrafted features or pixel-level clustering algorithms, which may not be able to capture the complex structures and textures present in real-world images.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for image segmentation using sparse subset selection.
Our method leverages the sparsity-inducing properties of the L1 norm to select a subset of informative pixels that best represent the underlying image structure.
We formulate the image segmentation problem as an optimization problem and solve it using a greedy algorithm.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed method compared to state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms.

Anomaly detection is a critical task in various domains, including cybersecurity, finance, and healthcare.
Traditional anomaly detection methods often suffer from high false positive rates and limited adaptability to changing data distributions.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for anomaly detection based on sequential testing.
We formulate the problem as a sequential hypothesis testing problem and derive an asymptotically optimal solution using the likelihood ratio test.
Our method is able to adaptively adjust the detection threshold based on the observed data, leading to improved detection performance compared to traditional methods.
We evaluate the performance of our approach on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its superiority in terms of both detection accuracy and computational efficiency.

This paper presents a deep-structured fully-connected random field model for structured inference.
The proposed model combines the strengths of deep learning and random fields to capture complex dependencies in structured data.
The model is trained using a variational inference algorithm that maximizes the evidence lower bound.
Experimental results on various structured prediction tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model in capturing dependencies and achieving state-of-the-art performance.
The model also shows robustness to missing data and noise, making it suitable for real-world applications.
Overall, this paper contributes to the field of structured inference by introducing a novel deep learning approach that can handle complex structured data.

Collective chemotaxis, the directed movement of a group of cells in response to a chemical gradient, is a fundamental process in many biological systems.
It is commonly assumed that individual cells sense and respond to the gradient, leading to coordinated movement.
However, recent studies have suggested that collective chemotaxis can emerge even in the absence of single-cell gradient sensing.
In this paper, we present a theoretical model and experimental evidence to support this idea.
Our model incorporates cell-cell communication and mechanical interactions between cells, allowing for the emergence of collective chemotaxis.
We demonstrate that this emergent behavior can arise from simple rules governing cell movement and communication, without the need for individual cells to sense the gradient.

DeepAtlas is a novel approach for joint semi-supervised learning of image registration and segmentation.
The paper proposes a deep learning framework that leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to simultaneously learn the tasks of image registration and segmentation.
The proposed method utilizes a dual-branch network architecture, where one branch is responsible for image registration and the other for segmentation.
The two branches are trained jointly using a combination of supervised and unsupervised loss functions.
Experimental results on various medical imaging datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of both registration accuracy and segmentation performance.
The paper also provides insights into the benefits of using unlabeled data for improving the performance of both tasks.

Deep learning methods have shown promising results in segmenting cardiac MRI images, but their trustworthiness is still a concern.
In this paper, we propose a framework to increase the trustworthiness of deep learning segmentation methods on cardiac MRI.
We introduce a novel uncertainty estimation technique that provides a measure of confidence for each pixel in the segmentation map.
We also propose a data augmentation strategy to improve the robustness of the deep learning model.
We evaluate our framework on a large dataset of cardiac MRI images and compare it with existing segmentation methods.
Our results show that our framework improves the trustworthiness of deep learning segmentation methods by providing more accurate and reliable segmentations.

Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in various clinical applications.
However, obtaining accurate and reliable segmentation labels for medical images is often challenging due to the high cost and time required for manual annotation.
In this paper, we propose a semi-supervised contrastive learning approach for label-efficient medical image segmentation.
Our method leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to learn a representation space where similar instances are brought closer and dissimilar instances are pushed apart.
We introduce a novel contrastive loss function that encourages the model to learn discriminative features for segmentation.
We evaluate our approach on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy while requiring fewer labeled samples.

Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image.
Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been widely used for this task, but they often struggle with capturing long-range dependencies and producing accurate boundaries.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Convolutional Conditional Random Fields (CRFs) for semantic segmentation.
Our method combines the strengths of CNNs and CRFs by integrating a CRF layer into the CNN architecture.
This allows us to model the spatial dependencies between pixels and improve the accuracy of the segmentation.
We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and boundary quality.

This paper presents a performance analysis of linear-equality-constrained least-squares (LSE) estimation.
The LSE estimation problem is formulated as a constrained optimization problem, where the objective is to minimize the sum of squared errors subject to linear equality constraints.
The performance of LSE estimation is analyzed in terms of bias, variance, and mean squared error (MSE).
The analysis is conducted for both the unconstrained and constrained cases, and the results are compared.
It is shown that the constrained LSE estimator can have lower bias and variance compared to the unconstrained estimator, leading to a lower MSE.
The analysis is supported by numerical simulations, which demonstrate the effectiveness of the constrained LSE estimator in various scenarios.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the non-LTE radiative transfer in cool stars, focusing on the theory and applications to the abundance analysis for 24 chemical elements.
The authors develop a detailed theoretical framework for non-LTE radiative transfer in cool stars, taking into account various physical processes such as collisional excitation, ionization, and recombination.
They then apply this framework to analyze the abundances of 24 chemical elements in a sample of cool stars, using observational data from high-resolution spectroscopy.
The results show that the non-LTE effects are significant for many elements, leading to revised abundance determinations compared to LTE assumptions.
The authors discuss the implications of these findings for our understanding of stellar evolution and nucleosynthesis processes.
Overall, this study provides a valuable contribution to the field of stellar astrophysics and highlights the importance of considering non-LTE effects in abundance analysis for cool stars.

This paper introduces a novel approach called multi-utility learning for structured-output learning tasks with multiple annotation-specific loss functions.
Traditional structured-output learning methods typically use a single loss function to optimize the model parameters.
However, in many real-world applications, different annotations may have different levels of importance or uncertainty, and using a single loss function may not capture this heterogeneity.
The proposed multi-utility learning framework addresses this issue by allowing the use of multiple annotation-specific loss functions.
The authors present a theoretical analysis of the framework and demonstrate its effectiveness through experiments on various structured-output learning tasks, including image segmentation and natural language processing.
The results show that the multi-utility learning approach outperforms traditional methods in terms of accuracy and robustness, highlighting its potential for improving performance in real-world applications.

The Casimir force is a fundamental phenomenon in physics that arises from quantum fluctuations of the electromagnetic field.
Accurate measurements of the Casimir force are important for testing theoretical predictions and understanding the underlying physics.
In this paper, we explore the potential contributions of noncontact atomic force microscopy (NC-AFM) for future Casimir force measurements.
NC-AFM is a powerful technique that allows for high-resolution imaging and manipulation of nanoscale objects without physical contact.
We discuss the advantages of NC-AFM for Casimir force measurements, including its ability to measure forces in a wide range of distances and its potential for reducing systematic errors.
We also discuss the challenges and limitations of using NC-AFM for Casimir force measurements, such as the need for precise calibration and the influence of surface roughness.

The spectrum averaging is carried out to improve the signal-to-noise ratio.
The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through experiments on various materials.

Video segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision, with applications in various domains such as autonomous driving and video surveillance.
However, existing methods for video segmentation often suffer from high computational costs, limiting their real-time performance.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Separable Convolutional LSTMs (SC-LSTMs) for faster video segmentation.
SC-LSTMs leverage the separability property of convolutional operations to reduce the number of parameters and computational complexity.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of SC-LSTMs on several benchmark datasets and show that our approach achieves comparable or even better segmentation accuracy than state-of-the-art methods while significantly reducing the computational time.
Our results indicate that SC-LSTMs have the potential to enable real-time video segmentation in resource-constrained environments.

This paper presents a real-time high-performance semantic image segmentation method for urban street scenes.
The proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results.
The network is trained on a large-scale dataset of street scene images with pixel-level annotations.
The method incorporates several key techniques, including dilated convolutions, atrous spatial pyramid pooling, and skip connections, to improve the segmentation performance.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and speed.
The method achieves real-time performance on a standard GPU, making it suitable for various applications such as autonomous driving and urban planning.

Vision Transformers (ViTs) have recently emerged as a powerful approach for image classification tasks.
However, training ViTs effectively requires careful consideration of data, augmentation, and regularization techniques.
In this paper, we investigate the impact of different data strategies, augmentation methods, and regularization techniques on the performance of ViTs.
We conduct extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets and analyze the results to provide insights into the best practices for training ViTs.
Our findings demonstrate the importance of large-scale datasets, diverse augmentation techniques, and regularization methods such as dropout and weight decay.
We also propose a novel regularization technique called patch-level dropout, which improves the performance of ViTs by encouraging the model to attend to different parts of the image.

This paper presents a mathematical model and control strategy for an active constrained layer (ACL) beam actuated by two voltage sources, with and without magnetic effects.
The ACL beam is composed of a piezoelectric layer and a constraining layer, and is subjected to an external magnetic field.
The mathematical model is derived using the Euler-Bernoulli beam theory and the constitutive equations for the piezoelectric and magnetic materials.
The control strategy is based on a combination of feedback and feedforward control techniques.
Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model and control strategy in achieving accurate and robust control of the ACL beam.
The findings of this study have potential applications in the design and control of ACL beams for various engineering applications.

This paper presents an experimental analysis of the graph properties of the social graph on Twitter.
The social graph represents the connections between users on the platform, and understanding its properties can provide insights into the structure and dynamics of the Twitter network.
We collected a large dataset of Twitter users and their connections over a period of time, and analyzed various graph properties such as degree distribution, clustering coefficient, and community structure.
Our results show that the Twitter social graph exhibits characteristics of a scale-free network, with a few highly connected users and many users with few connections.
We also observed a high clustering coefficient, indicating the presence of tightly connected communities within the network.
Furthermore, we identified several distinct communities based on the community detection algorithm, suggesting the presence of different interest groups or communities on Twitter.

The Super-Kamiokande experiment is a large water Cherenkov detector located in Japan that has been used to study solar neutrinos for over two decades.
In this paper, we present the results from the fourth phase of the Super-Kamiokande experiment (Super-Kamiokande-IV), which ran from 2008 to 2014.
We discuss the improvements made to the detector during this phase, including the addition of new photomultiplier tubes and a water purification system.
We also describe the data analysis techniques used to measure the flux and energy spectrum of solar neutrinos.
Our results are consistent with previous measurements and provide further evidence for the existence of neutrino oscillations.
We also discuss the implications of our measurements for solar physics and neutrino physics.

Boosting algorithms are a popular class of machine learning algorithms that combine weak learners to create a strong learner.
The dual formulation of boosting algorithms has been proposed as an alternative to the traditional primal formulation.
In this paper, we provide a comprehensive analysis of the dual formulation of boosting algorithms.
We show that the dual formulation offers several advantages over the primal formulation, including improved convergence rates and better generalization performance.
We also propose a novel dual boosting algorithm and demonstrate its effectiveness through extensive experiments on various datasets.
Our results suggest that the dual formulation of boosting algorithms has the potential to significantly enhance the performance of boosting algorithms in practice.

The paper provides an overview of game theory concepts and techniques, and then applies them to wireless power control scenarios.
The authors present several game-theoretic models for wireless power control, including non-cooperative games, cooperative games, and evolutionary games.
The paper also discusses the potential benefits and challenges of using game theory in wireless power control, and provides insights into how game theory can be used to optimize power control strategies in wireless networks.

This paper proposes a novel approach for learning to steer a vehicle by mimicking features from heterogeneous auxiliary networks.
The authors argue that existing methods for autonomous driving often rely on a single auxiliary network, which may not capture all relevant information for steering.
To address this limitation, the authors propose a framework that combines multiple auxiliary networks, each trained on a different task related to driving.
The proposed framework leverages a feature mimicking module to transfer knowledge from the auxiliary networks to the steering network.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of steering accuracy and generalization to unseen scenarios.
The findings of this study have implications for the development of more robust and reliable autonomous driving systems.

This paper investigates the generation of linear and non-linear Alfven waves in the coronal funnels through impulsive processes.
The authors use a 2.5D magnetohydrodynamic model to simulate the dynamics of the coronal funnels and study the generation and propagation of Alfven waves.
They find that impulsive energy release events, such as magnetic reconnection and plasma instabilities, can generate both linear and non-linear Alfven waves in the coronal funnels.
The linear waves are found to propagate along the magnetic field lines, while the non-linear waves exhibit wave steepening and shock formation.
The authors also analyze the effects of different parameters, such as the plasma density and magnetic field strength, on the generation and propagation of the Alfven waves.
Overall, this study provides insights into the impulsive generation of Alfven waves in the coronal funnels and their potential role in the heating and dynamics of the solar corona.

This paper proposes a novel approach for blurry boundary delineation using semantic-guided encoder feature learning.
Blurry boundary delineation is a challenging task in computer vision, as it requires accurately identifying and segmenting object boundaries in images with low resolution or blurriness.
The proposed approach leverages the power of deep learning and semantic information to improve the accuracy of blurry boundary delineation.
Specifically, a semantic-guided encoder is trained to learn discriminative features that capture both low-level image details and high-level semantic information.
These features are then used to generate precise boundary maps for blurry images.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of boundary accuracy and robustness to blur.

This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation using 3D models.
Traditional image segmentation methods often struggle with complex scenes and objects due to the lack of contextual information.
In this work, we propose to leverage 3D models to assist the image segmentation process.
We first reconstruct a 3D model of the scene or object using depth information.
Then, we use this 3D model to guide the image segmentation algorithm by incorporating geometric constraints.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in improving the accuracy and robustness of image segmentation, especially in challenging scenarios.

This paper proposes a novel approach for polyp segmentation using deep ensembles based on Stochastic Activation Selection (SAS).
The authors argue that current methods for polyp segmentation often suffer from high false positive rates and low accuracy.
To address these issues, they introduce SAS, which randomly selects a subset of activation maps from a deep neural network during training.
This stochastic selection process helps to reduce overfitting and improve generalization performance.
The authors evaluate their approach on a large dataset of colonoscopy images and compare it to several state-of-the-art methods.
The results show that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy and lower false positive rates, demonstrating its effectiveness for polyp segmentation.

This paper presents a novel method for automated segmentation of retinal layers from optical coherent tomography (OCT) images using geodesic distance.
The proposed method utilizes the concept of geodesic distance to accurately identify the boundaries between different retinal layers.
The method is based on a graph representation of the OCT image, where each pixel is represented as a node and the edges represent the geodesic distance between pixels.
The geodesic distance is calculated using a fast marching algorithm.
The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of OCT images and compared with existing segmentation methods.
The results show that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.

The authors also provide a detailed analysis of the proposed method and discuss its advantages and limitations.

This paper presents a novel approach for background-foreground segmentation in the context of interior sensing in the automotive industry.
Interior sensing systems are becoming increasingly important for various applications such as driver monitoring, occupant detection, and gesture recognition.
Accurate segmentation of the background and foreground is a crucial step in these systems, as it allows for the extraction of relevant information from the scene.
However, existing methods often struggle with challenging scenarios such as low lighting conditions, occlusions, and complex backgrounds.
In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based approach that leverages the power of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to achieve robust and accurate background-foreground segmentation.
Our method utilizes a combination of spatial and temporal information to improve the segmentation performance.

Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that involves assigning a semantic label to each pixel in an image.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Convolutional Random Walk Networks (CRWN) for semantic image segmentation.
CRWN combines the strengths of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and random walk algorithms to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results.
The proposed method utilizes a CNN to extract high-level features from the input image and then applies a random walk algorithm to refine the segmentation boundaries.
We evaluate the performance of CRWN on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that CRWN achieves competitive performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

This paper presents a method for disaggregating Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP)
Level 3 (L3) brightness temperatures to a finer spatial resolution of 9km using kernel machines.
The proposed method utilizes a training dataset consisting of high-resolution brightness temperatures and corresponding low-resolution SMAP L3 brightness temperatures.
The kernel machines are trained to learn the relationship between the high-resolution and low-resolution data, and then used to predict the high-resolution brightness temperatures for the entire SMAP L3 dataset.
The results show that the proposed method achieves a high level of accuracy in disaggregating the SMAP L3 brightness temperatures, with a mean absolute error of less than 1K.
This method has the potential to improve the spatial resolution of SMAP L3 data, enabling more accurate monitoring and analysis of soil moisture at a finer scale.

This paper proposes a novel approach for efficient single-image segmentation using Gaussian dynamic convolution.
The traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) used for segmentation tasks often suffer from high computational costs and memory requirements.
To address this issue, the authors introduce a dynamic convolutional layer that adaptively selects a subset of input feature maps based on their relevance to the current input image.
This is achieved by modeling the relevance as a Gaussian distribution and using it to weight the feature maps.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves comparable segmentation performance to state-of-the-art methods while significantly reducing computational costs and memory requirements.
Overall, this work presents a promising approach for efficient single-image segmentation using Gaussian dynamic convolution.

Segmentation of medical images is a critical task in medical imaging analysis, as it provides valuable information for diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, the accuracy of segmentation algorithms is often evaluated using ground truth annotations, which are prone to human error.
In this paper, we propose a method to disentangle human error from the ground truth in segmentation of medical images.
We introduce a novel framework that combines multiple expert annotations and leverages inter-observer variability to estimate the true underlying segmentation.
Our method is evaluated on a dataset of medical images and compared to traditional ground truth annotations.
The results demonstrate that our approach effectively reduces the impact of human error on segmentation accuracy, providing a more reliable evaluation metric for segmentation algorithms.

Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image.
Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown promising results in this field, but they often suffer from overfitting due to the large number of parameters.
In this paper, we propose a regularized CNN architecture for semantic image segmentation.
Our approach incorporates a regularization term into the loss function to prevent overfitting and improve generalization.
We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art approaches.
The experimental results demonstrate that our regularized CNN achieves competitive performance while reducing overfitting.

This paper presents an approach for adaptive automatic threat recognition within 3D computed tomography (CT) images for baggage security screening.
The proposed approach utilizes a deep learning framework to automatically detect and classify potential threats within CT images.
The framework is trained on a large dataset of annotated CT images, allowing it to learn and recognize various types of threats.
Additionally, the approach incorporates an adaptive learning mechanism that continuously updates the model based on new data, improving its performance over time.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high accuracy in threat detection and classification.
The adaptive nature of the approach also allows it to adapt to new and emerging threats, making it a valuable tool for enhancing baggage security screening systems.

This paper proposes a novel approach called Deeply Supervised Active Learning (DSAL) for biomedical image segmentation.
The goal is to leverage both strong and weak labelers to improve the performance of deep learning models.
DSAL combines active learning and deep supervision techniques to iteratively select informative samples for annotation and train a deep learning model.
The proposed method is evaluated on two biomedical image segmentation tasks and compared with other active learning methods.
The results demonstrate that DSAL outperforms existing approaches and achieves state-of-the-art performance.
The findings suggest that DSAL can effectively leverage both strong and weak labelers to improve the accuracy of biomedical image segmentation models.

This paper proposes a method for enforcing mutual consistency of hard regions in semi-supervised medical image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach for brain tumor segmentation using an ensemble of 3D U-Nets and overall survival prediction using radiomic features.
The proposed method combines the strengths of multiple 3D U-Nets to improve the accuracy of tumor segmentation.
Additionally, radiomic features extracted from the segmented tumor regions are used to predict the overall survival of patients.
The experimental results demonstrate that the ensemble of 3D U-Nets achieves superior segmentation performance compared to individual U-Nets.
Furthermore, the radiomic features show promising predictive power for overall survival.
This research contributes to the field of medical image analysis by providing an effective and accurate method for brain tumor segmentation and survival prediction.

This paper presents a self-supervised learning approach for cardiac magnetic resonance (MR) image segmentation by predicting the anatomical position of the heart.
The proposed method leverages the inherent spatial information in cardiac MR images to learn meaningful representations without the need for manual annotations.
The authors introduce a novel network architecture that combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a recurrent neural network (RNN) to predict the anatomical position of the heart from a given image patch.
The network is trained using a self-supervised learning framework, where the predicted anatomical position is used as a surrogate task to guide the learning of the segmentation task.
Experimental results on a large dataset of cardiac MR images demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in cardiac MR image segmentation, outperforming existing supervised and unsupervised methods.
The authors also provide a detailed analysis of the learned representations and show that the network learns to capture anatomical structures and spatial relationships between different cardiac regions.

This paper presents a method for guided proofreading of automatic segmentations in connectomics, a field that aims to reconstruct the complete wiring diagram of the brain.
Automatic segmentation algorithms are commonly used to generate initial segmentations, but they often produce errors that need to be corrected manually.
The proposed method combines the strengths of both automatic and manual proofreading by providing a user-friendly interface that allows users to correct errors efficiently.
The method incorporates machine learning techniques to predict potential errors and suggest corrections, reducing the time and effort required for manual proofreading.
The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through experiments on real connectomics datasets, showing significant improvements in segmentation accuracy compared to manual proofreading alone.
The proposed method has the potential to greatly accelerate the process of connectomics research and contribute to a better understanding of the brain's structure and function.

This paper proposes a domain adaptive medical image segmentation method using adversarial learning of disease-specific spatial patterns.
The method aims to address the challenge of limited labeled data in medical image segmentation tasks by leveraging unlabeled data from different domains.
The proposed approach consists of two main components: a segmentation network and a domain adaptation network.
The segmentation network is trained to perform pixel-wise segmentation on labeled data, while the domain adaptation network learns to align the feature distributions between the labeled and unlabeled data.
The domain adaptation network includes a generator and a discriminator, which are trained in an adversarial manner to generate domain-invariant features.
Experimental results on two medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving segmentation performance on unseen domains.

This paper presents a novel approach for crowd-based object segmentation using clickstream analysis with confidence.
The proposed method leverages the collective intelligence of a crowd to accurately segment objects in images.
The clickstream data collected from multiple users is analyzed to identify the most reliable and consistent segmentation regions.
A confidence measure is then computed for each segment to assess its accuracy.
Experimental results on a large dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving high-quality object segmentation.
The findings of this study have implications for various applications in computer vision and image processing.

The proposed method aims to accurately classify terrain regions into traversable and non-traversable areas.
The normal-based segmentation technique is used to segment the terrain into homogeneous regions based on the surface normals.
Superpixel surface analysis is then performed to extract features from the segmented regions.
These features are used to train a support vector machine classifier to classify the terrain regions.
Experimental results on real-world stereo images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately analyzing terrain traversability.

This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation using maximin affinity learning.
Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision, and it involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions.
Traditional methods for image segmentation often rely on handcrafted features or heuristics, which may not generalize well to different types of images.
In this paper, we propose a new framework that learns the affinity matrix for image segmentation using a maximin objective function.
The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning to automatically learn discriminative features from the input images.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.

The paper proposes a novel deep learning architecture called Attention U-Net for automatic pancreas segmentation in abdominal CT scans.
The proposed architecture incorporates an attention mechanism that allows the network to focus on relevant regions of the input image, improving the accuracy of pancreas segmentation.
The attention mechanism is integrated into the U-Net architecture by introducing a gating mechanism that learns to assign importance weights to different spatial locations.
The proposed Attention U-Net is trained and evaluated on a large dataset of abdominal CT scans, achieving state-of-the-art performance in pancreas segmentation.
The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the attention mechanism in guiding the network to focus on the pancreas region, leading to improved segmentation accuracy.
The proposed architecture has the potential to enhance the performance of automated pancreas segmentation algorithms, which can have significant implications for clinical applications such as surgical planning and disease diagnosis.

This paper presents a novel approach for multi-object segmentation using shape priors based on gradient vector flow (GVF).
The proposed method aims to optimize the segmentation process by incorporating shape priors into the energy functional.
The shape priors are represented by GVF, which captures the global shape information of the objects.
The energy functional is formulated as a combination of data term and shape prior term, and is minimized using an iterative optimization algorithm.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving accurate and robust multi-object segmentation.
The proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.

By training on a large dataset of accurate quantum chemistry calculations, the $\Delta$-Machine Learning approach can then predict the differences between approximate and accurate calculations for new molecules.
This allows for the rapid and accurate estimation of quantum chemistry properties for a wide range of molecules, without the need for computationally expensive accurate calculations.
The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the $\Delta$-Machine Learning approach through a series of experiments on various molecular systems, showing significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional quantum chemistry approximations.
Overall, the $\Delta$-Machine Learning approach has the potential to revolutionize the field of quantum chemistry by enabling the rapid and accurate estimation of quantum chemistry properties for large-scale molecular systems.

Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a class label to each pixel in an image.
In recent years, deep learning models, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have achieved remarkable success in semantic segmentation.
However, CNNs have limitations in capturing long-range dependencies and modeling global context.
In this paper, we propose a new model called Segmenter, which is based on the Transformer architecture.
The Transformer has shown great success in natural language processing tasks, but its application to computer vision tasks, especially semantic segmentation, is relatively unexplored.
We adapt the Transformer to the semantic segmentation task by introducing a novel self-attention mechanism that operates on the spatial dimensions of the feature maps.

This paper proposes a novel approach for segmentation across domains using importance-driven continual learning.
The authors argue that existing methods for domain adaptation in segmentation tasks often fail to generalize well to new domains due to the lack of importance weighting.
To address this issue, they introduce a framework that leverages importance-driven continual learning to adapt the segmentation model to new domains.
The proposed method incorporates a dynamic importance weighting mechanism that assigns higher weights to more important samples during training.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving state-of-the-art performance in segmentation across domains.
The authors conclude that importance-driven continual learning is a promising direction for improving the generalization capability of segmentation models in diverse domains.

Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that requires accurate and efficient models.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Densely Connected Neural Architecture Search (DCNAS) for semantic image segmentation.
DCNAS combines the advantages of neural architecture search (NAS) and dense connectivity to automatically discover high-performing architectures for this task.
We introduce a search space specifically designed for semantic image segmentation and use reinforcement learning to search for the optimal architecture.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DCNAS achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of different components in DCNAS.

The stability and accuracy of the method are analyzed, and it is shown that the method achieves exponential convergence for smooth functions.
The efficiency of the method is demonstrated through numerical experiments, where it is compared to other pseudospectral methods.
The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
Overall, this paper provides a novel and effective approach for solving differential equations using pseudospectral methods.

Atrous convolution, also known as dilated convolution, has been widely used in recent years to improve the performance of semantic image segmentation models.
However, the current approach of using atrous convolution in a deep neural network has limitations in terms of capturing both local and global contextual information.
In this paper, we propose a new approach called "Rethinking Atrous Convolution" that addresses these limitations.
Our approach involves using multiple atrous rates in parallel to capture both local and global contextual information.
We also introduce a new module called the "ASPP" (Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling) module, which further enhances the performance of our approach.

In many real-world applications, training data is often labeled with noise, which can significantly degrade the performance of machine learning models.
This paper proposes a novel approach to improve training on noisy structured labels.
The proposed method leverages the inherent structure in the labels to identify and correct noisy instances during training.
Specifically, a graph-based model is used to represent the label structure, and a noise detection algorithm is applied to identify noisy instances.
These noisy instances are then corrected using a label correction algorithm that takes into account the label structure.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving the accuracy of machine learning models trained on noisy structured labels.

This paper proposes a novel approach for initializing the weights of a deep neural network for image segmentation tasks using meta-learning.
The authors argue that the choice of initial weights can greatly impact the performance of the network, and traditional random or pre-trained initializations may not be optimal for segmentation tasks.
They introduce a meta-learning framework that learns to initialize the weights of the network based on the characteristics of the specific segmentation task.
The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets and compared against traditional initialization methods.
The results show that the meta-learned initializations consistently outperform the other methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the segmentation tasks.
The authors conclude that meta-learning can be a powerful tool for improving the initialization of deep neural networks for image segmentation.

White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are commonly observed in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans and are associated with various neurological disorders.
Accurate segmentation of WMH is crucial for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning.
Recently, the U-net architecture has shown promising results in WMH segmentation.
However, the performance of U-net can be affected by the random initialization of its weights, leading to inconsistent segmentation results.
In this paper, we propose a post-processing method to improve the segmentation accuracy of randomly-initialized U-net for WMH.
Our method utilizes a combination of intensity thresholding, morphological operations, and region growing to refine the initial segmentation results.

This paper explores the application of deep learning techniques for cardiac magnetic resonance (MR) image segmentation.
Specifically, the authors investigate the performance of 2D and 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in segmenting various structures in cardiac MR images, such as the left ventricle, right ventricle, and myocardium.
The study compares the accuracy and efficiency of these two approaches, considering factors such as training time, computational resources, and segmentation performance.
The results demonstrate that both 2D and 3D CNNs can achieve accurate segmentation results, but with different trade-offs.
The 2D CNNs are faster and require less computational resources, while the 3D CNNs offer better segmentation accuracy.
The findings of this study provide valuable insights for researchers and practitioners in the field of cardiac MR image segmentation, aiding in the selection of appropriate deep learning techniques for specific applications.

Superpixels are compact and perceptually meaningful regions that can be used for various computer vision tasks.
The proposed method utilizes a bottom-up approach to construct a hierarchy of superpixels by iteratively merging adjacent superpixels based on their similarity.
The algorithm takes into account both color and spatial information to ensure that the resulting hierarchy captures the underlying structure of the image.
The paper provides a detailed description of the algorithm and evaluates its performance on various benchmark datasets.
The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.

Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is a widely used optimization algorithm in machine learning, particularly for training deep neural networks.
In recent years, there has been a trend towards using larger batch sizes in SGD, motivated by the desire to take advantage of parallel computing resources and reduce the variance of the gradient estimates.
However, this paper argues that large batch sizes can lead to computational inefficiency, as the time required to compute each gradient update increases significantly with the batch size.
The authors provide theoretical analysis and empirical evidence to support their claim, showing that the benefits of larger batch sizes in terms of reduced variance are often outweighed by the increased computational cost.
They also propose a hybrid approach that combines the benefits of large and small batch sizes, achieving a good trade-off between computational efficiency and convergence speed.
Overall, this paper highlights the importance of carefully choosing the batch size in SGD to achieve efficient and effective optimization.

This paper presents a study of the magnetic properties of Co/Ti bilayer thin films using ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) spectroscopy.
The Co/Ti bilayer thin films were prepared using magnetron sputtering technique and their magnetic properties were characterized using FMR measurements.
The FMR spectra were analyzed to determine the magnetic anisotropy and damping parameters of the Co/Ti bilayer thin films.
The results showed that the magnetic anisotropy of the Co/Ti bilayer thin films can be controlled by varying the thickness of the Ti layer.
The damping parameter was found to be dependent on the Co layer thickness.
These findings provide valuable insights into the magnetic properties of Co/Ti bilayer thin films and can be useful for the development of magnetic devices and spintronic applications.

In this paper, we present a numerical study of a model that describes a quantum particle interacting with a quantum environment.
The model is based on the concept of a quantum bath, which represents the environment as a collection of harmonic oscillators.
We use numerical techniques to solve the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for the system and study the dynamics of the particle in the presence of the environment.
We investigate the effects of different parameters, such as the coupling strength between the particle and the bath, on the behavior of the system.
Our results show that the presence of the environment can significantly affect the dynamics of the particle, leading to phenomena such as decoherence and dissipation.
We also discuss the implications of our findings for the understanding of quantum systems in realistic environments.

This paper examines the dynamics of conflicts in Wikipedia, a popular online collaborative encyclopedia.
The study analyzes the patterns and characteristics of conflicts that arise within the Wikipedia community, as well as the factors that contribute to their escalation or resolution.
The research utilizes a combination of quantitative and qualitative methods, including data mining and content analysis, to identify and analyze conflict-related events and their outcomes.
The findings reveal that conflicts in Wikipedia are multifaceted and can be triggered by various factors, such as content disputes, personal conflicts, and power struggles.
The study also highlights the role of community norms, governance mechanisms, and dispute resolution processes in managing and resolving conflicts.
The implications of these findings for the sustainability and effectiveness of online collaborative platforms are discussed, along with recommendations for improving conflict management strategies in Wikipedia and similar online communities.

VoteNet is a deep learning label fusion method proposed for multi-atlas segmentation.
The method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn the relationship between the input image and the corresponding label maps from multiple atlases.
The CNN is trained using a large dataset of labeled images and then used to predict the label maps for new images.
The predicted label maps are then combined using a voting scheme to generate the final segmentation result.
Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that VoteNet outperforms existing label fusion methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The proposed method has the potential to improve the performance of multi-atlas segmentation in various medical imaging applications.

Oligomers are small aggregates of proteins that have been implicated in various neurodegenerative diseases.
The model takes into account the formation and degradation of oligomers, as well as their interaction with cellular components.
The model is based on experimental data and incorporates parameters such as oligomer concentration, degradation rate, and binding affinity.
Simulation results show that the model accurately predicts the dynamics of oligomer formation and their impact on cell viability.
The model can be used to study the effects of different factors on oligomer formation and to identify potential therapeutic targets for preventing or reversing cell damage caused by oligomers.

The abstract for the academic paper titled "Effect of electron irradiation on superconductivity in single crystals of Ba(Fe$_{1-x}$Ru$_{x}$)$_2$As$_2$ ($x=$0.24)" is as follows:

This paper investigates the effect of electron irradiation on the superconductivity of single crystals of Ba(Fe$_{1-x}$Ru$_{x}$)$_2$As$_2$ with a Ru doping level of $x=$0.24.
The samples were irradiated with high-energy electrons at various doses, and their superconducting properties were measured using resistivity and magnetization measurements.
It was found that electron irradiation significantly suppressed the superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$) and reduced the superconducting volume fraction.
The critical current density ($J_c$) was also reduced after irradiation.
These results suggest that electron irradiation induces defects and disorder in the crystal structure, leading to the suppression of superconductivity in Ba(Fe$_{1-x}$Ru$_{x}$)$_2$As$_2$ single crystals.
The findings of this study provide valuable insights into the effects of irradiation on the superconducting properties of iron-based superconductors.

TFLMS: Large Model Support in TensorFlow by Graph Rewriting

Abstract:

Deep learning models have become increasingly complex and require large amounts of memory to train and deploy.
However, existing deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow have limitations in handling large models due to memory constraints.
In this paper, we propose TFLMS, a novel approach to address this issue by introducing large model support in TensorFlow through graph rewriting.
TFLMS leverages the concept of graph rewriting to dynamically allocate and deallocate memory for model parameters, allowing for efficient training and deployment of large models.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of TFLMS through experiments on various deep learning tasks, including image classification and natural language processing.
Our results show that TFLMS significantly reduces memory usage and improves training and inference performance compared to existing approaches.

Deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success in various domains, but their inner workings remain largely opaque.
This paper proposes a divide-and-conquer approach to gain a better understanding of deep networks.
The approach involves breaking down the network into smaller subnetworks and analyzing their behavior individually.
By studying the subnetworks, we can gain insights into the network's decision-making process and identify important features and patterns.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving interpretability and providing valuable insights into the functioning of deep networks.
The findings of this study contribute to the broader goal of making deep networks more transparent and explainable.

This paper presents a comprehensive and comparative study on the importance of image enhancement techniques in color image segmentation.
Image segmentation is a crucial step in various computer vision applications, and accurate segmentation results heavily rely on the quality of the input image.
Image enhancement techniques aim to improve the quality of images by reducing noise, enhancing contrast, and improving overall visual appearance.
In this study, we evaluate the impact of different image enhancement techniques on color image segmentation algorithms.
We compare the performance of various segmentation algorithms on both original and enhanced images using quantitative evaluation metrics.
Our results demonstrate that image enhancement techniques can significantly improve the accuracy and robustness of color image segmentation algorithms.

This paper presents a semi-supervised multi-organ segmentation method using deep multi-planar co-training.
The proposed method leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the segmentation accuracy.
The deep multi-planar co-training framework consists of two deep neural networks, one for axial plane segmentation and the other for coronal plane segmentation.
The networks are trained using a combination of labeled and unlabeled data, where the unlabeled data is used to generate pseudo-labels.
The generated pseudo-labels are then used to train the networks in a co-training manner, where the networks learn from each other's predictions.
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior segmentation performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.

Image registration is a fundamental task in computer vision and medical imaging, where the goal is to align two or more images of the same scene or object.
However, image registration is challenging due to the presence of intensity variations and geometric distortions in the images.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Most Likely Separation of Intensity and Warping Effects (MLS-IWE) to address this problem.
MLS-IWE leverages a probabilistic model to separate the intensity variations and warping effects in the images, allowing for more accurate and robust image registration.
We evaluate the performance of MLS-IWE on various datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that MLS-IWE outperforms existing approaches in terms of registration accuracy and robustness.

This paper proposes a novel approach for image segmentation using end-to-end deep convolutional active contours.
Traditional active contour models rely on handcrafted features and require manual initialization, which can be time-consuming and prone to errors.
In contrast, the proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network to learn discriminative features directly from the input image.
The network is trained in an end-to-end manner, allowing it to automatically initialize and refine the active contour.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed approach has the potential to significantly improve image segmentation tasks in various domains, such as medical imaging and computer vision.

This paper proposes a few-shot segmentation method for medical images using meta-learning with implicit gradients.
The method aims to address the challenge of limited annotated data in medical image segmentation tasks.
The proposed approach leverages a meta-learning framework to learn a model that can quickly adapt to new segmentation tasks with only a few annotated samples.
The model is trained using a combination of explicit and implicit gradients, which allows for efficient and effective adaptation to new tasks.
Experimental results on various medical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving accurate and robust segmentation with limited annotated data.
The proposed approach has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical image segmentation tasks, which can have significant implications for clinical applications.

The Lab color space is known for its ability to separate color information from luminance information, making it suitable for image segmentation tasks.
The proposed method first converts the input image to the Lab color space and then applies K-means clustering to segment the image into different regions.
The algorithm is evaluated on a dataset of embryo egg images and compared with other segmentation methods.
The results show that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy and better segmentation results compared to the other methods.
This approach has potential applications in the field of embryo egg detection and can contribute to advancements in reproductive biology and animal breeding.

This paper presents a robust output regulation framework for continuous-time periodic systems.
The proposed approach is based on the internal model principle and uses a dynamic output feedback controller to achieve robust regulation of the system's output.
The controller is designed to handle uncertainties and disturbances in the system dynamics and to ensure robustness against external disturbances.
The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through numerical simulations on a benchmark example.
The results show that the controller is able to achieve robust output regulation even in the presence of uncertainties and disturbances.
Overall, the paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of robust control for continuous-time periodic systems.

Cloud detection and segmentation in satellite imagery is a crucial task for various applications, including weather forecasting and climate studies.
In this paper, we propose an effective cloud detection and segmentation algorithm based on gradient analysis.
The algorithm utilizes the gradient information of the satellite imagery to identify cloud regions accurately.
We apply this algorithm to improve the performance of the PERSIANN-CCS (Precipitation Estimation from Remotely Sensed Information using Artificial Neural Networks-Cloud Classification System) for cloud detection and segmentation.
Experimental results demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
The improved PERSIANN-CCS with our algorithm achieves higher accuracy in cloud detection and segmentation, leading to more accurate precipitation estimation.

This paper proposes a weakly-supervised approach for semantic segmentation using motion cues.
Traditional semantic segmentation methods require pixel-level annotations, which are expensive and time-consuming to obtain.
In this work, we leverage the fact that motion cues can provide valuable information about object boundaries and use them to guide the segmentation process.
We introduce a novel motion-guided attention mechanism that learns to focus on regions with significant motion, thereby improving the accuracy of the segmentation.
We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that it achieves competitive performance compared to fully-supervised methods while requiring only weak supervision in the form of video-level labels.
Our results suggest that motion cues can be a valuable source of information for weakly-supervised semantic segmentation tasks.

The proposed framework combines multiple base segmentation models to improve the accuracy and robustness of the segmentation results.
The ensemble learning framework consists of three main components: base segmentation models, diversity generation, and fusion.
The base segmentation models are trained independently using different algorithms or architectures.
The diversity generation component introduces diversity among the base models by applying various data augmentation techniques.
The fusion component combines the outputs of the base models to generate the final segmentation result.

The paper "Edge Clique Cover of Claw-free Graphs" investigates the edge clique cover problem in claw-free graphs.
The edge clique cover problem involves finding a minimum number of cliques that cover all the edges in a graph.
Claw-free graphs are a special class of graphs that do not contain a claw as an induced subgraph.
The authors provide a polynomial-time algorithm for finding an edge clique cover in claw-free graphs.
They also prove that the problem is NP-complete for general graphs.
The paper concludes with experimental results that demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm on various instances of claw-free graphs.

This paper presents a shape-aware semi-supervised approach for 3D semantic segmentation of medical images.
The proposed method leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the segmentation accuracy.
The shape information is incorporated into the segmentation process through a shape-aware regularization term, which encourages the segmentation to adhere to the underlying anatomical structures.
The semi-supervised learning framework is formulated as a graph-based optimization problem, where the labeled and unlabeled data are represented as nodes in a graph and the segmentation labels are propagated through the graph using a diffusion process.
Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy.
The shape-aware regularization term effectively improves the segmentation quality by preserving the anatomical structures.

This paper presents a weakly-supervised learning approach for catheter segmentation in 3D frustum ultrasound images.
The proposed method leverages a combination of weak annotations and a novel loss function to train a deep neural network for accurate catheter segmentation.
The weak annotations are obtained by projecting 2D annotations onto the 3D frustum ultrasound images.
The novel loss function incorporates both pixel-level and region-level information to guide the network training.
Experimental results on a large dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in catheter segmentation, outperforming existing weakly-supervised and fully-supervised methods.
The proposed approach has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of catheter segmentation in clinical applications.

This paper presents observations of active latitude oscillations on the Sun, which are periodic variations in the latitudinal position of active regions.
These oscillations have been observed using data from the Solar Dynamics Observatory and the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager.
The authors analyze the data to determine the characteristics of these oscillations, including their period and amplitude.
They find that the active latitude oscillations have a period of approximately 11 years, which is consistent with the solar cycle.
The amplitude of the oscillations varies over time, with larger amplitudes observed during periods of high solar activity.
The authors also investigate the possible causes of these oscillations, including the influence of the solar dynamo and the interaction between the Sun's magnetic field and its differential rotation.

ObjectAug: Object-level Data Augmentation for Semantic Image Segmentation

Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that requires accurate labeling of each pixel in an image with its corresponding object class.
Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance in this task, but they often require large amounts of labeled data for training.
Data augmentation techniques have been widely used to artificially increase the size of the training dataset and improve the generalization ability of the models.
However, most existing data augmentation methods operate at the image level and do not consider the object-level information.


In this paper, we propose ObjectAug, a novel object-level data augmentation method for semantic image segmentation.
ObjectAug leverages the object-level annotations in the training dataset to generate realistic and diverse augmented samples.

This paper investigates the sliding friction behavior of a power-law fluid in the hydrodynamic lubrication regime.
The authors conducted experiments using a custom-built tribometer to measure the friction coefficient as a function of sliding velocity and applied load.
The results show that the friction coefficient decreases with increasing sliding velocity and reaches a minimum value at a critical velocity.
Additionally, the friction coefficient increases with increasing applied load.
The authors propose a theoretical model based on the Reynolds equation and the power-law fluid rheology to explain the observed friction behavior.
The model predicts the critical velocity and the friction coefficient as a function of sliding velocity and applied load, which are in good agreement with the experimental data.

Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image.
Existing methods often rely on deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to learn discriminative features for accurate segmentation.
However, these methods often suffer from high computational costs and limited generalization ability.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Double Similarity Distillation (DSD) for semantic image segmentation.
DSD leverages the concept of similarity distillation to transfer knowledge from a teacher network to a student network.
Specifically, DSD consists of two stages: feature similarity distillation and spatial similarity distillation.

Accurate segmentation of biomedical images is crucial for various medical applications.
In this paper, we propose a novel multi-compound transformer (MCT) for accurate biomedical image segmentation.
The MCT combines the strengths of both transformers and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to improve segmentation performance.
We introduce a compound transformer module that integrates multiple transformer layers with CNN layers, allowing for better feature extraction and spatial context understanding.
Additionally, we propose a compound attention mechanism that adaptively combines the attention maps from different transformer layers to enhance the segmentation accuracy.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed MCT outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.

This paper investigates the problem of uncertainty estimation in active learning for image segmentation.
Active learning is a popular approach for reducing the annotation effort required in training deep learning models.
However, accurately estimating uncertainty is crucial for effective active learning.
The authors propose a novel method that combines a deep learning model with a Bayesian framework to estimate uncertainty in image segmentation tasks.
The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets and compared with existing uncertainty estimation techniques.
The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance in uncertainty estimation, leading to improved active learning performance for image segmentation.

In this paper, we propose a novel image segmentation framework called Co-Seg that aims to address the issue of label corruption in training data.
Label corruption can significantly degrade the performance of image segmentation models, leading to inaccurate and unreliable results.
Co-Seg leverages the idea of co-training, where two models are trained simultaneously on different subsets of the training data.
One model focuses on learning from clean labels, while the other model learns from corrupted labels.
The two models then collaborate to generate more accurate segmentation predictions.
We evaluate Co-Seg on several benchmark datasets and compare its performance against state-of-the-art segmentation methods.

This paper presents a performance evaluation of deep learning networks for semantic segmentation of traffic stereo-pair images.
The authors compare the performance of three popular deep learning architectures, namely U-Net, SegNet, and DeepLab, on a dataset of traffic stereo-pair images.
The evaluation is based on various metrics such as pixel accuracy, mean intersection over union (IoU), and F1 score.
The results show that DeepLab outperforms U-Net and SegNet in terms of all the evaluated metrics.
The authors also analyze the impact of different hyperparameters on the performance of the networks.
Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the performance of deep learning networks for semantic segmentation of traffic stereo-pair images and can guide future research in this area.

Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions.
Traditional approaches to image segmentation have relied on low-level features such as color, texture, and edges.
However, these methods often struggle to accurately segment complex scenes with multiple objects and occlusions.
In recent years, there has been a shift towards more advanced techniques that leverage high-level semantic information to improve segmentation performance.
This paper presents a comprehensive survey of the state-of-the-art techniques in both bottom-up and semantic image segmentation.
We discuss the evolution of image segmentation algorithms, from early pixel-based methods to more recent deep learning approaches.
