This paper presents a method for efficiently computing piecewise flat embeddings for data clustering and image segmentation.
The proposed method leverages the concept of piecewise flat embeddings, which represent data points as vertices in a graph and use edge weights to capture the similarity between points.
The authors introduce a novel algorithm that efficiently computes these embeddings by iteratively updating the edge weights based on the current clustering or segmentation.
The algorithm is designed to minimize the computational complexity while still producing accurate results.
The authors evaluate the proposed method on various datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving high-quality clustering and segmentation results.
The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.

PointRend is a novel approach to image segmentation that treats the task as a rendering problem.
Traditional segmentation methods typically assign a single label to each pixel, which can result in inaccurate boundaries and loss of fine-grained details.
In contrast, PointRend leverages a set of randomly sampled points within each object instance to generate high-resolution masks.
These points are then used to render the final segmentation mask, resulting in improved boundary quality and preservation of fine details.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that PointRend outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of both accuracy and visual quality.
Additionally, PointRend is computationally efficient and can be easily integrated into existing segmentation pipelines.

In contrast, PointRend leverages a set of randomly sampled points within each object instance to generate high-resolution masks.
These points are then used to render the final segmentation mask, resulting in improved boundary quality and preservation of fine details.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that PointRend outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of both accuracy and visual quality.
Additionally, PointRend is computationally efficient and can be easily integrated into existing segmentation pipelines.

In recent years, 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success in various computer vision tasks.
However, the large number of parameters and computational cost of 3D CNNs pose challenges for their deployment on resource-constrained devices.
In this paper, we propose a novel method called Channel-wise Automatic KErnel Shrinking (CAKES) to address this issue.
CAKES dynamically adjusts the kernel size of each channel in a 3D CNN based on its importance, thereby reducing the number of parameters and computational cost without sacrificing performance.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that CAKES achieves significant parameter reduction and computational cost reduction while maintaining competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
Our method provides a promising solution for efficient deployment of 3D CNNs on resource-constrained devices.

Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) is a challenging task in medical image analysis, particularly in the context of hip joint bone segmentation.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Intra- and Cross-modality Semantic Consistency (ICMSC) for UDA on hip joint bone segmentation.
Our method leverages the semantic consistency between intra-modality and cross-modality images to improve the segmentation performance.
Specifically, we introduce a dual-branch network architecture that consists of an intra-modality branch and a cross-modality branch.
The intra-modality branch is responsible for learning the segmentation task on the source domain, while the cross-modality branch learns to transfer the knowledge from the source domain to the target domain.
We also propose a semantic consistency loss that encourages the predicted segmentation maps from both branches to be consistent.

This paper proposes a novel method for screen content image segmentation using sparse decomposition and total variation minimization.
The method aims to accurately separate the foreground and background regions in screen content images, which are commonly encountered in various applications such as video surveillance and image editing.
The proposed method first decomposes the input image into a sparse representation using a dictionary learning algorithm.
Then, a total variation minimization algorithm is applied to refine the segmentation result by promoting piecewise smoothness in the image.
Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed method has the potential to be applied in real-world applications that require accurate and efficient screen content image segmentation.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, it is challenging due to the complexity and variability of medical images.
In this paper, we propose a novel spatial guided self-supervised clustering network (SGSCN) for medical image segmentation.
The proposed network leverages the spatial information of medical images to guide the clustering process, which improves the accuracy and robustness of the segmentation results.
We evaluate the performance of the SGSCN on a publicly available medical image dataset and compare it with state-of-the-art segmentation methods.
The experimental results demonstrate that the SGSCN achieves superior segmentation accuracy and outperforms existing methods in terms of both quantitative metrics and visual quality.

Hyperspectral unmixing is a challenging task in remote sensing, where the goal is to estimate the abundance fractions of different materials present in a mixed pixel.
Traditional unmixing methods often assume that the abundance fractions are spatially independent, which may not hold true in many real-world scenarios.
In this paper, we propose a collaborative sparse regression approach that takes into account the spatial correlation of the abundance fractions.
We model the spatial correlation using a graph-based representation and incorporate it into a sparse regression framework.
Experimental results on real hyperspectral datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method in improving the unmixing accuracy compared to traditional methods that do not consider spatial correlation.
Our approach has the potential to enhance the interpretation and analysis of hyperspectral imagery in various applications such as land cover classification and environmental monitoring.

This paper presents a study on the structure and morphology of epitaxially grown Fe3O4/NiO bilayers on MgO(001) substrates.
The bilayers were grown using molecular beam epitaxy and characterized using various techniques including X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and atomic force microscopy.
The results show that the Fe3O4 layer grows epitaxially on the MgO substrate with a cube-on-cube orientation relationship, while the NiO layer grows with a rotated cube-on-cube orientation.
The interface between the two layers is found to be sharp and coherent.
The morphology of the bilayers is found to be influenced by the growth conditions, with the Fe3O4 layer exhibiting a smooth surface and the NiO layer showing a rougher surface.
Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the structural and morphological properties of Fe3O4/NiO bilayers, which are important for their potential applications in spintronics and magnetoelectric devices.

Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in various clinical applications, such as disease diagnosis and treatment planning.
In recent years, deep learning models, especially convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have achieved remarkable success in medical image segmentation tasks.
However, CNNs have limitations in capturing long-range dependencies and suffer from high computational costs.
In this paper, we propose a novel medical image segmentation model called MISSFormer, which is based on the Transformer architecture.
We introduce a multi-scale self-attention mechanism to capture both local and global contextual information in medical images.
Additionally, we design a hybrid loss function that combines the Dice loss and the focal loss to address the class imbalance issue in medical image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel scale-space filtering framework called Hierarchical Image Peeling (HIP) that allows for flexible and efficient image processing.
HIP is based on the concept of peeling layers of an image, where each layer represents a different scale of the image.
The proposed framework provides a hierarchical representation of an image, allowing for the extraction of multi-scale features and the generation of scale-space pyramids.
The paper describes the theoretical foundations of HIP and presents several applications, including image denoising, edge detection, and texture analysis.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed framework compared to existing scale-space filtering methods.
Overall, HIP offers a flexible and powerful tool for image processing tasks that require multi-scale analysis.

The Third Gravitational Lensing Accuracy Testing (GREAT3) Challenge Handbook presents the results and analysis of the third iteration of the GREAT challenge, which aims to assess the accuracy of methods for measuring weak gravitational lensing.
Weak gravitational lensing is a phenomenon in which the light from distant galaxies is distorted by the gravitational pull of intervening matter, providing valuable information about the distribution of dark matter in the universe.
The challenge consists of simulating realistic images of galaxies and testing various methods for measuring their shapes and shears.
This handbook provides a detailed description of the challenge, including the simulation pipeline, the metrics used to evaluate the accuracy of the methods, and the results obtained by the participating teams.
The analysis of the results highlights the strengths and weaknesses of different methods and provides insights into the current state of the field.
The handbook also discusses the lessons learned from the challenge and provides recommendations for future improvements in the measurement of weak gravitational lensing.

Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a class label to each pixel in an image or video sequence.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for semantic segmentation of video sequences using Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM) networks.
We leverage the spatio-temporal information present in video sequences by extending the ConvLSTM architecture to incorporate both convolutional and recurrent layers.
Our model is trained on a large dataset of annotated video sequences and achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets.
We also demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in real-world scenarios by applying it to a video surveillance task.
Our results show that the proposed ConvLSTM-based approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.

The aim of the study is to investigate the feasibility and potential benefits of using eye-tracking data to improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation tasks.
The authors developed a software tool called Gaze2Segment, which combines eye-tracking data with traditional segmentation algorithms.
The tool was tested on a small group of participants who performed segmentation tasks on medical images while their eye movements were recorded.
The results showed that the integration of eye-tracking data improved the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process.
The findings suggest that eye-tracking technology has the potential to enhance medical image segmentation and could be a valuable tool for medical professionals in the future.

Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in various clinical applications, such as disease diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring.
Deep learning-based methods have shown promising results in medical image segmentation tasks.
However, these methods often require a large amount of annotated data for training, which is time-consuming and costly to obtain.
In this paper, we review recent advancements in deep network models for medical image segmentation with limited supervision.
We discuss various approaches, including semi-supervised learning, weakly supervised learning, and transfer learning, that aim to alleviate the need for fully annotated data.
We also analyze the strengths and limitations of these approaches and provide insights into future research directions.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach for skin cancer segmentation and classification using a combination of NABLA-N and Inception Recurrent Residual Convolutional Networks (IRRCNs).
Our method leverages the strengths of both networks to accurately segment and classify skin cancer images.
We evaluate our approach on a large dataset of skin cancer images and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.
The results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves superior performance in terms of segmentation and classification accuracy.
Our findings suggest that the combination of NABLA-N and IRRCNs can be a promising approach for skin cancer diagnosis and treatment.

Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image.
Existing methods typically rely on either image-level or semantic-level context to improve segmentation accuracy.
However, these methods often fail to capture the full range of contextual information available.
In this paper, we propose a novel framework called ISNet that integrates both image-level and semantic-level context for semantic segmentation.
ISNet consists of two modules: an image-level context module and a semantic-level context module.
The image-level context module captures global contextual information by aggregating features from multiple scales, while the semantic-level context module captures local contextual information by incorporating semantic information from neighboring pixels.

This paper proposes a novel approach for detecting missing method calls in software code by treating them as violations of the majority rule.
The majority rule states that if a method is called by the majority of instances of a class, it should also be called by the remaining instances.
The proposed approach involves analyzing the frequency of method calls in a codebase and identifying instances where a method is called by the majority of instances but not by the remaining instances.
The authors evaluate the effectiveness of their approach on a set of real-world codebases and compare it with existing techniques.
The results show that the majority rule approach outperforms existing techniques in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The findings of this study have implications for improving software quality by detecting and fixing missing method calls.

Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image.
While deep learning models have achieved impressive results in this task, they often struggle with capturing contextual information.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach that combines deep structured models with contextual information to improve semantic segmentation performance.
Our model leverages the power of deep learning to extract high-level features from images, while also incorporating contextual information through structured models.
We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.
Our findings highlight the importance of considering context in semantic segmentation tasks and provide insights into how deep structured models can be effectively utilized for this purpose.

This paper presents an enhancement neighborhood connected segmentation method for 2D-cellular images.
The proposed method utilizes a combination of region growing and edge detection techniques to accurately segment cellular structures in images.
The method starts by selecting seed points within the image and then grows regions around these points based on intensity and texture similarities.
Additionally, edge detection is used to refine the segmentation boundaries and improve the accuracy of the results.
Experimental results on a dataset of 2D-cellular images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately segmenting cellular structures.
The proposed method outperforms existing segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.

This paper proposes a method for accurately quantifying the uncertainty in neural network predictions of biomarkers, with the goal of improving the safety of deep learning models.
The authors argue that current deep learning models often lack the ability to provide reliable uncertainty estimates, which can lead to incorrect or misleading predictions in critical applications such as medical diagnosis.
The proposed method combines Bayesian neural networks with Monte Carlo dropout to estimate the predictive uncertainty of biomarker predictions.
The authors evaluate the method on a dataset of medical images and demonstrate that it provides more accurate uncertainty estimates compared to existing approaches.
They also show that incorporating these uncertainty estimates into decision-making processes can improve the safety and reliability of deep learning models in medical applications.
Overall, this paper contributes to the growing field of safe deep learning by addressing the important issue of uncertainty quantification in neural network predictions.

This academic paper investigates the crossover of a three-dimensional topological insulator, specifically Bi2Se3, to the two-dimensional limit.
The authors use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to study the electronic structure of Bi2Se3 thin films with varying thicknesses.
They find that as the thickness of the films decreases, the electronic structure undergoes a transition from a three-dimensional topological insulator to a two-dimensional system.
This transition is characterized by the disappearance of the Dirac cone feature in the electronic band structure.
The authors also observe a reduction in the bulk band gap and an increase in the surface state intensity as the film thickness decreases.
These findings provide valuable insights into the behavior of topological insulators in the two-dimensional limit and have implications for the design and fabrication of future electronic devices based on these materials.

This paper presents a novel approach for learning nonlinear Markov random fields (MRFs) using backpropagation.
MRFs are widely used in various fields, including computer vision and natural language processing, for modeling complex dependencies among variables.
However, existing methods for learning MRFs typically assume linearity, which limits their ability to capture nonlinear relationships.
In this work, we propose a new framework that combines the power of MRFs with the flexibility of neural networks.
We introduce a new class of nonlinear MRFs, called neural MRFs, which are learned using backpropagation.
Our approach allows for the modeling of complex nonlinear dependencies among variables, leading to improved performance in various tasks.

This paper examines the dynamics and biases of online attention in the context of aircraft crashes.
Using a large dataset of online news articles and social media posts, we analyze the patterns of attention towards aircraft crashes over a period of several years.
We find that attention towards aircraft crashes is highly dynamic, with peaks of attention following major incidents and quickly declining afterwards.
Furthermore, we identify several biases in the attention towards aircraft crashes, including a bias towards crashes involving commercial airlines and crashes with a high number of fatalities.
These biases are influenced by various factors, such as media coverage and public perception of risk.
Our findings contribute to a better understanding of the dynamics and biases of online attention, and have implications for the dissemination of information and the perception of risk in the context of aircraft crashes.

This paper presents a nonparametric clustering approach for image segmentation.
Traditional image segmentation methods often rely on assumptions about the underlying data distribution, which may not hold in practice.
In contrast, nonparametric clustering methods do not make any assumptions about the data distribution and can therefore be more flexible and robust.
The proposed method utilizes a density-based clustering algorithm to identify regions of similar pixel values in an image.
Experimental results on various image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately segmenting images.
The nonparametric clustering method shows promising potential for image segmentation tasks and can be a valuable tool in computer vision and image processing applications.

Instance segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that requires accurately localizing and segmenting each object instance in an image.
Traditional instance segmentation methods rely on large-scale annotated datasets, which are expensive and time-consuming to create.
In this paper, we propose a weakly supervised instance segmentation method using a hybrid network.
Our approach leverages both image-level class labels and bounding box annotations to train a network that can accurately segment object instances.
We introduce a novel hybrid loss function that combines both classification and segmentation losses to guide the network training.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance compared to fully supervised methods while requiring less annotation effort.

This paper presents a novel approach for uplink-downlink rate balancing in cooperating cellular networks.
The proposed method leverages the cooperation between neighboring base stations to optimize the allocation of resources and achieve a balanced rate between the uplink and downlink channels.
The authors formulate the problem as an optimization task and propose a distributed algorithm to solve it.
The algorithm takes into account the channel conditions, traffic demands, and resource availability to dynamically adjust the resource allocation.
Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving rate balancing and improving the overall network performance.
The findings of this study have implications for the design and operation of future cellular networks.

This paper presents a novel approach for visual saliency detection based on multiscale deep features.
The proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network to extract features at multiple scales, which are then combined to generate a saliency map.
The network is trained using a large dataset of images with ground truth saliency maps, allowing it to learn the discriminative features for saliency detection.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of accuracy and robustness.
The proposed method also achieves real-time performance, making it suitable for various applications such as image and video processing.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of visual saliency detection by leveraging the power of deep learning and multiscale analysis.

Quantum error correction is a crucial component in the development of reliable quantum computing systems.
However, designing and verifying quantum error correction codes can be challenging due to the complex nature of quantum systems.
In this paper, we propose a graphical approach for designing and verifying quantum error correction codes.
We introduce graphical structures that represent the logical and physical qubits, as well as the error correction operations.
These graphical structures provide a visual representation of the error correction code, making it easier to understand and analyze.
We also present a verification algorithm that uses these graphical structures to check the correctness of the error correction code.

Semantic image segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision, particularly in the context of traffic conditions analysis.
However, the performance of semantic image segmentation models heavily relies on the quality of ground truth annotations.
In this paper, we investigate the impact of ground truth annotation quality on the performance of semantic image segmentation models for traffic conditions analysis.
We propose a novel metric to quantify the quality of ground truth annotations and conduct experiments on a large dataset of traffic images.
Our results demonstrate that the quality of ground truth annotations significantly affects the performance of semantic image segmentation models, with higher quality annotations leading to improved segmentation accuracy.
We also analyze the factors that contribute to the quality of ground truth annotations and provide insights for improving the annotation process.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, obtaining accurate and reliable annotations for training deep learning models is challenging due to the limited availability of expert annotations.
In this paper, we propose a teacher-student framework for semi-supervised medical image segmentation that leverages both fully annotated and weakly annotated data.
The teacher network is trained on fully annotated data to provide pseudo-labels for weakly annotated data.
The student network is then trained on a combination of fully annotated and pseudo-labeled data.
Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves competitive performance compared to fully supervised methods while requiring fewer expert annotations.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, obtaining accurate pixel-level annotations for training deep learning models is time-consuming and expensive.
In this paper, we propose a weakly supervised approach for medical image segmentation that leverages extreme points as weak annotations.
We introduce a novel loss function that encourages the model to focus on the extreme points during training.
We evaluate our approach on two publicly available medical image datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art weakly supervised methods.
Our results demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive segmentation performance while significantly reducing the need for expensive pixel-level annotations.

Super-resolution is a technique used to enhance the resolution of low-resolution images.
In recent years, low-rank matrix decomposition has emerged as a powerful tool for super-resolution.
This paper investigates how low-rank matrix decomposition can aid in both internal and external learnings for super-resolution.
Internal learning refers to the process of learning the low-rank structure of the image itself, while external learning involves leveraging external data to improve super-resolution performance.
The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of various low-rank matrix decomposition methods and their impact on internal and external learnings for super-resolution.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of low-rank matrix decomposition in improving super-resolution performance and highlight the importance of selecting appropriate decomposition methods for different scenarios.

This paper presents a novel algorithm for the ISIC 2017 Skin Lesion Segmentation Challenge, which aims to accurately segment skin lesions from dermoscopic images.
The proposed algorithm combines k-means clustering and an ensemble of regressions to achieve accurate and robust segmentation results.
The k-means clustering is used to initialize the ensemble of regressions, which then iteratively refines the segmentation boundaries.
Experimental results on the ISIC 2017 dataset demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.
The algorithm also achieves competitive results in terms of computational efficiency.
Overall, the proposed algorithm provides a promising approach for skin lesion segmentation in clinical practice.

Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is an important problem in machine learning, as it helps to identify instances that do not belong to the training distribution.
Existing methods for OOD detection often rely on task-specific assumptions or require access to labeled OOD data.
In this paper, we propose a task-agnostic approach for OOD detection using kernel density estimation (KDE).
Our method leverages the inherent structure of the training data to estimate the density of the in-distribution instances and uses this estimate to detect OOD instances.
We evaluate our method on various benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art OOD detection methods.
The results show that our approach achieves competitive performance without relying on task-specific assumptions or labeled OOD data.

This paper presents a novel approach to message passing inference in deep learning models.
The authors propose a method called "Deeply Learning the Messages" (DLM) that aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of message passing algorithms.
The DLM method leverages the power of deep learning techniques to learn the messages exchanged between nodes in a graph-based model.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of DLM on various benchmark datasets and compare it with existing message passing algorithms.
The results show that DLM outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
The paper concludes by discussing the potential applications and future directions of DLM in the field of deep learning and graph-based models.

This paper proposes a novel approach for image segmentation using a combination of Markov Random Fields (MRF) and U-Net architectures.
The proposed method, called MRF-UNet Product of Experts, leverages the strengths of both MRF and U-Net models to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation tasks.
The MRF component captures the spatial dependencies between pixels, while the U-Net component extracts high-level features from the input image.
The Product of Experts framework combines the predictions from both models to generate the final segmentation result.
Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The MRF-UNet Product of Experts presents a promising direction for further advancements in image segmentation research.

Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into different regions or objects.
In recent years, deep learning techniques have shown promising results in various computer vision tasks, including image segmentation.
This paper presents SegNet, a deep convolutional encoder-decoder architecture specifically designed for image segmentation.
The proposed architecture consists of an encoder network that extracts high-level features from the input image and a decoder network that reconstructs the segmented image.
The encoder network utilizes a series of convolutional and pooling layers to progressively downsample the input image, while the decoder network uses upsampling and deconvolutional layers to recover the spatial resolution of the segmented image.
Additionally, skip connections are introduced to preserve fine-grained details during the upsampling process.

Medical image segmentation is a critical task in various clinical applications, but it is often challenging due to the inherent uncertainty in the segmentation process.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach for uncertainty quantification in medical image segmentation using normalizing flows.
Normalizing flows are a flexible class of generative models that can capture complex distributions.
We adapt normalizing flows to the task of medical image segmentation by training them to model the posterior distribution of the segmentation given the input image.
We then use the trained normalizing flows to estimate the uncertainty in the segmentation by sampling from the posterior distribution.
We evaluate our approach on a dataset of brain MRI scans and compare it to existing uncertainty quantification methods.

K-Net: Towards Unified Image Segmentation is an academic paper that proposes a novel approach for unified image segmentation.
The paper introduces a new deep learning architecture called K-Net, which combines the strengths of both convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs).
The K-Net architecture consists of a CNN module for feature extraction and an RNN module for capturing spatial dependencies.
The paper also presents a new loss function called the K-loss, which incorporates both pixel-level and region-level information.
Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed K-Net outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The paper concludes by discussing the potential applications and future directions of the K-Net framework in the field of image segmentation.

Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
In this paper, we propose a novel mixed-supervised dual-network framework for medical image segmentation.
The framework combines the strengths of both supervised and unsupervised learning approaches to improve segmentation accuracy.
The supervised network is trained using labeled data, while the unsupervised network leverages unlabeled data to learn the underlying structure of the images.
The two networks are then combined to generate the final segmentation results.
Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate that our proposed framework outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness.

This paper proposes a rate optimal multiple testing procedure for high-dimensional regression problems.
The procedure is designed to control the false discovery rate (FDR) while maximizing the power of the tests.
The authors derive the optimal rate of convergence for the FDR and show that their procedure achieves this rate.
They also provide theoretical guarantees for the power of the tests.
The proposed procedure is compared to existing methods through simulations and real data analysis, demonstrating its superior performance in terms of both FDR control and power.
Overall, this paper presents a novel and effective multiple testing procedure for high-dimensional regression problems.

In recent years, there has been a growing trend in the field of deep learning to develop increasingly complex and deep neural network architectures.
However, this paper argues that simpler architectures can often outperform their deeper and more complex counterparts.
The authors present a series of experiments comparing the performance of simple and complex architectures on various tasks, including image classification and natural language processing.
The results consistently show that the simpler architectures achieve comparable or even better performance than the more complex ones.
The authors also discuss the potential reasons behind this phenomenon, such as the increased risk of overfitting in deeper architectures.
Overall, this paper highlights the importance of considering simplicity in neural network design and challenges the prevailing notion that deeper and more complex architectures always lead to better performance.

The U-Net architecture has been widely used in various medical image segmentation tasks due to its effectiveness in capturing both local and global contextual information.
However, the traditional skip connections in U-Net may not fully exploit the channel-wise relationships between feature maps.
In this paper, we propose UCTransNet, a novel U-Net variant that incorporates the Transformer module to enhance the skip connections from a channel-wise perspective.
Specifically, we introduce a channel-wise attention mechanism to capture long-range dependencies and enhance feature representation.
Experimental results on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate that UCTransNet achieves superior performance compared to the original U-Net and other state-of-the-art methods.
Our findings suggest that rethinking skip connections in U-Net from a channel-wise perspective with Transformer can significantly improve the performance of medical image segmentation tasks.

We formulate the problem as an optimization task and propose an efficient algorithm to solve it.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
Furthermore, our method is computationally efficient, making it suitable for real-time applications.

Semantic segmentation of urban scene images is a challenging task due to the presence of very fine details and complex structures.
In this paper, we propose a novel approach that combines the strengths of transformers and convolutions to improve the accuracy of semantic segmentation.
Our method, called Bilateral Awareness Network (BANet), leverages the self-attention mechanism of transformers to capture long-range dependencies and the spatial information captured by convolutions to preserve local details.
We introduce a bilateral attention module that enables the network to attend to both global and local contexts simultaneously.
We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that BANet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
Our results show that the combination of transformers and convolutions can effectively address the challenges of semantic segmentation in very fine resolution urban scene images.

This paper presents a novel approach for surface segmentation in irregularly sampled space using convex priors.
The proposed method aims to find the optimal surface segmentation by minimizing an energy function that incorporates both data fidelity and prior information.
The irregularly sampled space is represented by a graph structure, and the surface segmentation problem is formulated as a graph cut problem.
The convex priors are used to regularize the segmentation and enforce smoothness.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method compared to existing approaches.
The proposed method has potential applications in various fields such as medical imaging, computer vision, and graphics.

This paper presents a novel approach for polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image semantic segmentation using a combination of 3D discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and Markov random field (MRF) techniques.
The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional SAR image segmentation methods by incorporating both spatial and spectral information.
The 3D DWT is used to decompose the polarimetric SAR image into different frequency subbands, which are then used to extract relevant features for segmentation.
The MRF model is employed to capture the spatial dependencies between neighboring pixels and enforce smoothness in the segmentation results.
Experimental results on real-world polarimetric SAR images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately segmenting different land cover classes.
The proposed approach offers a promising solution for polarimetric SAR image segmentation, with potential applications in various fields such as agriculture, urban planning, and environmental monitoring.

This paper presents a tunable coupled-mode dispersion compensation technique and its application to on-chip resonant four-wave mixing.
The proposed technique utilizes a pair of waveguides with different dispersion characteristics to compensate for the dispersion mismatch in the four-wave mixing process.
The dispersion compensation is achieved by adjusting the coupling strength between the two waveguides, allowing for precise control of the dispersion compensation.
The effectiveness of the technique is demonstrated through numerical simulations and experimental measurements.
The results show that the proposed technique can effectively compensate for the dispersion mismatch and enhance the efficiency of the four-wave mixing process.
This tunable coupled-mode dispersion compensation technique has potential applications in on-chip optical signal processing and communication systems.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning.
However, obtaining accurate annotations for training deep learning models is often challenging due to the limited availability of expert annotations.
In this paper, we propose a contrastive learning framework for medical image segmentation that leverages both global and local features.
Specifically, we introduce a global feature encoder and a local feature encoder to extract discriminative features from medical images.
These features are then used to train a segmentation network using a contrastive loss function.
We evaluate our approach on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.

This paper presents a novel 3D deep coarse-to-fine framework for volumetric medical image segmentation.
The proposed framework consists of two stages: a coarse segmentation stage and a fine segmentation stage.
In the coarse segmentation stage, a 3D fully convolutional network is used to generate an initial segmentation map.
This map is then refined in the fine segmentation stage using a 3D U-Net network.
The framework is trained using a combination of supervised and unsupervised learning, with the unsupervised learning component being used to generate adversarial examples.
The effectiveness of the proposed framework is evaluated on a dataset of volumetric medical images, and the results show that it outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.

Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method in detecting unhealthy leaves in different environmental conditions.
The proposed method has potential applications in agriculture and plant disease diagnosis, enabling early detection and prevention of leaf diseases.

In this paper, we define blow-ups in generalized complex geometry and study their properties.
We show that blow-ups preserve the generalized complex structure and provide explicit formulas for the blow-up map and the exceptional divisor.
We also investigate the behavior of blow-ups under various operations, such as taking products and quotients.

This paper proposes a novel self-ensembling contrastive learning approach for semi-supervised medical image segmentation.
The proposed method leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the segmentation performance.
The self-ensembling mechanism is used to generate pseudo-labels for the unlabeled data, which are then used to train the segmentation model.
The contrastive learning objective is employed to encourage the model to learn meaningful representations of the medical images.
Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art semi-supervised segmentation methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.
The proposed method also achieves competitive performance compared to fully supervised methods, indicating its potential for practical applications in medical image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting roots in soil using the U-Net architecture.
The U-Net architecture is a convolutional neural network that has been widely used for image segmentation tasks.
In this study, we adapt the U-Net architecture to segment roots in soil images.
We propose a modified U-Net architecture that incorporates skip connections and data augmentation techniques to improve the accuracy of root segmentation.
We evaluate our approach on a dataset of soil images with ground truth annotations for root segmentation.
Our results show that the proposed U-Net architecture achieves high accuracy in segmenting roots in soil images, outperforming existing methods.

The Social Force Model (SFM) is a widely used pedestrian simulation model that aims to capture the collective behavior of individuals during evacuation scenarios.
In this paper, we investigate the stationarity of the SFM by analyzing the movement patterns of pedestrians in different evacuation scenarios.
Our results show that the SFM is not stationary, as the movement patterns of pedestrians change over time.
Specifically, we observe that pedestrians tend to move faster and take shorter paths as the evacuation progresses.
These findings have important implications for the design and optimization of evacuation strategies, as they suggest that the behavior of pedestrians cannot be accurately predicted based on static models.
Therefore, future research should focus on developing dynamic models that can capture the evolving nature of pedestrian movement during evacuations.

Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image.
While deep learning models have achieved impressive results in this field, there is still a lack of understanding of how these models make predictions and what factors contribute to their performance.
In this paper, we propose a diagnostic framework for semantic segmentation models that aims to provide insights into their decision-making process.
We introduce several diagnostic tasks, including object localization, boundary detection, and occlusion reasoning, and evaluate their effectiveness on a state-of-the-art semantic segmentation model.
Our results show that these diagnostic tasks can help identify the strengths and weaknesses of the model, and provide valuable insights for improving its performance.
We believe that our diagnostic framework can contribute to the development of more interpretable and robust semantic segmentation models.

This paper presents a novel approach for designing efficient and invariant convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for dense prediction tasks.
The proposed method leverages the concept of group equivariant CNNs to achieve translation invariance while reducing computational complexity.
The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on various dense prediction tasks, including semantic segmentation and depth estimation.
Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance while significantly reducing the computational cost compared to traditional CNN architectures.
The authors also provide insights into the design choices and hyperparameters that contribute to the efficiency and invariance of the proposed CNNs.
Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of deep learning for dense prediction tasks.

The proposed method has the potential to be applied in various applications, such as medical image analysis and object recognition.

This paper presents an uncertainty-based human-in-the-loop system for industrial tool wear analysis.
The system utilizes machine learning algorithms to predict tool wear based on sensor data collected from the manufacturing process.
However, due to the inherent uncertainty in the prediction models, human intervention is required to validate and refine the predictions.
The system incorporates a user interface that allows operators to review and provide feedback on the predicted tool wear levels.
This feedback is then used to update the prediction models and improve their accuracy.
The effectiveness of the system is demonstrated through experiments conducted on real-world manufacturing data.

This paper studies fair division and redistricting problems, which include optimally dividing a heterogeneous resource among individuals (with different preferences over the items) and fairly drawing borders of districts to accommodate a given population in a way that everyone has nearly equal political power.
Both problems are fundamental in many real-world applications, yet they pose significant challenges to each other in terms of the solutions.
We first show that the classic optimization approach, which optimally solves the fair division problem, can lead to extremely unfair district borders in the redistricting problem.
For instance, it may produce districts in which most voters are minorities in their own districts.
Then we propose a new paradigm to study these problems, by viewing them as a heterogeneous matching problem, and design efficient algorithms that optimize fairness in both problems simultaneously.
In particular, our algorithms ensure that after division, each district is composed of individuals who have nearly equal preference for the items (or political power).

Abstract: CIDI-Lung-Seg: A Single-Click Annotation Tool for Automatic Delineation of Lungs from CT Scans

Automatic segmentation of lungs in CT scans is a fundamental step towards computer-aided detection, diagnosis, and treatment of pulmonary diseases.
However, it remains a challenging task, mainly due to the lungs' intricate structures and their proximity to the heart and other organs.
In this paper, we present a single-click annotation tool, called CIDI-Lung-Seg, for efficient and effective delineation of lungs in CT scans.
Our approach is based on a deep learning model that utilizes a conditional instance-discrimination inference (CIDI) framework to improve the segmentation performance.
We evaluated our method on 320 CT scans from the public LUNA16 dataset, and the results showed that CIDI-Lung-Seg achieved a mean dice similarity coefficient of 0.9378, outperforming the state-of-the-art.


Our tool is designed to be user-friendly and can be easily operated by radiologists and clinicians without extensive knowledge of computer vision or deep learning.

Recent works on omnidirectional image segmentation have shown the efficacy of incorporating contextual information across different ranges for accurate pixel-level labeling.
However, existing methods mainly rely on either a limited number of fixed ranges or a single modulated range, which may not adequately capture the rich variations in the omni-range context.
In this paper, we present an Omni-Range Context module that can flexibly capture the omni-range context from a set of input features.
Specifically, given a set of input features, our module can be flexibly configured to use a sub-set of features with specific ranges of interest, enabling the model to focus on the most relevant context.
We show that the proposed module can be easily integrated into existing segmentation frameworks to enhance their performance.
When evaluated on four standard benchmarks for omnidirectional segmentation, our method achieves state-of-the-art performance.

Unsupervised learning allows computational finding of intrinsic patterns in data without explicit alignment to known structures.
We present an unsupervised learning framework for the discovery of communities in transactional data, such as found in electronic medical records, collaborative filtering systems, and social networks.
Our framework addresses the problem of detecting communities in a sparse transactional data matrix where each row and column corresponds to an entity (e.g., a patient, user, or peer) and each sparse element indicates a transaction (e.g., a diagnosis, a movie rating, or a communication).
The problem is inherently unsupervised because there is no known ground truth for communities; computational approaches must mine for communities without any alignment to known structures.
Compared to previous work, we propose a new precise definition for the quality of a community detection mapping in terms of popular visualization techniques.
This allows a direct evaluation of the quality of a detected mapping without relying on external ground truth.

We use high-speed imaging and numerical modelling to investigate water droplet penetration inside narrow, open-ended pores, characterised by a diameter of ∼1 mm.
In particular, we analyse the dependence of capillary influx and splashing on droplet size and on the initial contact angle.
We find that the closed pore generates a stronger capillary force, which results in a more effective attraction of the liquid.
Interestingly, we observe that, before completing the penetration, the liquid protrudes from the pore, wets the external surface, and finally detaches.
The total ingress time is significantly longer than the cavity emptying time, thus revealing that the liquid evacuation is controlled by capillary inertia.
We quantify the liquid protrusion length as a function of the contact angle and find that it corresponds to the meniscus pinning regime.

Towards active learning of image segmentation, we address the setting where, given a limited budget of queries, a learner has to select the most informative pixels to query the underlying ground truth.
In this setting, uncertainty is commonly exploited as a measure of informativeness.
However, standard uncertainty estimates, e.g., entropy, are not optimal as they do not account for the cost of acquiring ground truth.
In this paper, we propose a new uncertainty measure that we refer to as cost-sensitive uncertainty.
Our proposed measure yields a higher score for pixels that are uncertain under the current labeling, but more expensive to query; and vice-versa.
We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach on three real-world image segmentation datasets, where we show that our approach yields superior segmentation performance compared to standard uncertainty measures.

In this paper, we propose a method for the segmentation of infrared images of cross-country scenes.
The proposed method consists of three steps: preprocessing, region segmentation, and region labeling.
In the preprocessing step, anisotropic diffusion is used for noise reduction and flat field correction.
In the region segmentation step, we use a novel region growing technique in combination with a watershed algorithm to obtain initial regions.
Finally, in the region labeling step, these initial regions are merged using color and texture information to produce the final segmentation.
The proposed method has been evaluated using infrared images from different datasets, and the results show that it is effective in segmenting cross-country scenes.

Recent works in crowd-based object segmentation have mostly relied on either a) labeling a new training dataset, b) using pre-trained models without adapting to the new dataset, or c) using complex models tuned on different datasets.
In this work, we tackle the problem of training a crowd-based object segmentation model from scratch, i.e., without any available pre-trained models or labeled training data.
To this end, we follow a data-centric approach leveraging click-stream data collected via an online annotation tool.
We propose a clickstream analysis framework that compensates for the limitations of the crowd by dynamically adapting the amount of labeling effort spent on each pixel.
This is done in a data-driven fashion using a deep neural network that predicts the quality of the crowd's annotations without ground truth.
We show that our approach, which is trained entirely on click-stream data, is able to achieve better performance than models trained on ground truth data alone.

Recent progress in semantic segmentation largely concentrates on image-based approaches.
However, for cities with tall buildings and dense streets, the perspective of aerial images shows a significant deviation from the ground images, making it challenging to directly apply the image-based methods.
To this end, we propose a novel framework, named PointFlow, for aerial image segmentation.
It models the semantics propagation in a point-based manner, allowing us to handle the large-scale perspective variation and thus ease the segmentations on aerial images.
In particular, given a sparse set of points, our framework flows the semantics from source points to target points in an iterative manner.
At each iteration, we estimate a sparse semantic label field from the current point predictions, and then update the point predictions by propagating the estimated label field.

We present a stable and efficient pseudospectral scheme for the approximation of partial differential equations (PDEs) using Barycentric Gegenbauer quadratures.
These are high-order accurate, total-variation-diminishing (TVD), and entropy-stable for a wide range of linear and nonlinear PDEs in convection dominated regimes.
We demonstrate that the Barycentric Gegenbauer quadratures achieve their optimal order of accuracy in the absence of dispersion effects, such as stiffness and nonlinearity.
We introduce suitable techniques to handle nonlinearity and dispersion in a stable manner.
Our approach is based on a modulation technique that introduces extra variables to decouple the nonlinear and dispersive effects from the TVD property.
We demonstrate the efficacy of the method through numerical examples.

Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision with a wide range of applications.
However, training such models requires large amounts of accurately annotated data, which is difficult and expensive to obtain.
In this paper, we tackle the problem of limited data and annotations in semantic segmentation by proposing a new approach that combines the use of image-based and instance-based training data.
We show that by using a multi-task learning framework, we can effectively leverage both types of data to improve the performance of semantic segmentation models.
Furthermore, we present a new instance-based loss function that utilizes an ensemble of instance-based models to improve the robustness of our approach.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on the Cityscapes and CamVid datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance on both datasets with a significant reduction in the amount of training data required.

Recent studies have demonstrated the potential of deep learning for medical image analysis.
However, these methods usually require a large amount of manually annotated training data, which is difficult to obtain for medical images.
In this paper, we present a semi-supervised learning method for left atrium segmentation in cardiac MR images.
Our method leverages a large amount of unlabeled data and a small amount of manually annotated data to train a deep neural network.
To deal with the class imbalance and the lack of annotated data, we use a mutual consistency training strategy, which ensures that the predictions from the model with semi-supervised labels are similar to the fully supervised labels.
Our method achieves a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.8033 and a Hausdorff distance of 7.35 mm on a public dataset, which outperforms the state-of-the-art fully-supervised method by a large margin.

To deal with the class imbalance and the lack of annotated data, we use a mutual consistency training strategy, which ensures that the predictions from the model with semi-supervised labels are similar to the fully supervised labels.
Our method achieves a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.8033 and a Hausdorff distance of 7.35 mm on a public dataset, which outperforms the state-of-the-art fully-supervised method by a large margin.

We perform qubit state tomography in a superconducting circuit by using weak measurements.
By periodically weakly measuring the qubit, we obtain statistical moments of the readout signals, which are used to estimate the state of the qubit.
We demonstrate a tomographic scheme in which weak measurements followed by a projective measurement are performed, and a tomogram of the qubit is obtained.
We apply the proposed method to a superconducting flux qubit, and perform tomographic reconstruction of the qubit state with high fidelity.
The presented scheme is useful for obtaining the quantum state of a superconducting qubit, which is necessary for the analysis of quantum information processing tasks and for verifying the correctness of quantum algorithms.

Many neurons exhibit morphological plasticity, altering the shape and connectivity of their dendritic spines in response to physiological cues.
Here, we show that chronic activation of endogenous signaling pathways downstream of bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) receptors leads to the rapid loss of dendritic spines in cortical neurons in culture and dendritic simplification in neurons in mouse brain slices.
Signaling was specific to BMP ligands because Activin did not produce these effects and because the BMP pathway inhibitors, Dorsomorphin and DMH1, blocked the signaling.
Interestingly, the effects of BMP signaling in culture were blocked by inhibitors of histone deacetylase (HDAC) activity, including sodium butyrate and trichostatin A, but not by the kinase inhibitors, suggesting a link between BMP signaling and HDAC activity.
Moreover, BMP ligands induced recruitment of HDAC2 and 3 to the nucleus as shown by immunofluorescence and pull-down assays.
Inhibiting HDAC activity blocked the ability of BMP ligands to simplify dendritic structures, to cause a decrease in synaptic puncta number, and to cause an increase in the percentage of neurons with a single punctum.

We present a conditional random field (CRF) model and a deep learning-based feature learning approach for hyperspectral image (HSI) segmentation.
The CRF model is a traditional statistical model used for image segmentation tasks, where pixel-level labels are predicted based on the features of the pixels and the spatial dependencies between the pixels.
The deep learning-based feature learning approach is used to learn a low-dimensional feature representation of the hyperspectral data, which is then used as input to the CRF model.
The proposed approach was evaluated on the Indian Pines hyperspectral dataset, and achieved a segmentation accuracy of 94.4%.


The CRF model uses a probabilistic approach to capture the spatial dependencies between pixels, and is trained using a maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) approach.
The deep learning-based feature learning approach is based on a convolutional neural network (CNN), which is trained using a supervised learning approach.

We present a novel gated conditional random field (CRF) loss for weakly supervised semantic image segmentation, which combines the benefits of supervised and unsupervised training while mitigating their respective shortcomings.
Whereas supervised segmentation typically provides precise but sparse training labels, unsupervised methods exhibit smooth but inconsistent predictions.
By conditioning the CRF on a mask obtained from a segmentation confidence map, we provide stronger guidance to the model where it is more uncertain, producing more consistent and accurate segmentations.
Furthermore, our method is able to explicitly leverage additional supervision, despite its noise, to further improve performance.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on the PASCAL VOC 2012 semantic image segmentation benchmark, obtaining state-of-the-art performance.
Code is available at https://github.com/NVlabs/paced-crf.

Recent advances in deep learning have achieved remarkable performance in semantic image segmentation.
However, training deep segmentation models requires a large amount of labeled images, which are difficult to obtain.
Data augmentation is a useful technique to generate more training samples by applying different transformations to the original images.
Most data augmentation methods focus on image-level augmentation, which applies the same transformation to all objects in an image.
This is a limitation for semantic image segmentation, as it cannot increase the diversity of objects in an image.
In this paper, we introduce a new data augmentation method called ObjectAug, which performs object-level data augmentation for semantic image segmentation.

In this paper, we propose a new method for segmenting meaningful objects in SAR images.
The proposed method is based on a multi-scale non-local active contour model.
The non-local operation is implemented by a Gaussian weighted distance map, which can describe the long-range spatial dependence with a single parameter.
In the multi-scale framework, a series of Gaussian weighted distance maps are employed as the internal energy and the external energy of the active contour model, respectively.
By minimizing the energy function, a series of active contours are generated in different scales.
Finally, the segmentation result is obtained by combining the information from the multi-scale active contours.

Academic biographies on Wikipedia undergo preferential editing, with notable professors more likely to have biographies than less notable ones, and with those biographies more likely to be of higher quality, according to a study published in the Journal of Documentation.
These findings run counter to the notion of Wikipedia as a democratic encyclopedia and raise questions about the information found in the world's most popular reference work.


The research team, from the University of Pittsburgh and Wikitonia, analyzed 7,634 academic biographies from the English-language Wikipedia on February 7, 2017, linking each subject to the highest-ranked institution with which they were associated and categorizing each subject by discipline.
They then determined each subject's "notability" by whether or not they had their own academic biography on Wikipedia and calculated a "quality" score for each subject based on the average number of words in their biography and the average number of references linked to that biography.


The researchers found that subjects associated with institutions ranked among the top 100 universities in the world were more likely to have a Wikipedia biography than those affiliated with institutions that rank outside the top 1000.
A similar trend was observed in subjects who had earned a PhD or other doctoral degree and those who had not.

We present a fully convolutional two-stream fusion network (TCN) for real-time interactive image segmentation.
The TCN is designed to leverage the benefits of both feed-forward and recurrent neural networks while avoiding their limitations.
Our network is composed of two streams: a feed-forward convolutional neural network (CNN) stream and a recurrent convolutional neural network (RCNN) stream.
The CNN stream provides initial segmentation results, which are refined by the RCNN stream in a coarse-to-fine fashion.
The two streams are combined at the feature level using a concatenation layer, which allows the network to leverage the strengths of both streams and improve the segmentation performance.
We evaluate the TCN on the interactive image segmentation benchmark ISBI 2017 and achieve competitive results with state-of-the-art methods.

We show how to construct optimal image segmentations using particle methods.
Our approach is based on minimization of a functional that trades off between segmenting pixels correctly and minimizing the gradient of the resulting segmentation.
This functional is a Sobolev gradient, that is, the sum of the gradients of all pixels, weighted by a per-pixel smoothness term.
We propose to approximate this Sobolev gradient by a particle system, and show that, under an approximation scheme, the global minimizer of the particle system corresponds to the optimal segmentation.
Furthermore, we show how to efficiently solve the particle system using a block-coordinate descent algorithm.
We evaluate our method on the benchmark datasets of the 2016 CAMELYON challenge, and show that it compares favorably to state-of-the-art segmentation methods, while being simpler, faster, and requiring less parameter tuning.

Fast panoptic segmentation is a fundamental task for many computer vision applications.
Existing methods usually concatenate prediction branches for different categories, yielding a huge increase in model size and computation.
In this work, we propose a lightweight and efficient approach for fast panoptic segmentation, termed AinnoSeg.
Specifically, we introduce a weight-shared U-Net whose output channels are dynamically determined by the intermediate features.
A key insight is that the hierarchical features in the U-Net can be naturally aligned with the panoptic segmentation hierarchy (i.e., instance-level, stuff-level, and thing-level), and therefore the U-Net can be adapted to different parts of the hierarchy with different output channels.
This adaptability allows us to selectively enlarge the capacity for hard instances (e.g., small stuff) while keeping a small model size for easy instances (e.g., large things).

Recent progress in artificial intelligence has enabled the automation of various agriculture-related tasks, such as crop and weed detection.
However, creating a large and diverse dataset for training deep learning models can be a time-consuming and laborious process, which can hinder the development of accurate and robust models.
In this paper, we present a data generation framework that automatically creates a large and diverse dataset for training deep learning models to detect crops and weeds.
Our framework utilizes a combination of image segmentation, edge detection, and geometric projection algorithms to generate synthetic training data that closely resembles real-world images.
Furthermore, our framework can rapidly create datasets of various sizes and crop types, making it suitable for a wide range of applications.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through extensive experiments, showing that our framework can significantly improve the accuracy and robustness of deep learning models for crop and weed detection.

We present a technique for improving the performance of random walker image segmentation and registration algorithms.
Our method involves precomputing and storing intermediate results for a fixed set of input parameters.
By storing these precomputed results, we are able to significantly reduce the time required to compute the final result for any given input image.
We find that our method is particularly useful for segmentation and registration problems that involve large images or a large number of images.
Our method is adaptable in the sense that it can be used with any random walker algorithm that utilizes a graphical model representation.
We present experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of our method on a number of different images.

We consider the problem of predicting a structured output variable y, which depends on an input x through a possibly nonlinear, parametric mapping function f(x, θ).
In many applications, such as chemoinformatics and bioinformatics, one has a very large number of samples, and an abundance of features, but only a small number of training examples for each class of interest.
For example, a dataset of 100,000 molecules may have activity data for 1000 molecules with a particular biological response, but only 10 examples for a rarer phenotype.
We propose a boosting approach which is applicable in such cases.
We handle the parametric nature of the mapping by using a Gaussian process (GP) surrogate model.
This allows us to construct a distribution over the space of possible functions, given a particular input.

Automatic image segmentation is a classic problem in image processing, with many applications in areas such as medical imaging, remote sensing, and biological imaging.
In this paper, we present an automatic image segmentation method based on dynamic region merging.
Our method combines the advantages of both region-based and edge-based segmentation methods, while avoiding the drawbacks of each.
The proposed method is efficient, automatic, and does not require any user interaction.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on a variety of images, including those with complex shapes and textures.
We also compare our method to other state-of-the-art segmentation methods, and show that it performs favorably in terms of segmentation quality and efficiency.

Recent works have shown that the attention mechanism can be applied to convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to improve performance on image recognition tasks.
We observe that these works mostly focus on applying attention mechanism within the last few layers of CNNs, where the spatial dimensions of the feature maps are already very small, and the attention mechanism can effectively "attend" to the most important features.
However, in the early layers of CNNs where the feature maps are still very large, the attention mechanism is often not effective, as there are simply too many positions for the attention to focus on.
In this work, we propose a simple and effective approach to overcome this limitation.
We introduce a new type of layer that we call the "AttentionBoost" layer, which works by combining the feature maps from the previous layer with the attention maps generated by a single-layer CNN.
This allows the attention mechanism to effectively attend to the most important features in the early layers of the network, even when the feature maps are very large.

Encoder Fusion Network with Co-Attention Embedding (EFN-CAE) is a new deep learning architecture designed for the task of referring image segmentation.
EFN-CAE leverages a fusion of high-level and low-level features learned by two encoders to highlight the referred objects in the image.
Furthermore, a co-attention mechanism is introduced to model the relationship between the referring expression and the image, generating spatial attention weights to focus on the relevant areas.
The referred regions are obtained by fusing global and local features of the image using the attention weights.
In addition, we introduce a novel referredness measure to weigh the importance of each referred region.
This measure is learned jointly with the segmentation network.

In this paper, we propose a novel image segmentation enhancement technique based on active contour and topological alignments.
Our method combines the advantages of both approaches to achieve accurate and robust segmentation results.
We begin by initializing an active contour model using a set of seed points and then iteratively refine the segmentation by considering topological alignments between the contour and the image.
The topological alignments are computed using a novel graph-based approach that considers the local structure of the image.
The proposed method is evaluated on a variety of images and compared to state-of-the-art image segmentation techniques.
The results show that the proposed method achieves improved segmentation accuracy and robustness, especially in challenging images with complex structures and textures.

We propose a Performance analysis of an improved MUSIC Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) estimator, which utilizes the MUSIC algorithm for DoA estimation of a uniform linear array (ULA).
In our improved algorithm, we employ the eigenvalue decomposition (EVD) and the Toeplitz structure of the correlation matrix to reduce the computational complexity, as well as a new technique to select the parameter in the MUSIC algorithm, which is based on the use of the Cauchy prior.
By using these improvements, we enhance the performance of the MUSIC DoA estimator.
In this paper, we analyze the performance of our improved algorithm by calculating the root mean square error (RMSE) and the mean absolute error (MAE) between the DoAs estimated by the improved algorithm and the true angles.
The performance analysis is carried out by varying the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and the number of sources.
The results show that our improved algorithm provides a significant performance improvement in comparison to the conventional MUSIC algorithm, especially for low SNR values and a small number of sources.

We present an approach to spontaneous noise spectroscopy of atomic vapor that aims to suppress the dominant source of noise in the scheme, namely, the noise induced by the vacuum environment of the atomic sample.
The approach is based on a combination of common mode rejection and a optimized cavity configuration.
We describe the noise reduction mechanisms and discuss the coherence properties of the scheme.
The presented approach can be implemented in a variety of platforms, including optically trapped atoms and cells.

We propose a novel configuration that enables efficient common mode rejection of the vacuum noise, which is the dominant noise source in the scheme.

We describe the noise reduction mechanisms and discuss the coherence properties of the scheme.
The presented approach can be implemented in a variety of platforms, including optically trapped atoms and cells.

We propose a novel configuration that enables efficient common mode rejection of the vacuum noise, which is the dominant noise source in the scheme.

We present results of gamma-ray spectroscopy measurements of positron annihilation in glycerol performed at beam line 16C1 of the Institute for Basic Science, UNIST.
Gamma-ray emission from the title compound was detected in the energy range up to 3100 MeV.
The analysis of the obtained spectra allowed us to determine the lifetime and positron energy spectrum of the positronium (Ps) state in glycerol.
No evidence of the quasi-free Ps state was found.
We compare the results with recent ab initio calculations of the positron affinity and the positron state properties in glycerol.
Good agreement between the experimental results and theoretical predictions was obtained.

We propose a fast fully octave convolutional neural network (FCN) for document image segmentation.
Our network dynamically scales the convolutional kernels by a factor of two between every two layers, which we refer to as octave convolution.
This approach reduces the parameters by a factor of two per layer and shrinks the computational cost, yet it does not reduce the receptive field of the network.
We evaluate our method on the publicly available ICDAR 2015 document image segmentation benchmark.
Our network achieves a higher accuracy with a significantly reduced computational cost compared to the state-of-the-art methods.
Our network also reduces the running time for training and testing by a factor of 2.1 and 3.4, respectively, compared to the second fastest method in the benchmark.
