Upon applying a voltage, ion-gel-gated oxide transistors undergo a reversible nanoscale conductance evolution.
We directly image, with nanometer resolution, this evolution in asymmetric InGaZnO thin-film transistors using scanning gate microscopy (SGM).
Nanoscale conductance evolution is induced by the ion gel, which is encapsulated in a polymer dielectric.
When a positive voltage is applied to the gate, indium ions are extracted from the oxide and migrate into the ion gel, leading to a conductance decrease.
Conductance recovery occurs upon removal of the gate voltage.
Our results show that the nanoscale conductance evolution is governed by ion movements in the dielectric, the extraction of In ions from the InGaZnO channel, and trap-assisted tunneling.

An increasingly popular approach to compressive sensing beamforming (CSB) is to use multiple snapshots of the desired signal, taken successively, and exploit the redundancy between the snapshots to further enhance compression performance.
In this paper, we consider the single-snapshot setting, in which the sensor array computes a compressed beamformer output based on a single arbitrary snapshot of the desired signal plus additive noise.
The resulting beamformer is inspired by the recently introduced multi-snapshots CSB, which explicitly utilizes the redundancy between multiple snapshots.
We show that the single-snapshot output can be equivalently obtained by projecting the multi-snapshot output onto the column space of the noise subspace.
We derive the projection relationship and propose an algorithm to compute the projection matrix.
Simulation results confirm the improved performance of the proposed method over existing single-snapshot CSBs.

An efficient dispersion modeling method for multilayered open coaxial waveguides is presented in this paper.
It is based on the mode-matching technique in which the modal propagation constant of each layer is obtained by matching the tangential components of the electric field at the interfaces between adjacent layers.
This approach permits the determination of the dispersion characteristics of multilayered open coaxial waveguides in a relatively simple and straightforward manner without any complicated mathematical procedures.
The obtained results are in good agreement with existing theoretical and experimental data.
The effects of the dielectric layer thickness, radii of the inner and outer conductors, and the permittivity of the dielectric material on the dispersion characteristics are investigated in detail.
It is found that the dispersion properties of the multilayered open coaxial waveguides can be manipulated by adjusting the geometric parameters and the permittivity of the dielectric material.

This paper presents SSHMT, a novel semi-supervised hierarchical merge tree algorithm for the segmentation of electron microscopy images.
The SSHMT algorithm combines the strengths of both supervised and unsupervised learning, using a hierarchical merge tree structure to combine labeled and unlabeled data for efficient segmentation.
The proposed method utilizes a novel cost function that considers both label consistency and spatial coherence, enabling accurate segmentation of electron microscopy images while preserving important structural details.


The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in segmenting a variety of electron microscopy images, including those with complex structures and noisy backgrounds.
The SSHMT algorithm is shown to outperform state-of-the-art semi-supervised segmentation methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.


The paper concludes by discussing the potential applications of the SSHMT algorithm in the field of electron microscopy image segmentation, and suggests further research directions in the development of more robust and efficient segmentation methods.

In this paper, we propose a regularized convolutional neural network (R-CNN) for semantic image segmentation.
Our network is based on a fully convolutional architecture and is trained using a supervised learning approach.
We use a regularization term in the loss function to improve the segmentation performance.
The regularization term is based on the idea of structural similarity, which measures the similarity between two images based on their structure.
We show that the addition of the regularization term to the loss function improves the segmentation performance by encouraging the network to produce outputs that are more similar to the ground truth.

In this paper, we address the problem of transductive image segmentation, which directly segments images in the wild without accessing any labeled images.
Unlike conventional semi-supervised learning methods that use a seed/initialization (e.g., a few labeled pixels) to bootstrap the segmentation, self-training directly learns image-specific segmentations without requiring any seed.
We show that by training an ensemble of predictors, self-training can correct prediction errors and boost the segmentation performance.
However, when uncertainty is estimated, the self-training process can be stuck in a local minimum, resulting in sub-optimal performance.
In this work, we analyze the cause of such local minima and propose a simple data augmentation technique that effectively avoids them.
We further propose an uncertainty-aware self-training framework that significantly improves the segmentation performance by selecting hard/challenging examples for the self-training process.

In this paper, we introduce BASNet and demonstrate its effectiveness and efficiency through a comprehensive set of experiments.
We show that BASNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on a variety of image segmentation benchmarks, while maintaining a high level of efficiency.

In this work, we propose a novel, learning-based approach for the segmentation of 3D and 4D multi-surface multi-object knee MRI data.
Our method utilizes a cost function that is learned from a large dataset of manually segmented images.
The cost function is designed to be invariant to patient-specific variations in anatomy and scanner settings, and is trained to segment multiple objects, including bone, cartilage, and meniscus, in 3D and 4D space.
We evaluated our method on a large dataset of images from the Osteoarthritis Initiative and compared it to a state-of-the-art, manual segmentation method.
Our results show that our method is comparable to the manual segmentation method in terms of accuracy, while providing significant time savings.
Furthermore, our method is able to generalize to images that were not included in the training dataset, demonstrating its ability to handle unseen data.

Our findings have important implications for understanding the behavior of complex random matrices and offer new insights into their applications in science and engineering.

Abstract: We propose a method for the fully-automatic segmentation of the spine from 3D tomographic images, with subsequent reconstruction of a 3D spine model.
Our approach includes a training set and a testing set of cervical, thoracic, and lumbar SPECT/CT images from 99 patients.
For training, we used 17,482 manually drawn contours of vertebrae by three observers, and additional 4,696 automatically segmented vertebrae as the initial labels.
For testing, we used 1,992 contours with ground truth.
Our approach is based on a convolutional neural network with a V-Net architecture trained using the Dice similarity coefficient as the loss function.

This paper proposes a fully transformer-based network for semantic image segmentation.
Unlike previous approaches that use convolutional neural networks (CNNs) as the backbone for segmentation, we use a transformer-based network as the backbone.

The abstract for the academic paper titled "A 3D Coarse-to-Fine Framework for Volumetric Medical Image Segmentation" would be:

Medical image segmentation is crucial for the diagnosis and treatment of various diseases.
We propose a 3D coarse-to-fine framework for volumetric medical image segmentation that incorporates a fully convolutional network (FCN) and a conditional random field (CRF).
The FCN is trained on a sparse set of labeled voxels, which are obtained by applying a threshold to the intensity values of the medical image.
The CRF is then used to refine the segmentation results obtained by the FCN.
The proposed framework is evaluated on a dataset of abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans and compared to a state-of-the-art method.
The results show that the proposed framework improves the segmentation accuracy and is able to handle large variations in the intensity values of the medical images.

An ab-initio quantum mechanical methodology, namely van der Waals density-functional theory (DFT), is used to evaluate the equilibrium geometries, intermolecular interactions, and electronic properties of bulk solids with cubic diamond, face-centered cubic (FCC), and body-centered cubic (BCC) structures.
DFT provides a straightforward and effective way to investigate the properties of molecules and solids without recourse to parameterized or fitted models.
The method is applicable to both small molecules and macromolecular assemblies, as well as to crystalline and amorphous solids.
In the present study, the van der Waals DFT is used to investigate the equilibrium structures of bulk solids with simple cubic (SC), FCC, and BCC structures, namely, silicon carbide, diamond, and iron respectively.
The intermolecular interactions and the electronic properties of these bulk solids are evaluated and compared.
It is shown that the van der Waals DFT provides a useful tool for investigating the properties of bulk solids.

Semantic image segmentation, namely pixel-level labeling, is a fundamental but challenging task in computer vision.
One of its main challenges is to accurately but efficiently assign labels to each pixel in the image.
In this paper, we present a novel approach to semantic image segmentation via deep parsing network (DPN).
Our DPN is composed of a shared-weight parsing network and a group of task-specific parsing networks.
The shared-weight parsing network is pre-trained on a large amount of image-text pairs, which not only leverages the power of image and text information but also implicitly learns image representations and spatial-level relationships between pixels.
The group of task-specific parsing networks are then fine-tuned on various pixel-level labeling tasks with different datasets.

In this paper, we propose a new approach to image segmentation that takes into account the structural prior knowledge of the object of interest.
We use a parametric model of the human body as our prior knowledge and cast the image segmentation problem as a sparse reconstruction problem.
We show that this approach is able to accurately segment images of humans while being more efficient than state-of-the-art image segmentation techniques.

We then sparse reconstruct the image pixels using our parametric model as the prior.

Unsupervised image segmentation is a classic problem in image processing, which is to segment images automatically without any prior knowledge of the images, target, or training.
We propose an approach for unsupervised image segmentation based on optimizing a global criterion in a Bayesian network framework.
Our approach combines the advantages of both a global and local criteria optimization.
The global criterion is used to capture the overall structure of the image, while the local criterion is used to refine the segmentation results at a finer scale.
We optimize the criteria using a dynamic programming approach.
The experimental results show that our approach is effective in segmenting images and outperforms other state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of segmentation quality.

In this paper, we develop a finite element formulation of general boundary conditions for incompressible flows.
We consider the Navier-Stokes equations in their full, non-conservative form, including the effects of inertial forces and viscous dissipation.
The boundary conditions are formulated using a discrete representation of the flow domain, which allows for the imposition of arbitrary boundary conditions on the interior and exterior of the domain.
The formulation is based on the concept of natural boundaries, which enables the treatment of general boundary conditions such as outflow, slip, and no-slip conditions.
We demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the formulation through a series of numerical examples, including the flow of an incompressible fluid through a pipe with different boundary conditions and the flow around a cylinder with a slip condition.
The proposed formulation provides a flexible and efficient tool for the numerical simulation of incompressible flows with complex boundary conditions.

We present a shape-based image segmentation approach that utilizes a variant of the popular Monte Carlo MCMC (Markov Chain Monte Carlo) algorithm for sampling from a joint distribution of pixels and shapes.
Our approach incorporates nonparametric shape priors into the segmentation process, allowing us to recover object structures without relying on any parameterized shape models.
We define a shape latent representation as a collection of region-shaped bins that are modeled as nonparametric distributions.
This enables the algorithm to discover the underlying shape structures in an unsupervised manner.
We further propose an efficient MCMC sampling strategy that explores the shape and pixel variables in a coordinated manner, significantly improving the convergence speed compared to existing MCMC-based segmentation methods.
The proposed approach is evaluated on synthetic and real-world images, and the results demonstrate its ability to accurately segment objects while effectively exploiting the shape information.

Our approach utilizes a pre-trained model to generate synthetic data that closely resembles the real world data distribution.
We demonstrate that our method can generate high quality datasets with minimal effort and time, and can improve the accuracy of crop and weeds detection models.
Furthermore, we show that our method is general and can be applied to other similar detection tasks.

This research contributes to the fields of computer vision and interior design by providing a new tool for automatic object detection and color harmonization.

This paper presents a novel approach to ballast degradation evaluation using a machine vision algorithm implemented in Matlab.
Ballast degradation is a critical issue in railway maintenance and its accurate assessment is crucial for ensuring safety and efficiency.
Traditional methods of evaluation are often time-consuming and subjective.
To address these challenges, we propose a machine vision algorithm that can automatically analyze and quantify the degree of ballast degradation.
The algorithm is designed to process and analyze images of ballast, identify the key features associated with degradation, and provide a quantitative measure of the degradation level.
The implementation of the algorithm in Matlab allows for efficient processing and easy integration with existing systems.

This paper explores the concept of hybrid hypercomputing, a theoretical model that aims to unify quantum and classical computation.
The study delves into the potential of combining the strengths of both computational models to overcome their individual limitations.
It discusses the principles of quantum and classical computing, their differences, and how they can be integrated in a hybrid model.
The paper also examines the potential applications and challenges of hybrid hypercomputing.
The findings suggest that this unification could lead to significant advancements in computational power and efficiency, opening new avenues for research in various scientific fields.
However, the practical realization of hybrid hypercomputing requires further investigation and technological advancements.

The paper also discusses the potential benefits of morphological neurons, such as their ability to handle non-linear operations and their robustness against noise.
The findings suggest that further research and development in this area could lead to significant advancements in artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies.

This paper investigates the environmental, thermal, and electrical susceptibility of Black Phosphorus Field Effect Transistors (BP FETs).
The study provides a comprehensive analysis of the stability of BP FETs under various conditions, including exposure to air, heat, and electrical stress.
The results reveal that BP FETs exhibit significant degradation in performance when exposed to ambient conditions due to the high reactivity of black phosphorus with oxygen and water.
Additionally, the devices show a considerable decrease in stability under thermal and electrical stress.
The findings suggest that encapsulation techniques and device engineering are crucial for improving the stability and performance of BP FETs.
This study contributes to the understanding of the limitations of BP FETs and provides insights for future research and development in this field.

This paper presents a novel chaotic image encryption method using a generalized threshold function.
The proposed method integrates the advantages of chaos theory and threshold functions to enhance the security and robustness of image encryption.
The encryption process involves the use of a chaotic map for permutation and a generalized threshold function for diffusion, ensuring high sensitivity to initial conditions and parameters.
The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method provides superior security performance in terms of key space, key sensitivity, statistical attacks, and differential attacks.
Furthermore, it exhibits excellent robustness against noise and cropping attacks.
This innovative approach to image encryption has potential applications in secure image transmission and storage.

This paper presents a novel approach to fundus image segmentation using boundary and entropy-driven adversarial learning.
The study aims to address the challenges in accurately segmenting retinal structures in fundus images, which is crucial for diagnosing and monitoring various ocular diseases.
The proposed method leverages the adversarial learning framework to enhance the discriminative capability of the segmentation model.
It introduces a boundary loss function to emphasize the importance of accurate boundary prediction and an entropy loss function to encourage the model to make confident predictions.
Experimental results on public fundus image datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.
This research contributes to the advancement of medical image analysis and has potential applications in automated diagnosis systems for ocular diseases.

This paper investigates the relationship between tail risk constraints and maximum entropy in financial modeling.
It proposes a novel approach to portfolio optimization that incorporates tail risk constraints, which are often overlooked in traditional models.
The study demonstrates that by considering tail risk, investors can achieve more efficient and robust portfolio allocations.
Furthermore, the paper introduces a new method based on the principle of maximum entropy to estimate the probability of extreme losses.
The results show that this method provides more accurate estimates than conventional techniques, thereby enhancing portfolio risk management.
The findings have significant implications for both academics and practitioners in the fields of finance and risk management.

The model's performance is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements over existing semi-supervised learning methods.
The results suggest that the integration of uncertainty estimation in multi-view co-training can effectively improve the model's performance in 3D object recognition tasks.
This research contributes to the advancement of semi-supervised learning techniques in the field of 3D object recognition.

This paper presents DeepIGeoS, a novel deep learning-based interactive geodesic framework for medical image segmentation.
The proposed method combines the strengths of deep learning models and interactive geodesic methods to provide accurate and efficient segmentation of medical images.
DeepIGeoS employs a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn a feature representation that is used to compute a geodesic distance map.
The user interaction is incorporated into the geodesic computation, allowing for intuitive and flexible control over the segmentation process.
The effectiveness of DeepIGeoS is evaluated on several medical imaging datasets, demonstrating superior performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art methods.
The proposed framework has potential applications in various medical imaging tasks, including tumor detection, organ segmentation, and anatomical structure delineation.

This paper presents a novel approach for embryo egg detection using K-means segmentation based on Lab color space.
The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of embryo egg detection in the field of poultry farming and embryology.
The proposed method involves converting the RGB color space of the image to Lab color space, followed by K-means clustering for image segmentation.
The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using various metrics such as precision, recall, and F1-score.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional RGB-based K-means segmentation in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
This research contributes to the advancement of image processing techniques in the field of embryology and offers potential applications in automated poultry farming systems.

This paper presents a novel approach to fuzzy image segmentation using an evolutionary algorithm with self-configuration.
The proposed method aims to address the challenges of determining optimal parameters and thresholds in traditional fuzzy image segmentation techniques.
The evolutionary algorithm is designed to adaptively adjust these parameters, enhancing the segmentation performance.
The self-configuration aspect allows the system to autonomously adapt to different image characteristics, improving the robustness and versatility of the segmentation process.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and adaptability compared to conventional fuzzy image segmentation techniques.
This research contributes to the field of image processing by providing a more flexible and efficient solution for image segmentation tasks.

This paper presents a novel probabilistic approach to image segmentation in video sequences.
The proposed method leverages the temporal continuity in video data to improve the accuracy and robustness of segmentation.
The approach is based on a probabilistic graphical model that captures the spatial and temporal dependencies between pixels, and uses a Bayesian inference algorithm for segmentation.
The model is flexible and can handle different types of video content, including scenes with complex motion and changing backgrounds.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of both segmentation quality and computational efficiency.
The paper also discusses potential applications of the method in video editing, object tracking, and scene understanding.

This paper presents a novel approach for brain tumor segmentation and overall survival prediction using an ensemble of 3D U-Nets and radiomic features.
The study focuses on the application of deep learning techniques for the accurate segmentation of brain tumors from MRI scans.
The proposed method utilizes an ensemble of 3D U-Nets, which significantly improves the segmentation performance by leveraging the strengths of multiple models.
Furthermore, the paper explores the use of radiomic features for predicting the overall survival of patients.
These features, extracted from the segmented tumor regions, provide valuable insights into tumor characteristics that are strongly correlated with patient survival.
The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both segmentation accuracy and survival prediction.

This paper presents a novel teacher-student framework for semi-supervised medical image segmentation using mixed supervision.
The proposed method leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the performance of segmentation tasks.
The teacher model, trained on labeled data, guides the student model, which learns from both labeled and unlabeled data.
The student model is then fine-tuned using the teacher's predictions on unlabeled data.
Experimental results on several medical imaging datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, showing significant improvements over existing semi-supervised learning methods.
This framework has potential applications in medical imaging where labeled data is often scarce and expensive to obtain.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation, termed Piecewise Flat Embedding (PFE).
The PFE method aims to address the challenges associated with traditional image segmentation techniques, such as sensitivity to noise and inability to handle complex structures.
The proposed method leverages the concept of piecewise flatness, embedding the image in a high-dimensional space where the segmentation problem is transformed into a simpler one.
The PFE method is robust to noise, can handle images with complex structures, and is computationally efficient.
Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of the PFE method in comparison to existing image segmentation techniques.
The paper also discusses potential applications of the PFE method in various fields, including computer vision, medical imaging, and remote sensing.

This paper presents a novel approach to color image segmentation using Voronoi region-based adaptive unsupervised learning.
The proposed method overcomes the limitations of traditional segmentation techniques by dynamically adapting to the unique characteristics of each image.
The algorithm begins by partitioning the image into Voronoi regions, which are then iteratively refined using a combination of color and spatial information.
The adaptive nature of the algorithm allows it to effectively handle images with varying color distributions and spatial structures.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing unsupervised segmentation techniques in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
The paper also discusses potential applications of this approach in areas such as image editing, object recognition, and computer vision.

This paper explores the potential contributions of noncontact atomic force microscopy (nc-AFM) in future Casimir force measurements.
The Casimir force, a quantum mechanical phenomenon, is challenging to measure due to its minute nature and the influence of various environmental factors.
The paper discusses the principles of nc-AFM and its advantages over traditional methods in measuring the Casimir force.

The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of computational efficiency and scalability.
This research provides valuable insights into the design of more effective algorithms for solving CSPs defined by partially-ordered forbidden patterns.

The main focus is on the correlation between the presence of Petersen cores and the level of oddness in cubic graphs.
The findings suggest a strong connection between the two, providing new insights into the structure and characteristics of cubic graphs.
This research opens up new avenues for further exploration in the field of graph theory.

This paper investigates the Ott-Antonsen (OA) attractiveness in parameter-dependent oscillatory networks.
The OA theory is a powerful tool for reducing the dimensionality of large populations of oscillators, but its applicability to parameter-dependent networks has not been thoroughly explored.
We present a comprehensive analysis of the OA attractiveness for such networks, considering both static and dynamic parameters.
Our findings reveal that the OA attractiveness is robust under a wide range of parameter variations, making it a versatile tool for the analysis of complex oscillatory networks.
We also identify certain conditions under which the OA attractiveness may break down, providing valuable insights for future research.
The results have significant implications for the study of various real-world systems, including neural networks, power grids, and climate models.

This paper introduces SemSegLoss, a Python package that provides a comprehensive collection of loss functions specifically designed for semantic segmentation tasks.
Semantic segmentation, a crucial task in computer vision, often requires specialized loss functions to optimize model performance.
However, the implementation of these functions can be complex and time-consuming.
SemSegLoss addresses this issue by offering a wide range of pre-implemented loss functions, including cross-entropy loss, dice loss, and Jaccard loss, among others.
The package is designed to be user-friendly, efficient, and easily integrated into existing machine learning pipelines.
Experimental results demonstrate that using SemSegLoss can significantly improve the performance of semantic segmentation models.

We propose a unified model that simultaneously learns region, edge, and contour information from images.
The model is trained on a large dataset of diverse images, enabling it to generalize well to new images.
Our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our model through extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets.
The results show that our unified model can accurately segment images, highlighting its potential for various applications such as object detection, image editing, and medical imaging.

This paper presents a novel approach for small target detection in search and rescue operations using distributed deep learning and synthetic data generation.
The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of locating small targets in complex environments, which is a critical challenge in search and rescue missions.
The proposed method leverages the power of distributed deep learning algorithms to process large-scale data and synthetic data generation techniques to augment the training dataset.
The results demonstrate that our approach significantly enhances the detection performance compared to traditional methods.
Furthermore, the use of synthetic data addresses the issue of limited real-world data in training deep learning models.
This research contributes to the advancement of search and rescue technology and has potential applications in various fields such as disaster management, military operations, and wildlife monitoring.

This paper presents an in-depth study of Kernel Spectral Clustering (KSC), a non-linear version of spectral clustering that uses the kernel trick to operate in a high-dimensional feature space.
The paper begins with a comprehensive overview of the theoretical foundations of KSC, including its mathematical formulation, algorithmic implementation, and the role of the kernel function.
It then explores various applications of KSC in diverse fields such as image segmentation, bioinformatics, and social network analysis.
The paper also discusses the challenges and limitations of KSC, such as the choice of the kernel function and the scalability issue.
Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that KSC can outperform traditional spectral clustering in handling complex and non-linearly separable data.
The paper concludes with future research directions in improving the efficiency and effectiveness of KSC.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on robust submodular minimization and its applications in cooperative modeling.
We introduce a novel algorithm for submodular minimization that is robust to noise and uncertainties, overcoming the limitations of existing methods.
The proposed algorithm is based on a new theoretical framework that integrates robust optimization and submodular functions.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through extensive experiments on various cooperative modeling tasks, including network design, sensor placement, and cooperative game theory.
The results show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of both solution quality and computational efficiency.
This research opens up new avenues for the application of robust submodular minimization in cooperative modeling and other related fields.

This paper introduces FedDG, a novel approach to medical image segmentation using Federated Domain Generalization (FDG) via episodic learning in continuous frequency space.
The study addresses the challenge of data heterogeneity and privacy in medical imaging, which often hampers the performance of deep learning models.
FedDG leverages the concept of domain generalization to learn a model on multiple domains while ensuring data privacy through federated learning.
The proposed method employs episodic training in the continuous frequency space to enhance the model's generalization ability.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that FedDG outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy, robustness, and privacy preservation.
The findings suggest that FedDG could be a promising solution for privacy-preserving medical image segmentation in multi-center scenarios.

This paper presents the design and application of a novel variable temperature environmental capsule for scanning electron microscopy (SEM) in gases and liquids at ambient conditions.
The capsule allows for in-situ observations of samples in their native state, overcoming the limitations of conventional SEM that requires high vacuum conditions.
The design incorporates a heating and cooling system, enabling temperature control from -20°C to 100°C.
The capsule's performance was evaluated through a series of experiments involving various materials and conditions.
The results demonstrate the capsule's ability to provide high-resolution images and valuable insights into the dynamic behaviors of samples under different environmental conditions.
This innovative tool opens up new possibilities for research in materials science, biology, geology, and other fields.

This paper presents a novel approach to 3D surface segmentation using a deep neural network (DNN) based on contour tree hierarchy.
The study aims to address the challenges in segmenting complex 3D surfaces in various fields such as computer graphics, medical imaging, and geospatial analysis.
The proposed method leverages the contour tree hierarchy to capture the topological structure of 3D surfaces, which is then processed by the DNN for accurate segmentation.
Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
Furthermore, the proposed method shows robustness against noise and can handle large-scale datasets.
This research opens up new possibilities for advanced 3D surface analysis and manipulation.

It also discusses the challenges and limitations of implementing deep learning in healthcare settings, such as data privacy concerns and the need for large, annotated datasets.
The paper concludes with a discussion on future directions and potential advancements in this rapidly evolving field.
This review is intended to serve as a primer for researchers, clinicians, and other stakeholders interested in the intersection of artificial intelligence and healthcare.

The proposed method leverages the strengths of LDA for initial topic modeling and DNNs for advanced pattern recognition.

Experimental results on several historical document datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, showing significant improvements in segmentation accuracy compared to existing methods.
The study also discusses potential applications of this approach in digital humanities and archival science.

This paper presents a novel approach to address the challenge of highly imbalanced medical image segmentation, specifically for the detection of Multiple Sclerosis (MS) lesions.
The study introduces the use of asymmetric loss functions and deep densely connected networks to improve the performance of segmentation models.
The proposed method is designed to handle the imbalance between the lesion and non-lesion classes, which is a common issue in medical image analysis.
The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated using a large dataset of MS patients.
The results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy.
This research contributes to the advancement of automated MS lesion detection, potentially leading to more accurate diagnoses and better patient management.

This paper presents a novel approach to improve aleatoric uncertainty quantification in multi-annotated medical image segmentation using normalizing flows.
Aleatoric uncertainty, which arises from inherent noise in the data, is a critical aspect in medical image analysis.
However, existing methods often fail to accurately quantify this uncertainty, leading to potential inaccuracies in diagnosis and treatment planning.
To address this issue, we propose a new framework that leverages the power of normalizing flows, a class of deep generative models, to model the complex distribution of aleatoric uncertainty.
Our method provides a more accurate and reliable uncertainty quantification, as validated on several medical imaging datasets.
The results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods, offering significant potential for enhancing the reliability and effectiveness of medical image analysis.

This paper presents a novel isotropic inverse-problem approach for two-dimensional phase unwrapping.
The study aims to address the inherent limitations of traditional phase unwrapping methods, which often struggle with noise and discontinuities.
The proposed method leverages the isotropic property of the wrapped phase to formulate the unwrapping problem as an inverse problem.
This approach allows for the incorporation of prior information and noise modeling, leading to more robust and accurate unwrapping results.
The paper provides a detailed mathematical formulation of the proposed method, along with experimental results demonstrating its superior performance over conventional techniques.
The findings of this study have significant implications for various fields, including radar imaging, optical metrology, and magnetic resonance imaging.

The paper further discusses the implications of these results for the development of more accurate and efficient turbulence models.

The framework is designed to optimize a combination of these loss functions, allowing for more accurate and flexible learning.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and flexibility.
The paper also provides theoretical analysis, showing that the proposed method can effectively balance between different loss functions and adapt to various structured data.
This work opens up new possibilities for learning from complex structured data with multiple types of annotations.

Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets illustrate the superior performance of the proposed method in comparison to existing unsupervised learning algorithms.
The findings of this study have significant implications for the field of machine learning, particularly in tasks involving high-dimensional data and complex data structures.

This paper presents a novel approach to adaptive parameter estimation in distributed networks using a diffusion-based least mean square (LMS) algorithm.
The proposed method allows for node-specific adaptation, enabling each node to estimate its own parameters independently while still benefiting from the information shared by neighboring nodes.
The performance of the proposed algorithm is evaluated in terms of mean-square deviation and network mean-square deviation.
The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional diffusion-based LMS algorithms in terms of convergence speed and estimation accuracy.
Furthermore, the paper provides a detailed analysis of the algorithm's stability and robustness against variations in network topology and environmental conditions.
This research has significant implications for the design of adaptive distributed systems in various fields, including signal processing, machine learning, and wireless sensor networks.

This paper presents a novel approach to medical image segmentation using consensus-based semi-supervised learning and graph cuts.
The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation, a critical aspect of medical image analysis that directly impacts diagnosis and treatment planning.
The proposed method combines the strengths of semi-supervised learning, which utilizes both labeled and unlabeled data, and graph cuts, a powerful tool for image segmentation.
The consensus-based approach ensures that the final segmentation result is an agreement among multiple segmentation hypotheses.
Experimental results on various medical imaging datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving high-quality segmentation results.
The study also discusses potential applications and future directions for further research in this area.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the challenges of inter-annotator agreement in automated skin lesion segmentation.
It explores the variability in human annotations and its impact on the performance of machine learning models.
The study introduces a novel approach to handle inter-annotator disagreement, which includes a robust training strategy and a consensus-based annotation method.
The proposed method is evaluated using a large dataset of skin lesion images with annotations from multiple experts.
The results demonstrate that our approach significantly improves the segmentation performance and reduces the effect of inter-annotator variability.
This research contributes to the advancement of automated skin lesion segmentation, which is crucial for early detection and treatment of skin cancer.

This paper presents a novel approach to 2D medical image segmentation using contrastive semi-supervised learning.
The study aims to address the challenges of limited annotated medical images and the high cost of manual annotation.
The proposed method leverages unlabeled data to improve the performance of segmentation models.
It introduces a contrastive loss function that encourages the model to produce similar representations for the same class and different representations for different classes.
The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated on several public medical image datasets, demonstrating significant improvements over existing supervised and semi-supervised methods.
The results suggest that contrastive semi-supervised learning can effectively utilize unlabeled data to enhance the performance of medical image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach to infant brain MRI segmentation using deep convolutional neural network (CNN) ensembles and suggestive annotations.
The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of MRI segmentation, a critical process in diagnosing and treating various neurological conditions in infants.
The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning algorithms and the collective intelligence of multiple CNN models to achieve superior segmentation performance.
Additionally, the use of suggestive annotations further enhances the model's ability to identify and delineate different brain structures.
Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
This research contributes to the ongoing efforts to advance medical imaging technology and has potential implications for improving infant brain health outcomes.

This paper presents a novel approach to 3D medical image segmentation using multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) with iterative refinement.
The proposed method addresses the challenges of accurate and efficient segmentation of complex anatomical structures in medical images, which is crucial for diagnosis, treatment planning, and surgical navigation.
The method employs multiple agents that learn to segment the image collaboratively and iteratively refine the segmentation results.
The agents are trained using reinforcement learning, enabling them to adapt to the complexity and variability of medical images.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the accuracy and efficiency of 3D medical image segmentation.
The method also shows potential for interactive segmentation, where the user can guide the segmentation process, making it more flexible and user-friendly.

The model leverages the power of deep learning to extract hierarchical features and learn high-level semantics, thereby improving the accuracy of salient object detection.
DeepSaliency is designed to perform two tasks simultaneously: saliency prediction and semantic segmentation.
The model is trained on a large-scale dataset and evaluated using standard benchmarks.
Experimental results demonstrate that DeepSaliency outperforms state-of-the-art models in terms of precision, recall, and F-measure.
The model also exhibits robustness against variations in object size, location, and background complexity.

This paper presents a novel algorithm,
Multi-hop Diffusion Least Mean Squares (LMS), for energy-constrained distributed estimation in sensor networks.
The proposed method addresses the challenge of energy conservation in distributed estimation, a critical issue in wireless sensor networks where nodes operate on limited power.
The algorithm leverages the multi-hop communication strategy to reduce energy consumption while maintaining estimation accuracy.
Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional diffusion LMS in terms of energy efficiency and estimation performance, particularly in networks with stringent energy constraints.
The paper also provides a theoretical analysis of the algorithm's convergence and stability properties.

This paper presents a novel approach to few-shot segmentation, combining global and local contrastive learning.
The study proposes a dual-branch architecture that separately captures global and local features, enhancing the model's ability to distinguish between target and background classes.
The global branch focuses on the overall image context, while the local branch concentrates on detailed features.
The model is trained using a contrastive loss function, encouraging the learning of discriminative features.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing few-shot segmentation methods, highlighting the effectiveness of combining global and local contrastive learning.
This research provides a new perspective on few-shot learning and opens up new avenues for future research in this area.

This paper introduces ISNet, a novel framework for semantic segmentation that integrates image-level and semantic-level context.
Semantic segmentation is a critical task in computer vision, which involves classifying each pixel in an image into a specific category.
Existing methods primarily focus on exploiting local features or global context, but often neglect the semantic-level context.
ISNet addresses this gap by incorporating both image-level and semantic-level context into a unified framework.
The image-level context captures the overall scene information, while the semantic-level context focuses on the relationships between different semantic categories.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that ISNet significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy, proving the effectiveness of integrating both levels of context for semantic segmentation.

This paper presents an efficient evolutionary-based method for image segmentation, a critical task in image processing and computer vision.
The proposed method combines the strengths of genetic algorithms and multi-objective optimization to segment images accurately and efficiently.
The algorithm is designed to optimize the segmentation process by minimizing the intra-class variance and maximizing the inter-class variance.
The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using several benchmark images and compared with existing segmentation techniques.
The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the existing techniques in terms of accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness to noise.
This research contributes to the field by providing a novel and effective approach for image segmentation, with potential applications in various domains such as medical imaging, remote sensing, and video surveillance.

The paper explores various multi-fidelity modeling techniques, including co-kriging, multi-fidelity Gaussian process regression, and surrogate modeling.
It also discusses their applications in diverse fields such as aerospace engineering, climate modeling, and machine learning.
The paper further highlights the challenges and potential future directions in the development and application of multi-fidelity models.
The aim is to provide researchers and practitioners with a deeper understanding of the current state of multi-fidelity modeling and its potential for future research and applications.

This paper presents a novel approach to unsupervised image segmentation using the Deffuant-Weisbuch (DW) model from social dynamics.
The DW model, typically used to simulate opinion dynamics in social networks, is adapted to address the problem of image segmentation.
The proposed method treats each pixel as an agent with an initial opinion (color value) and allows these agents to interact based on the DW model rules.
The interactions result in the formation of clusters of pixels with similar color values, effectively segmenting the image.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional image segmentation techniques in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
The paper also discusses potential applications of this approach in various fields such as computer vision, medical imaging, and remote sensing.

This paper presents a novel approach to higher order differentiation over finite fields, with a particular focus on its applications in generalising the cube attack.
The cube attack is a powerful cryptanalytic method used to analyse and break symmetric key cryptographic primitives.
We introduce a new mathematical framework that allows for a more efficient computation of higher order derivatives, which is a crucial step in the cube attack.
Our approach is based on algebraic techniques and exploits the properties of finite fields to reduce the computational complexity.
We provide a detailed theoretical analysis of our method, as well as experimental results that demonstrate its effectiveness.
This research not only enhances the cube attack, but also contributes to the broader field of cryptanalysis by providing new insights into the algebraic structure of cryptographic functions.

This paper presents a novel approach to domain adaptation, specifically focusing on scribble-based co-segmentation.
The study proposes a method that leverages scribbles, simple user annotations, to adapt a pre-trained model to a new domain.
The approach is based on the idea that scribbles can provide high-level semantic guidance, which can be used to align the feature distributions of different domains.
The paper introduces a co-segmentation framework that jointly optimizes the segmentation results of the source and target domains, ensuring that the model learns consistent and transferable features.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing domain adaptation techniques in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
The study contributes to the field by providing a new perspective on domain adaptation and offering a practical solution for real-world applications.

This paper introduces W-Net, a novel deep learning model for fully unsupervised image segmentation.
The model is designed to overcome the limitations of existing methods that require manual annotation or prior knowledge.
W-Net is a two-stage network that first generates an over-segmented image and then merges the segments to produce the final segmentation.
The model is trained using a combination of unsupervised learning techniques, including auto-encoders and clustering.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that W-Net outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised segmentation methods in terms of both segmentation quality and computational efficiency.
The proposed model has potential applications in various fields such as medical imaging, remote sensing, and computer vision.

This paper presents a novel approach to probabilistic image segmentation, termed as "Tree-Cut".
The method is based on the concept of graph cuts, but with a unique twist that involves the construction of a tree structure to represent the image.
The Tree-Cut algorithm is designed to handle uncertainties in image data, making it particularly suitable for applications where the image quality is poor or the objects of interest are not clearly defined.
The paper provides a detailed description of the Tree-Cut method, including its mathematical formulation and algorithmic implementation.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional graph cut-based methods in terms of both segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The Tree-Cut approach opens up new possibilities for probabilistic image segmentation, offering a robust and efficient solution to this challenging problem.

This paper presents a novel approach to the automated segmentation of cervical nuclei in Pap smear images using a deformable multi-path ensemble model.
The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of cervical cancer screening by automating the process of identifying and segmenting cervical nuclei, a critical step in the diagnosis of cervical cancer.
The proposed model combines the strengths of deformable models and multi-path ensemble learning to achieve high segmentation accuracy.
It leverages the power of deep learning to extract complex features from Pap smear images and uses a deformable model to adapt to the shape variations of cervical nuclei.
The model's performance was evaluated using a large dataset of Pap smear images, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing methods.
This research contributes to the advancement of computer-aided diagnosis systems in cervical cancer screening, potentially improving diagnostic accuracy and reducing the workload of pathologists.

This paper presents a novel approach to interactive image segmentation using label propagation through complex networks.
The proposed method leverages the inherent structure of images as complex networks, where nodes represent pixels and edges signify the relationship between them.
The segmentation process is guided by user interaction, where the user labels a few representative pixels, and these labels are propagated through the network.
The method is based on the assumption that pixels within the same segment are highly interconnected, thus forming a community within the network.
The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods.
This research opens up new avenues for incorporating complex network theory into image analysis tasks.

The algorithm's performance is rigorously evaluated through extensive simulations and real-world data, demonstrating its superior efficiency and robustness compared to existing methods.
This research not only contributes to the theoretical understanding of phase retrieval but also provides a practical tool for various applications.

This paper presents a novel approach to segmenting camera-trap images using multi-layer robust principal component analysis (RPCA).
Camera-trap images are a valuable resource for wildlife monitoring and ecological studies, but their analysis is often hindered by the presence of various types of noise and interference.
Traditional image segmentation methods often fail to accurately separate the objects of interest from the background.
To address this issue, we propose a multi-layer RPCA-based method that effectively separates foreground objects from complex backgrounds, even in the presence of noise and occlusions.
Our method leverages the robustness of RPCA to outliers and its ability to handle high-dimensional data.
Experimental results on a large dataset of camera-trap images demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, showing significant improvements in segmentation accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods.

This paper presents Box-Adapt, a novel approach to domain-adaptive medical image segmentation using bounding box supervision.
The study addresses the challenge of domain shift in medical image analysis, which often leads to a significant drop in the performance of segmentation models when applied to new, unseen data.
Box-Adapt leverages bounding box annotations, which are easier to obtain than pixel-wise annotations, to adapt a segmentation model to a new domain.
The proposed method involves a two-stage training process: pre-training on source domain with pixel-wise annotations and fine-tuning on target domain with bounding box annotations.
Experimental results on several medical imaging datasets demonstrate that Box-Adapt significantly outperforms existing domain adaptation methods, providing more accurate and robust segmentation results.
The study suggests that bounding box supervision can be an effective strategy for domain adaptation in medical image segmentation.

This paper presents a comprehensive comparison of the 3-fluid dynamic model with experimental data.
The 3-fluid dynamic model, a theoretical framework used to describe the behavior of multi-phase flows, is evaluated against empirical data collected from various experiments.
The study aims to validate the accuracy and reliability of the model in predicting fluid dynamics under different conditions.
The results indicate a significant correlation between the model predictions and experimental observations, suggesting the model's effectiveness.
However, certain discrepancies were also noted, highlighting areas for further refinement of the model.
This research provides valuable insights for improving multi-phase flow models and contributes to the broader understanding of fluid dynamics.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on image segmentation of cross-country scenes captured in the Infrared (IR) spectrum.
The primary focus is to develop and evaluate algorithms that can effectively segment and interpret IR images, which are typically characterized by low contrast, high noise, and complex backgrounds.
The paper introduces a novel segmentation method that combines adaptive thresholding, region growing, and edge detection techniques.
The proposed method is tested on a large dataset of cross-country scenes and compared with existing segmentation techniques.
The results demonstrate that our method significantly improves the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation in IR spectrum, thereby enhancing the performance of subsequent tasks such as object detection and recognition.
This research has potential applications in various fields including autonomous vehicles, surveillance systems, and remote sensing.

The study aims to determine the effectiveness of this strategy in predicting the performance of WIG20 futures, a leading index of the Warsaw Stock Exchange.
The research employs historical data analysis and simulation techniques to evaluate the potential returns and risks associated with this investment strategy.
The findings suggest that the Zipf strategy can provide valuable insights for short-term investment decisions in WIG20 futures, although it is not without risks.
This study contributes to the existing literature on financial market prediction and offers practical implications for investors and financial analysts.

This paper presents a novel approach to multi-level image thresholding using a Type II Fuzzy Entropy and an Adaptive Plant Propagation Algorithm (APPA).
The proposed method aims to address the limitations of traditional image thresholding techniques, which often struggle with handling uncertainties and noise in images.
The Type II Fuzzy Entropy is employed to effectively manage these uncertainties, while the APPA is used to optimize the threshold values.
The APPA is an evolutionary algorithm inspired by the natural propagation behavior of plants.
The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using several benchmark images and compared with other state-of-the-art thresholding methods.
The results demonstrate that our approach provides superior performance in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation that combines fuzzy classification and contextual region growing.
Image segmentation is a critical task in image processing and computer vision, with applications ranging from medical imaging to autonomous vehicles.
Traditional methods often struggle with complex images, leading to inaccurate segmentations.
Our proposed method addresses these challenges by integrating fuzzy classification, which handles uncertainty and ambiguity in pixel classification, with contextual region growing, which considers spatial relationships between pixels.
Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness, particularly in images with high levels of noise and complexity.
This research opens new avenues for improving image segmentation techniques and their applications.

This paper presents a novel approach to optimal decision-making in mixed-agent partially observable stochastic environments using reinforcement learning.
The study focuses on environments where both human and artificial agents interact, and the state of the environment is partially observable and stochastic.
The proposed method integrates reinforcement learning with Bayesian inference to optimize decision-making under uncertainty.
The algorithm learns from the environment and adjusts its strategies based on the observed outcomes, allowing for efficient and adaptive decision-making.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in various scenarios, outperforming traditional methods in terms of both speed and accuracy.
This research contributes to the field of artificial intelligence by providing a robust framework for decision-making in complex, mixed-agent environments.

This paper explores the theoretical frameworks and experimental evidence that suggest the existence of physics beyond the Standard Model.
The Standard Model of particle physics, while successful in explaining a wide range of phenomena, has several limitations and unanswered questions.
These include the nature of dark matter, the matter-antimatter asymmetry in the universe, and the hierarchy problem.
Various theories such as supersymmetry, string theory, and quantum gravity have been proposed to address these issues.
The paper also discusses the experimental efforts to detect new physics, including collider experiments, dark matter searches, and neutrino oscillation experiments.
The discovery of physics beyond the Standard Model would have profound implications for our understanding of the universe.

This paper presents a novel image segmentation method that integrates Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence-based fuzzy C-means clustering, morphological reconstruction, and wavelet frames.
The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and robustness of image segmentation, particularly in dealing with images with complex textures and noise.
The KL divergence-based fuzzy C-means clustering enhances the clustering performance by considering the statistical characteristics of the data.
The morphological reconstruction is used to eliminate the small regions and noise.
The wavelet frames are employed to capture the multi-scale and directional information of the image.
Experimental results on various types of images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms several state-of-the-art image segmentation methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to noise.

This paper presents a novel combinatorial definition of the Theta-invariant derived from Heegaard diagrams.
The Theta-invariant is a topological invariant that plays a crucial role in the study of 3-manifolds, particularly in the context of Heegaard Floer homology.
Our approach simplifies the computation of the Theta-invariant by reducing it to a combinatorial problem on Heegaard diagrams.
We provide a detailed exposition of our method, including a step-by-step algorithm for computing the Theta-invariant.
We also discuss the implications of our results for the study of knot theory and 3-manifold topology.
Our findings open up new avenues for the exploration of the combinatorial aspects of Heegaard Floer homology and its invariants.

This paper presents a novel approach to neuron reconstruction using Hidden Markov Models (HMMs).
The primary objective is to maximize the likelihood of accurate neuron reconstruction from microscopy images.
The proposed method involves the application of HMMs to model the complex spatial structure of neurons and the uncertainty in the image data.
The model parameters are estimated using a maximum likelihood approach, which is computationally efficient and robust to noise.
Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
This research opens up new avenues for the application of HMMs in the field of neuroscience and provides a powerful tool for the analysis of neuronal structures.

This paper presents a novel approach to 3D biomedical image segmentation by combining Fully Convolutional Neural Networks (FCNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs).
The proposed method leverages the strengths of both FCNNs and RNNs to achieve high accuracy in segmenting 3D biomedical images.
FCNNs are used to extract spatial features from the images, while RNNs are employed to capture the sequential information in the 3D context.
The combination of these two types of networks allows for more precise segmentation of complex structures in 3D biomedical images.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, outperforming state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy and efficiency.
This research opens up new possibilities for improving the diagnosis and treatment of diseases by providing more accurate 3D biomedical image segmentation.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the robust output regulation problem for continuous-time periodic systems.
The primary focus is on developing a systematic and efficient approach to design robust output regulators for such systems under the influence of external disturbances.
The proposed method is based on the internal model principle and the geometric control theory.
The paper also introduces a novel concept of the robust regulation error system, which is instrumental in the analysis and synthesis of the robust output regulator.
The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through numerical simulations.
The results show that the designed robust output regulator can achieve satisfactory tracking and disturbance rejection performance, even in the presence of system uncertainties and external disturbances.

The results show that the proposed model outperforms traditional MRFs and other state-of-the-art models in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
This research opens up new possibilities for the application of MRFs in areas such as image processing, computer vision, and machine learning.

The results demonstrate that these cavities exhibit high stability and quality factor, making them suitable for various applications in quantum information processing, optical communication, and sensing.
The paper also highlights the challenges in fabricating these cavities and proposes potential solutions to overcome these issues.
The findings of this study contribute to the advancement of photonic crystal technology and its applications.

This paper presents a novel approach to aerial image segmentation using online maps as a learning source.
The study proposes a method that leverages the rich, detailed information available in online maps to train a deep learning model for segmenting aerial images.
The model is designed to recognize various features such as buildings, roads, vegetation, and water bodies.
The proposed approach overcomes the limitations of traditional methods that require extensive manual labeling and are often constrained by the availability of high-quality training data.
Experimental results demonstrate that the model trained with online map data significantly outperforms models trained with manually labeled data, highlighting the potential of online maps as a valuable resource for aerial image segmentation.
The study's findings have implications for various applications, including urban planning, environmental monitoring, and disaster management.

The paper concludes with potential applications and future directions for this research.

This paper investigates the problem of resource allocation in Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar systems for non-coherent localization of multiple targets.
The primary objective is to optimize the allocation of power and antennas to enhance the localization accuracy.
A novel resource allocation algorithm is proposed, which is based on the Cramér-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB) for the localization error.
The algorithm aims to minimize the total transmitted power under the constraint of a certain localization accuracy.
Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly improves the localization performance compared to existing methods.
The paper also discusses the trade-off between the localization accuracy and the resource consumption, providing valuable insights for the design of efficient MIMO radar systems.

This paper introduces Pick-and-Learn, a novel method for automatic quality evaluation of noisy-labeled image segmentation.
The proposed method aims to address the challenges associated with the quality assessment of noisy labels, which is a critical issue in supervised learning.
Pick-and-Learn leverages a self-training strategy to select high-quality labels from noisy ones, and subsequently uses these labels to train the segmentation model.
The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets.
The results demonstrate that Pick-and-Learn significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of both segmentation accuracy and robustness to label noise.
This research provides a new perspective on the problem of noisy labels in image segmentation and offers a practical solution for improving the performance of segmentation models trained with noisy labels.

This paper presents a novel approach to specifying and orchestrating service contracts using automata.
The study explores the use of automata theory in the context of service-oriented computing, focusing on the formal specification and orchestration of service contracts.
The paper introduces a formal model for service contracts, based on labelled transition systems, and proposes an automata-based algorithm for their orchestration.
The proposed approach provides a rigorous foundation for the design and implementation of service contracts, enabling the automatic verification of their properties and the generation of correct-by-construction orchestrations.
The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through a series of case studies, showing its applicability to real-world scenarios.
The results indicate that automata-based specification and orchestration of service contracts can significantly improve the reliability and efficiency of service-oriented systems.

This paper presents a novel approach to anomaly detection in time series of graphs using locality statistics.
The study introduces a new method that leverages the local structure of graphs to identify anomalous behavior over time.
The proposed technique is based on the premise that anomalies are local events that significantly deviate from the norm, and thus, can be effectively detected by examining the local statistics of a graph.
The paper provides a comprehensive evaluation of the proposed method on various synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in accurately detecting anomalies.
The results also highlight the method's robustness against noise and its scalability to large-scale graphs.
This research contributes to the growing body of literature on graph-based anomaly detection, offering a new perspective that emphasizes the importance of locality in identifying unusual patterns.

TBAC combines the strengths of active contour models and template matching techniques to achieve robust and accurate segmentation of objects in images.
The proposed method involves the use of a template to guide the evolution of the active contour, enabling it to effectively handle variations in object appearance and shape.
The paper provides a detailed description of the TBAC algorithm, along with its mathematical formulation.
Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of TBAC in comparison to existing image segmentation methods, particularly in terms of accuracy and robustness to noise and shape variations.
The paper also discusses potential applications of TBAC in various fields such as medical imaging, computer vision, and remote sensing.

This paper presents a novel Quality-Aware Memory Network (QAMN) for interactive volumetric image segmentation.
The proposed model aims to improve the quality of segmentation by leveraging a memory module that stores high-quality segmentation examples.
The QAMN model is designed to learn from the stored examples and adaptively update its segmentation strategy based on the quality of the current segmentation.
The paper also introduces a quality-aware loss function to guide the learning process.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed QAMN model outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation quality and interaction efficiency.
The proposed model has potential applications in medical imaging, where accurate and efficient segmentation of volumetric images is crucial.

This paper presents a comprehensive benchmark for food image segmentation, a critical task in understanding food intake and dietary habits.
We introduce a large-scale dataset, comprising diverse food images collected from various sources, annotated with pixel-level segmentation masks.
The dataset covers a wide range of food categories, capturing the complexity and variability of real-world food items.
We also propose a novel evaluation metric that considers both segmentation accuracy and the importance of different food regions.
Furthermore, we provide baseline results using state-of-the-art segmentation models, highlighting the challenges of food image segmentation.
This benchmark aims to facilitate future research in food image analysis and its applications in health and dietary studies.

This paper introduces NeurReg, a novel neural network-based approach for image registration and its application to image segmentation.
The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning to align images, overcoming the limitations of traditional registration techniques.
NeurReg is designed to be robust, efficient, and capable of handling large deformations, making it suitable for a wide range of applications.
We demonstrate the effectiveness of NeurReg through extensive experiments on various datasets, showing significant improvements over existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
Furthermore, we explore the application of NeurReg in image segmentation tasks, where it exhibits superior performance by providing more accurate and detailed segmentations.
This work not only presents a new perspective on image registration but also opens up new possibilities for its application in image segmentation.

This paper introduces the Medical Transformer, a novel approach to medical image segmentation that utilizes gated axial-attention.
The proposed model addresses the limitations of traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) by leveraging the transformer architecture, which has shown superior performance in various domains.
The Medical Transformer is designed to capture long-range dependencies and intricate structures in medical images, which are crucial for accurate segmentation.
The gated axial-attention mechanism further enhances the model's ability to focus on relevant features while ignoring irrelevant ones.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the Medical Transformer, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency.
This research opens up new possibilities for the application of transformer models in medical image analysis.

This paper provides a comprehensive survey on automatic image co-segmentation, a rapidly evolving field in computer vision.
Image co-segmentation aims to segment common objects from a group of related images automatically.
This survey discusses the fundamental theories, methodologies, and algorithms of image co-segmentation, including traditional and deep learning-based methods.
It also presents a comparative analysis of various techniques, highlighting their strengths, weaknesses, and applicability.
Furthermore, it discusses the challenges and potential future directions in this field.
This survey serves as a valuable reference for researchers and practitioners interested in the automatic image co-segmentation domain.

This paper presents a novel approach to segment skin lesions using machine learning algorithms trained on noisy annotations.

To overcome this, we propose a robust learning model that can effectively learn from imperfectly annotated data.
