This paper introduces the Inhomogeneity Estimation by Orthogonal Primary Functions (IEOPF), a novel active contour model for image segmentation.
The model is designed to handle images with inhomogeneities, a common challenge in image processing.
The IEOPF model employs orthogonal primary functions to estimate the inhomogeneity, which is then incorporated into the energy functional of the active contour model.
The proposed model is tested on synthetic and real images, demonstrating its effectiveness in segmenting images with inhomogeneities.
The results show that the IEOPF model outperforms existing models in terms of accuracy and robustness.
This research contributes to the field of image processing by providing a new approach to handle inhomogeneities in image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach to detecting missing method calls in object-oriented programming by considering them as violations of the majority rule.
The majority rule, in this context, refers to the common practice of calling certain methods together in a specific sequence.
The proposed technique uses static analysis to identify these common patterns and detect deviations.
The paper discusses the implementation of this approach and evaluates its effectiveness using several open-source software systems.
The results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively identify missing method calls, thereby improving code quality and reducing debugging time.
The paper also highlights potential areas for further research and improvement.

This paper presents a novel approach to citrus segmentation by integrating supervised and unsupervised learning techniques.
The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of citrus segmentation, a critical task in automated citrus harvesting and grading systems.
The proposed method first employs unsupervised learning to cluster the citrus pixels based on color and texture features.
Then, supervised learning is used to classify the clustered pixels into citrus and non-citrus categories.
Experimental results on various citrus datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
This research contributes to the advancement of automatic citrus harvesting and grading systems, potentially leading to significant improvements in productivity and cost-effectiveness.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the accuracy of Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) segmentation with hidden Potts and Markov mesh prior models.
The study employs three different algorithms: Path Constrained Viterbi Training (PCVT), Iterated Conditional Modes (ICM), and Graph Cut based algorithms.
The paper provides a detailed comparison of these algorithms in terms of their performance and accuracy in MAP segmentation.
The results indicate that the accuracy of MAP segmentation significantly depends on the choice of the algorithm.
The paper also discusses the strengths and weaknesses of each algorithm, providing valuable insights for researchers and practitioners in the field of image processing and computer vision.
The findings of this study can guide the selection of appropriate algorithms for MAP segmentation tasks in various applications.

This paper presents the third part of a study on modelling galaxy spectra in the presence of interstellar dust.
The focus is on extending the models developed for nearby galaxies to the distant Universe.
The paper discusses the challenges and complexities of this extension, including the need to account for variations in dust properties and the effects of cosmic evolution.
The models are tested against observational data from both nearby and distant galaxies, demonstrating their applicability across a wide range of redshifts.
The results provide new insights into the role of dust in shaping galaxy spectra and the evolution of galaxies over cosmic time.
The models also offer a valuable tool for interpreting future observations of distant galaxies.

This paper presents a novel approach to ultra-high resolution image segmentation by leveraging locality-aware contextual correlation.
The study proposes a new model that integrates both global and local contexts to enhance the accuracy of image segmentation.
The model is designed to handle ultra-high resolution images, which are often challenging due to their large size and complex details.
The proposed method is based on the concept of locality-awareness, which allows the model to focus on specific regions of the image, thereby improving the efficiency and effectiveness of the segmentation process.
The paper also introduces a new correlation mechanism that captures the contextual relationships within and between local regions.
Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency, making it a promising solution for ultra-high resolution image segmentation.

This paper introduces Sem-GAN, a novel approach to image-to-image translation that ensures semantic consistency between the input and output images.
Sem-GAN leverages the power of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and incorporates a semantic consistency loss function to maintain the semantic information during the translation process.
The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets and compared with state-of-the-art methods.
The results demonstrate that Sem-GAN significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of both visual quality and semantic consistency.
Furthermore, the proposed method is robust to changes in the input images and can handle a wide range of translation tasks.
This paper provides a new perspective on image-to-image translation and opens up new possibilities for future research in this area.

This paper presents a novel approach to video semantic segmentation using Clockwork Convnets.
The proposed method leverages the temporal redundancy present in videos to reduce the computational cost of segmentation without compromising the quality of results.
The Clockwork Convnets operate by selectively updating certain parts of the network at different rates based on the complexity and variability of the video content.
This approach allows for efficient processing of video data, making it suitable for real-time applications.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves comparable or superior performance to existing methods while significantly reducing computational requirements.
This work contributes to the field of computer vision by providing a more efficient method for video semantic segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach to 3D medical image segmentation using an attention-guided active learning strategy.
The proposed method aims to reduce the need for extensive manual annotations, a common challenge in medical image analysis.
The strategy employs a sparse annotation technique, which leverages the attention mechanism to identify critical regions in the images.
Active learning is then used to iteratively train the segmentation model, improving its performance with each iteration.
Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly reduces the annotation effort while maintaining high segmentation accuracy.
This work has potential implications for improving efficiency in medical image analysis and could be applied to various medical imaging modalities.

The proposed method combines object localization and boundary preservation techniques to improve the accuracy and efficiency of object segmentation.
The study introduces a new algorithm that uses personal fixations data to guide the segmentation process, effectively identifying and isolating objects of interest in complex scenes.
The algorithm also incorporates boundary preservation techniques to maintain the integrity of object shapes.
Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
This research has significant implications for various applications, including image editing, computer vision, and human-computer interaction.

This paper presents a comprehensive comparative study of various statistical skin detection algorithms applied to sub-continental human images.
The study aims to evaluate the performance and accuracy of these algorithms in detecting and segmenting skin regions in images from diverse ethnic backgrounds, specifically focusing on sub-continental populations.
The algorithms under study include Gaussian Mixture Models, Bayesian Classifier, Support Vector Machines, and Artificial Neural Networks.
The evaluation is based on several metrics such as precision, recall, F1-score, and overall accuracy.
The results provide valuable insights into the strengths and weaknesses of each algorithm, offering guidance for future research and development in skin detection technology.
The study also highlights the need for more inclusive and diverse datasets in the field of skin detection.

This paper presents a novel approach for Out-of-Distribution (OOD) detection in multi-label datasets using the latent space of $β$-Variational Autoencoder ($β$-VAE).
The study focuses on the challenge of identifying OOD samples in multi-label datasets, which is a critical task in machine learning and data analysis.
The proposed method leverages the properties of $β$-VAE, a type of generative model, to map the data into a lower-dimensional latent space.
This mapping is then used to distinguish between in-distribution and OOD samples.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in detecting OOD samples, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods.
The paper also discusses potential applications and future directions for this research.

It also demonstrates that countries with higher economic complexity have more stable economies and are better equipped to withstand economic shocks.
The paper further explores the implications of economic complexity for economic policy and development strategies.
The findings suggest that promoting economic complexity can be a viable strategy for sustainable economic development and reducing income inequality.

The results demonstrate that our approach significantly improves the performance of image segmentation tasks, reducing errors and increasing speed.
This research opens up new possibilities for the application of reinforced active learning in image analysis and computer vision.

While QKD has been the primary focus of quantum cryptography research, this paper argues that there are other promising applications that deserve attention.
These include Quantum Money, Quantum Digital Signatures, and Quantum Secret Sharing.
The paper provides an overview of these applications, discussing their potential benefits and challenges.
It also highlights the need for further research in these areas to fully realize the potential of quantum cryptography.
The paper concludes by emphasizing the importance of exploring quantum cryptography beyond QKD, as it could lead to more secure and efficient cryptographic systems.

This paper presents a novel approach to hyperspectral unmixing using collaborative sparse regression with spatially correlated supports.
Hyperspectral unmixing is a critical task in remote sensing, aiming to identify and quantify the constituent materials of each pixel in a hyperspectral image.
Traditional methods often fail to consider the spatial correlation of the materials, leading to suboptimal results.
To address this issue, we propose a collaborative sparse regression model that incorporates spatial correlation into the unmixing process.
The model leverages the spatial correlation of the materials' distribution to enhance the unmixing performance.
Experimental results on both synthetic and real hyperspectral data demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method in improving the accuracy of hyperspectral unmixing.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using an autoregressive unsupervised learning model.
The proposed method leverages the inherent spatial dependencies in images to generate accurate and coherent segmentations without the need for manual annotation.
The model is trained on a large dataset of diverse images, allowing it to generalize well to unseen data.
Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing unsupervised segmentation methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
Furthermore, the autoregressive nature of the model allows for the generation of multiple plausible segmentations for a given image, providing a measure of uncertainty in the segmentation process.
This work has potential applications in a variety of fields, including computer vision, medical imaging, and remote sensing.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the automatic segmentation of teeth in X-ray images, a critical task in dental diagnostics and treatment planning.
We review the current trends and methodologies in this field, highlighting the challenges and limitations of existing approaches.
To facilitate future research, we introduce a novel dataset of annotated dental X-ray images.
We also provide a benchmarking of various state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms on this dataset, offering insights into their performance and applicability in real-world scenarios.
Finally, we discuss potential future directions in this area, emphasizing the need for more robust and accurate segmentation techniques.
This work aims to stimulate further research and development in automatic teeth segmentation, ultimately contributing to improved dental healthcare.

This paper presents a novel self-learning Artificial Intelligence (AI) framework for skin lesion image segmentation and classification.
The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of skin cancer diagnosis by automating the process of identifying and classifying skin lesions.
The proposed framework utilizes deep learning algorithms for image segmentation, feature extraction, and classification.
The results demonstrate that the self-learning AI framework outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy, precision, and recall.
The framework also exhibits robustness against variations in image quality and lesion characteristics.
This research contributes to the field of medical imaging and AI, offering potential for early and accurate skin cancer diagnosis, thereby improving patient outcomes.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the automated design of deep learning methods for biomedical image segmentation.
The research focuses on the development and evaluation of novel algorithms that can automatically generate effective deep learning models, eliminating the need for manual design and tuning.
The proposed methods are based on reinforcement learning and genetic algorithms, which are used to search the vast space of possible model architectures.
The performance of these automated methods is evaluated on several biomedical image segmentation tasks, including the segmentation of brain tumors, lung nodules, and cells in microscopy images.
The results demonstrate that the automatically designed models can achieve comparable or even superior performance to manually designed models, while significantly reducing the time and effort required for model design.
This study suggests that automated design of deep learning methods holds great potential for improving the efficiency and effectiveness of biomedical image analysis.

This paper presents a novel unsupervised adaptation method for multi-modal cardiac image segmentation using point-clouds and entropy minimisation.
The proposed method, named Adapt Everywhere, addresses the challenge of domain shift in medical imaging, which often leads to a significant drop in the performance of segmentation models.
The method leverages the inherent structure of point-clouds to adapt the model to new domains without requiring any labelled data.
Furthermore, it employs entropy minimisation to ensure the consistency of predictions across different modalities.
Extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of Adapt Everywhere, outperforming state-of-the-art unsupervised domain adaptation methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to domain shift.
The results suggest that the proposed method can be a promising tool for improving the performance of cardiac image segmentation in clinical practice.

This paper presents a novel linear framework for region-based image segmentation and inpainting that incorporates curvature penalization.
The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image processing tasks by considering the curvature information of the image regions.
The framework is based on a variational approach and uses a level set method for image segmentation and a partial differential equation for image inpainting.
The curvature penalization term is introduced to preserve the smoothness and continuity of the image structures.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both segmentation and inpainting quality, particularly in dealing with images containing complex structures and textures.
The linear nature of the framework also ensures computational efficiency, making it suitable for real-time applications.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the modeling and control of an active constrained layer (ACL) beam actuated by two voltage sources, considering both scenarios with and without magnetic effects.
The ACL beam is a smart structure that has been widely used in vibration control applications.
The mathematical model of the ACL beam is derived using Hamilton's principle and the assumed mode method.
The influence of magnetic effects on the beam's dynamic behavior is also investigated.
Two control strategies, namely, the optimal control and the sliding mode control, are designed to suppress the vibration of the ACL beam.
Numerical simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed models and control strategies.

This paper presents a novel approach to video semantic segmentation, a critical task in computer vision, by integrating labels propagation and refinement.
The proposed method aims to improve efficiency and accuracy by leveraging temporal coherence in videos.
The algorithm first propagates labels from keyframes to non-keyframes, then refines the segmentation results using a lightweight network.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in terms of both speed and accuracy.
Furthermore, the proposed method is computationally efficient, making it suitable for real-time applications.
This research contributes to the advancement of video semantic segmentation techniques and has potential implications for various applications such as autonomous driving, video surveillance, and human-computer interaction.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using Cellular Automata (CA).
Image segmentation is a crucial process in image analysis and computer vision, which partitions an image into multiple segments to simplify and/or change the representation into something more meaningful and easier to analyze.
The proposed method leverages the dynamic behavior of CA, a discrete computational model, to perform image segmentation.
The paper discusses the principles of CA, the design of the proposed CA-based image segmentation method, and its implementation.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional image segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
The paper also explores potential applications of the CA-based image segmentation in various fields such as medical imaging, remote sensing, and object recognition.

The study begins with a comprehensive overview of the algorithm's historical development and its fundamental principles.
It then explores the algorithm's role in determining the greatest common divisor (GCD) of two integers, highlighting its efficiency and computational simplicity.
The paper further discusses the algorithm's extension to the Euclidean domain and its implications for the broader field of number theory.
The study also presents various proofs and mathematical models to elucidate the algorithm's workings and its connection to the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic.
The paper concludes with a discussion on the algorithm's modern applications, including cryptography and coding theory.

This paper presents a novel approach for unsupervised segmentation of 3D medical images using clustering and deep representation learning.
The proposed method does not require any prior knowledge or training data, making it highly applicable in scenarios where annotated data is scarce or unavailable.
The method first extracts deep features from the 3D medical images using a pre-trained 3D convolutional neural network.
Then, a clustering algorithm is applied to group similar features together, forming distinct segments.
Experimental results on various types of medical images, including MRI and CT scans, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately segmenting different anatomical structures.
The proposed method outperforms several state-of-the-art unsupervised segmentation methods, showing its potential for practical applications in medical image analysis.

This paper presents a novel Generalized Asymmetric Dual-front Model (GADM) for active contours and image segmentation.
The proposed model is designed to handle complex segmentation tasks, including those with weak boundaries, noise, and intensity inhomogeneity.
The GADM is based on a dual-front strategy, which allows it to capture both the interior and exterior boundaries of objects.
The model also incorporates an asymmetric speed function to handle intensity inhomogeneity and a regularization term to suppress noise.
Experimental results on synthetic and real images demonstrate the superior performance of the GADM in terms of accuracy, robustness, and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art methods.
The GADM has potential applications in various fields, including medical imaging, computer vision, and pattern recognition.

This paper presents a novel active set algorithm for estimating parameters in generalized linear models (GLMs) with ordered predictors.
The algorithm is designed to handle the unique challenges posed by ordered predictors, such as the need for monotonicity constraints.
The proposed method is based on a quadratic approximation of the log-likelihood function, which allows for efficient computation and robust performance.
The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of simulation studies and real data applications.
The results show that the proposed method provides accurate parameter estimates and outperforms existing methods in terms of computational efficiency and stability.
This research contributes to the field of statistical modeling by offering a new tool for handling GLMs with ordered predictors.

This paper presents an innovative approach to automatic color image segmentation using a square elemental region-based seeded region growing and merging method.
The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional image segmentation techniques by incorporating a square elemental region-based approach, which enhances the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process.
The method begins with an initial segmentation into square elemental regions, followed by a seeded region growing process, and finally a merging process to combine similar regions.
The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using various color images, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving high-quality segmentation results.
The method is robust, computationally efficient, and capable of handling images with complex structures and varying textures.
This research contributes to the field of image processing by providing a novel method for automatic color image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach to image co-segmentation using deep metric learning.
Image co-segmentation, the task of segmenting common objects from a set of images, is a challenging problem in computer vision.
Traditional methods often fail to capture the complex variations in object appearance.
To address this, we propose a deep metric learning-based method that learns a similarity metric between image regions, enabling the model to identify common objects more accurately.
Our method leverages a deep convolutional neural network to extract robust features and a metric learning layer to learn the similarity.
Extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and robustness.

This paper presents a novel Meta Segmentation Network (MSN) for ultra-resolution medical images.
The proposed MSN addresses the challenges of high computational cost and memory consumption associated with processing ultra-resolution images.
It employs a meta-learning approach that adapts to new tasks with minimal training data, making it suitable for medical applications where annotated data is scarce.
The MSN also incorporates a multi-scale feature fusion module to capture both local and global context information, enhancing the segmentation performance.
Extensive experiments on various medical imaging datasets demonstrate that the MSN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and robustness.
The proposed network has potential applications in various medical imaging tasks, including disease diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper presents a novel approach to solving the crystallographic phase problem using dynamical scattering in electron diffraction.
The phase problem, a fundamental challenge in crystallography, involves determining the phase of a wave when only its intensity can be measured.
Our method leverages the unique properties of dynamical scattering in electron diffraction to extract phase information.
We provide a comprehensive theoretical framework for this approach, supported by experimental data from various crystal structures.
The results demonstrate that our method can accurately retrieve phase information, offering a promising solution to the phase problem.
This could significantly enhance the accuracy and efficiency of crystal structure determination, with potential applications in materials science, chemistry, and biology.

This paper presents a novel approach to multi-label segmentation of medical images with lesions using dynamic multiscale tree learning and ensemble strong classifiers.
The proposed method addresses the challenges of accurately identifying and classifying multiple types of lesions in medical images, which is crucial for effective diagnosis and treatment planning.
The dynamic multiscale tree learning algorithm is designed to adaptively learn and adjust to the complexity and diversity of the lesions.
The ensemble strong classifiers further enhance the segmentation performance by integrating the decisions of multiple weak classifiers.
Experimental results on various types of medical images demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency compared to existing methods.
This research contributes to the advancement of medical image analysis and has potential applications in computer-aided diagnosis and personalized medicine.

The paper first introduces the concept of differential geometry and its application in image processing.
It then details the proposed segmentation method, which involves extracting differential geometric features from multimodal MRI brain images and using these features to segment the images.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
This research has significant implications for the development of more effective diagnostic tools in neurology.

The proposed method employs exclusive independent probability estimation to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process.
The DenseNets architecture is utilized to extract and fuse high-level features from different scales, which significantly improves the discriminative capability of the model.
The exclusive independent probability estimation further refines the segmentation results by considering the exclusive relationship among different classes.
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
This study provides a promising tool for the automatic and accurate segmentation of IsoIntense Infant Brain MRI, which is crucial for the early diagnosis and treatment of various neurological disorders.

This paper presents a comprehensive quantitative test of general theories of the intrinsic laser linewidth.
The study involves a detailed examination of the Schawlow-Townes linewidth formula, which has been a cornerstone in the understanding of laser linewidths.
The paper also explores the Henry alpha factor, which is crucial in determining the linewidth enhancement factor.
The experimental results obtained from various types of lasers, including semiconductor and fiber lasers, are compared with theoretical predictions.
The findings reveal a significant discrepancy between the experimental results and the predictions of the Schawlow-Townes formula, suggesting the need for a more comprehensive theory.
The paper concludes with a discussion on the implications of these findings for future research in laser technology and quantum optics.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the modeling and semigroup formulation of charge or current-controlled active constrained layer (ACL) beams.
The research focuses on three assumptions: electrostatic, quasi-static, and fully-dynamic.
The paper first introduces the mathematical modeling of ACL beams, followed by the development of a semigroup formulation.
The electrostatic assumption simplifies the model by neglecting the time variation of electric fields, while the quasi-static assumption considers slow time variations.
The fully-dynamic assumption, on the other hand, takes into account all time variations.
The results of this study provide a deeper understanding of the behavior of ACL beams under different assumptions and contribute to the optimization of their control and performance.

This academic paper presents a novel approach to gaze estimation, a critical aspect of human-computer interaction.
Traditionally, gaze estimation has been focused on the eye region, but this paper proposes a full-face appearance-based method.
The study demonstrates that the entire face contributes to gaze direction and that utilizing full-face information significantly improves gaze estimation accuracy.
The paper also introduces a new large-scale dataset for gaze estimation, collected under diverse conditions.
The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing eye-based methods, particularly in real-world, unconstrained environments.
This research has significant implications for the development of more natural and efficient human-computer interaction systems.

Moldable tasks are computational tasks that can be executed on different numbers of processors.
The paper introduces novel algorithms that optimize the scheduling of these tasks, aiming to minimize the overall completion time.
The algorithms are based on advanced mathematical models and are designed to be adaptable to various computing environments.
The paper also includes a comparative analysis of the proposed algorithms with existing ones, demonstrating their superior efficiency and adaptability.
The results of this study have significant implications for high-performance computing, cloud computing, and other areas where efficient task scheduling is critical.

This paper presents a novel approach to semantic segmentation using RGBD sensing, with a focus on incremental class discovery.
Traditional methods of semantic segmentation are limited by their inability to adapt to new classes after training.
Our proposed method overcomes this limitation by incorporating an incremental learning framework that allows the model to learn new classes without forgetting the previously learned ones.
We introduce a new RGBD dataset for semantic segmentation, which includes a diverse set of classes.
Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy and adaptability.
This research opens up new possibilities for real-world applications of semantic segmentation, particularly in dynamic environments where the set of object classes can change over time.

This paper investigates the collective spontaneous emission from a system of quantum dots.
Quantum dots, nanoscale semiconductor particles, exhibit unique optical and electronic properties due to their quantum confinement, making them ideal for studying quantum phenomena.
We explore the collective behavior of these quantum dots under specific conditions, focusing on their spontaneous emission - a fundamental quantum process where an excited quantum system relaxes to its ground state by emitting a photon.
Our study reveals that the collective spontaneous emission can be significantly enhanced compared to the emission from individual quantum dots.
This finding has potential implications for the development of quantum information technologies, including quantum computing and quantum communication.
The paper also discusses the theoretical framework, experimental setup, and potential applications of our findings.

This paper presents a novel approach to volumetric medical image segmentation using Positional Contrastive Learning (PCL).
The proposed method leverages the inherent spatial information in volumetric images to enhance the segmentation performance.
PCL is designed to learn discriminative features by contrasting positive and negative samples based on their spatial positions.
The effectiveness of PCL is evaluated on several benchmark datasets of different medical imaging modalities, including CT and MRI scans.
Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency.
This study suggests that PCL can be a promising tool for improving the quality of medical image analysis, which is crucial for accurate disease diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation, termed Hierarchical Piecewise-Constant Super-regions (HPCS).
The HPCS method aims to overcome the limitations of existing segmentation techniques by providing a more accurate and detailed representation of an image.
The proposed method works by dividing an image into a hierarchy of super-regions, each of which is characterized by a piecewise-constant intensity profile.
The hierarchical nature of the method allows for a flexible and adaptive representation of the image, capturing both fine and coarse details.
Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the HPCS method in terms of both segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed method has potential applications in various fields, including computer vision, image processing, and medical imaging.

Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the HPCS method in terms of both segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
The proposed method has potential applications in various fields, including computer vision, image processing, and medical imaging.

This paper introduces w-Net, a novel dual supervised medical image segmentation model that incorporates multi-dimensional attention and cascade multi-scale convolution.
The model aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation, a critical task in medical image analysis.
The proposed w-Net model employs a dual supervision mechanism to guide the learning process, enhancing the model's ability to capture intricate details and complex structures in medical images.
Furthermore, the model integrates a multi-dimensional attention mechanism to focus on significant features and suppress irrelevant ones.
It also utilizes a cascade multi-scale convolution to extract features at different scales effectively.
Experimental results on various medical image datasets demonstrate that the proposed w-Net model outperforms existing state-of-the-art segmentation models in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency.

This paper presents a novel approach to unssupervised image segmentation using global and local criteria optimization based on Bayesian Networks.
The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional image segmentation techniques, which often fail to accurately segment complex images due to the lack of prior knowledge.
Our approach integrates global and local criteria into a unified Bayesian framework, allowing for the optimization of both criteria simultaneously.
The global criterion ensures the overall coherence of the segmentation, while the local criterion preserves the details of the image.
Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in producing high-quality segmentation results, outperforming several state-of-the-art techniques.
This research opens up new possibilities for improving image segmentation in various applications, including computer vision, medical imaging, and remote sensing.

This paper presents a novel, efficient semidefinite programming (SDP) approach to solving binary quadratic problems (BQP).
BQP, a NP-hard problem, has wide applications in various fields such as machine learning, operations research, and computer vision.
Traditional methods often suffer from high computational complexity or poor solution quality.
Our proposed method leverages the power of SDP relaxation to provide a fast and high-quality solution to BQP.
We demonstrate the superiority of our approach through extensive computational experiments on various benchmark instances.
The results show that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of both solution quality and computational efficiency.

This paper investigates the well-posedness and robust preconditioners for discretized fluid-structure interaction (FSI) systems.
FSI systems are complex and challenging to solve due to the coupling of fluid and solid domains.
The paper first establishes the well-posedness of the discretized FSI system under certain conditions.
It then proposes robust preconditioners to improve the efficiency and stability of the iterative solution process.
Numerical experiments are conducted to validate the theoretical results and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed preconditioners.
The findings of this study provide valuable insights into the numerical solution of FSI problems and have potential applications in various fields such as engineering, physics, and biology.

We explore various DL architectures, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), and their variants.
The paper also discusses the implementation of these architectures, their performance comparison, and the challenges encountered.
The results demonstrate that DL architectures significantly enhance the segmentation accuracy compared to traditional methods, thereby providing a promising tool for advanced biomedical research.
The paper concludes with future directions for optimizing DL-based nuclear image segmentation.

This paper investigates the phenomenon of overfitting in neural networks, specifically in the context of image segmentation tasks under class imbalance conditions.
Overfitting, a common issue in machine learning, occurs when a model learns the training data too well, negatively impacting its performance on unseen data.
Class imbalance, another prevalent problem, arises when the number of instances of different classes in a dataset is unequal.
We conduct a series of experiments using various neural network architectures and image datasets to understand how class imbalance influences overfitting.
Our findings suggest that class imbalance exacerbates overfitting in image segmentation tasks, and we propose several strategies to mitigate this issue.
This research contributes to the broader understanding of overfitting in neural networks and provides practical insights for improving model performance in image segmentation tasks.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using nonparametric clustering techniques.
The study aims to overcome the limitations of traditional parametric methods, which often require a priori knowledge of the number of clusters and their distribution.
The proposed method employs a nonparametric clustering algorithm that does not require any assumptions about the data distribution and can automatically determine the number of clusters.
The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through extensive experiments on various image datasets.
The results show that the nonparametric clustering approach provides superior performance in terms of both segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.
This research opens up new possibilities for image segmentation, particularly in applications where the number of segments is unknown or varies across images.

This paper introduces CRNet (Cross-Reference Networks), a novel approach for few-shot segmentation.
The primary objective of CRNet is to address the challenge of segmenting objects in images with limited annotated examples.
CRNet leverages cross-referencing between a support set and a query image to generate more robust and discriminative features.
It also introduces a new cross-reference mechanism that enhances the interaction between the support and query features, thereby improving the segmentation performance.
Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that CRNet significantly outperforms existing few-shot segmentation methods, establishing a new state-of-the-art in the field.
The paper also provides comprehensive ablation studies to validate the effectiveness of the proposed cross-reference mechanism.

This paper presents a novel approach to sketch colorization using adversarial segmentation loss.
The study proposes a new framework that leverages the strengths of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and segmentation networks to improve the colorization of sketches.
The proposed method aims to address the common issues in sketch colorization such as color bleeding and lack of detail.
The adversarial segmentation loss function encourages the model to generate colorized sketches that are not only visually appealing but also semantically meaningful.
Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both visual quality and quantitative evaluations.
This research opens up new possibilities for the application of GANs in sketch colorization and other related fields.

The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of motion capture data analysis by introducing a fine-grained segmentation method.
The proposed DTFCN model is designed to capture long-range dependencies in the temporal domain, which is crucial for understanding complex human motions.
The model is evaluated on several benchmark datasets and compared with existing methods.
The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art techniques in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
This research opens up new possibilities for the application of deep learning techniques in motion capture data analysis and related fields.

This paper explores a variant of the classic hat game, known as Ebert's asymmetric three person three color Hat Game.
The game involves three players, each wearing a hat of one of three colors, and the objective is to correctly guess the color of one's own hat.
The twist in this version is the asymmetric information each player has about the others' hats.
The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the game, including its mathematical model, strategies for optimal play, and implications for game theory.
The study reveals that the game's complexity increases significantly with the introduction of asymmetry, leading to intriguing strategic possibilities.
The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of decision-making processes under uncertainty and asymmetric information.

This paper presents a novel multi-layer approach to superpixel-based higher-order Conditional Random Field (CRF) for semantic image segmentation.
The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation by leveraging the advantages of superpixels and higher-order CRFs.
The multi-layer approach involves the generation of superpixels at different scales, which are then integrated into a higher-order CRF framework.
The framework is designed to capture both local and global contextual information, thereby enhancing the segmentation performance.
Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving superior segmentation accuracy compared to existing methods.
The paper also discusses potential applications of this approach in various fields such as computer vision, image processing, and machine learning.

The results demonstrate that the use of dependent types can significantly improve the performance of solutions to sequential decision problems.

This paper presents a novel hierarchical self-supervised learning approach for medical image segmentation, leveraging multi-domain data aggregation.
The study aims to address the challenges of limited annotated data and high annotation costs in medical imaging.
The proposed method involves a hierarchical learning structure that progressively learns from easy to complex tasks, improving the model's generalization ability.
It also incorporates multi-domain data aggregation to enhance the diversity of the training data, thereby improving the robustness of the model.
Experimental results on various medical imaging datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, outperforming several state-of-the-art techniques in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency.
This research contributes to the advancement of self-supervised learning techniques in the field of medical image analysis, with potential applications in disease diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper presents an in-depth study on recursive quantum repeater networks.
Quantum repeaters are pivotal in long-distance quantum communication, enhancing the transmission fidelity and extending the communication distance.
This study introduces a novel recursive structure for quantum repeater networks, which significantly improves the efficiency and scalability of quantum communication systems.
The recursive design allows for a more flexible and robust network, capable of adapting to various communication demands and error rates.
Theoretical analysis and simulations demonstrate the superiority of the proposed recursive network over traditional linear repeater chains in terms of communication rate and distance.
This research opens up new avenues for the design and implementation of large-scale quantum networks.

The proposed method significantly improves the speed and accuracy of edge detection in digital images.
The structured forests algorithm is trained on a large dataset of manually annotated images, enabling it to learn and generalize the characteristics of edges.
The algorithm is then applied to new images, rapidly identifying edges with a high degree of precision.
Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing edge detection techniques in terms of both speed and accuracy.
This research has potential applications in a wide range of fields, including computer vision, image processing, and artificial intelligence.

This paper presents a novel model for the heating of the Solar North Polar Coronal Hole (SNPCH).
The model is based on the analysis of high-resolution solar observations and incorporates the latest advancements in solar physics.
The proposed model suggests a unique heating mechanism that is driven by the magnetic reconnection of the coronal magnetic field lines.
The model successfully reproduces the observed temperature and density profiles of the SNPCH, providing a better understanding of the physical processes occurring in this region.
The results have significant implications for solar wind acceleration and space weather prediction.
The model also offers new insights into the fundamental processes of solar coronal heating, which remains one of the most challenging problems in astrophysics.

This paper presents a novel approach to abdominal multi-organ segmentation using voxel-level Siamese representation learning.
The study aims to address the challenges of inter-subject and intra-subject variability in abdominal organ segmentation.
The proposed method leverages a Siamese network to learn a voxel-level representation that captures the anatomical context of each voxel, thereby improving the segmentation performance.
The network is trained using a novel loss function that encourages the learning of similar representations for voxels belonging to the same organ and different representations for voxels from different organs.
Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the accuracy and consistency of abdominal multi-organ segmentation.
The study contributes to the field of medical image analysis by providing a new perspective on representation learning for organ segmentation tasks.

This paper presents a novel image segmentation enhancement technique that combines active contour and topological alignments.
Image segmentation is a crucial process in various fields such as medical imaging, computer vision, and pattern recognition.
However, traditional methods often struggle with issues such as noise interference and boundary leakage.
To address these challenges, we propose an innovative technique that integrates active contour models, known for their robustness against noise, with topological alignments, which provide accurate boundary detection.
Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and noise resistance.
This research opens new avenues for improving image segmentation quality and has potential applications in numerous domains.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on improving learning effectiveness for object detection and classification in cluttered backgrounds.
The research focuses on developing advanced machine learning algorithms that can accurately identify and classify objects in complex and cluttered environments.
The proposed methods aim to overcome the challenges of occlusion, varying object scales, and high intra-class variability.
The paper introduces a novel approach that combines deep learning techniques with traditional image processing methods to enhance the performance of object detection and classification systems.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves the accuracy and robustness of object detection and classification in cluttered backgrounds compared to existing methods.
This research has potential applications in various fields, including autonomous driving, surveillance, and robotics.

This paper investigates the reduction of ion heating during magnetic reconnection by large-scale effective potentials.
Magnetic reconnection, a fundamental process in plasma physics, often leads to significant ion heating.
However, the mechanisms behind this phenomenon remain unclear.
This study presents a novel approach to understanding and mitigating ion heating during magnetic reconnection.
By employing large-scale effective potentials, we demonstrate a significant reduction in ion heating.
Our findings provide valuable insights into the control of ion heating in magnetic reconnection, with potential applications in fusion energy research and space physics.

A multilayer surface detector for ultracold neutrons (UCNs) is described.
The
top $^{10}$B layer is exposed to the vacuum chamber and directly captures UCNs.

The ZnS:
Ag layer beneath the $^{10}$B layer is a few microns thick, which is
sufficient to detect the charged particles from the $^{10}$B(n,$\alpha$)$^7$Li
neutron-capture reaction, while thin enough so that ample light due to $\alpha$
and $^7$Li escapes for detection by photomultiplier tubes.
One-hundred-nm thick
$^{10}$B layer gives high UCN detection efficiency, as determined by the mean
UCN kinetic energy, detector materials and others.
Low background, including
negligible sensitivity to ambient neutrons, has also been verified through
pulse-shape analysis and comparisons with other existing $^3$He and $^{10}$B
detectors.

Pixelwise segmentation of the left ventricular (LV) myocardium and the four
cardiac chambers in 2-D steady state free precession (SSFP) cine sequences is
an essential preprocessing step for a wide range of analyses.
Variability in
contrast, appearance, orientation, and placement of the heart between patients,
clinical views, scanners, and protocols makes fully automatic semantic
segmentation a notoriously difficult problem.
Here, we present ${\Omega}$-Net
(Omega-Net): a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture for
simultaneous localization, transformation into a canonical orientation, and
semantic segmentation.
First, an initial segmentation is performed on the input
image, second, the features learned during this initial segmentation are used
to predict the parameters needed to transform the input image into a canonical
orientation, and third, a final segmentation is performed on the transformed
image.
In this work, ${\Omega}$-Nets of varying depths were trained to detect
five foreground classes in any of three clinical views (short axis, SA,
four-chamber, 4C, two-chamber, 2C), without prior knowledge of the view being
segmented.
The architecture was trained on a cohort of patients with
hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and healthy control subjects.

Current image segmentation techniques usually require that the user tune
several parameters in order to obtain maximum segmentation accuracy, a
computationally inefficient approach, especially when a large number of images
must be processed sequentially in daily practice.
The use of evolving fuzzy
systems for designing a method that automatically adjusts parameters to segment
medical images according to the quality expectation of expert users has been
proposed recently (Evolving fuzzy image segmentation EFIS).
However, EFIS
suffers from a few limitations when used in practice mainly due to some fixed
parameters.
For instance, EFIS depends on auto-detection of the object of
interest for feature calculation, a task that is highly application-dependent.

This shortcoming limits the applicability of EFIS, which was proposed with the
ultimate goal of offering a generic but adjustable segmentation scheme.
In this
paper, a new version of EFIS is proposed to overcome these limitations.

Deep learning methods have achieved promising performance in many areas, but
they are still struggling with noisy-labeled images during the training
process.
Considering that the annotation quality indispensably relies on great
expertise, the problem is even more crucial in the medical image domain.
How to
eliminate the disturbance from noisy labels for segmentation tasks without
further annotations is still a significant challenge.
In this paper, we
introduce our label quality evaluation strategy for deep neural networks
automatically assessing the quality of each label, which is not explicitly
provided, and training on clean-annotated ones.
We propose a solution for
network automatically evaluating the relative quality of the labels in the
training set and using good ones to tune the network parameters.
We also design
an overfitting control module to let the network maximally learn from the
precise annotations during the training process.

This paper presents a novel unsupervised domain adaptation framework, called
Synergistic Image and Feature Adaptation (SIFA), to effectively tackle the
problem of domain shift.
Domain adaptation has become an important and hot
topic in recent studies on deep learning, aiming to recover performance
degradation when applying the neural networks to new testing domains.
Our
proposed SIFA is an elegant learning diagram which presents synergistic fusion
of adaptations from both image and feature perspectives.
In particular, we
simultaneously transform the appearance of images across domains and enhance
domain-invariance of the extracted features towards the segmentation task.
The
feature encoder layers are shared by both perspectives to grasp their mutual
benefits during the end-to-end learning procedure.
Without using any annotation
from the target domain, the learning of our unified model is guided by
adversarial losses, with multiple discriminators employed from various aspects.

Interactive single-image segmentation is ubiquitous in the scientific and
commercial imaging software.
In this work, we focus on the single-image
segmentation problem only with some seeds such as scribbles.
Inspired by the
dynamic receptive field in the human being's visual system, we propose the
Gaussian dynamic convolution (GDC) to fast and efficiently aggregate the
contextual information for neural networks.
The core idea is randomly selecting
the spatial sampling area according to the Gaussian distribution offsets.
Our
GDC can be easily used as a module to build lightweight or complex segmentation
networks.
We adopt the proposed GDC to address the typical single-image
segmentation tasks.

text:
Recently, there has been focus on penalized log-likelihood covariance
estimation for sparse inverse covariance (precision) matrices.
The penalty is
responsible for inducing sparsity, and a very common choice is the convex $l_1$
norm.
However, the best estimator performance is not always achieved with this
penalty.
The most natural sparsity promoting "norm" is the non-convex $l_0$
penalty but its lack of convexity has deterred its use in sparse maximum
likelihood estimation.
In this paper we consider non-convex $l_0$ penalized
log-likelihood inverse covariance estimation and present a novel cyclic descent
algorithm for its optimization.
Convergence to a local minimizer is proved,
which is highly non-trivial, and we demonstrate via simulations the reduced
bias and superior quality of the $l_0$ penalty as compared to the $l_1$
penalty.

We study type one generalized complex and generalized Calabi--Yau manifolds.

We introduce a cohomology class that obstructs the existence of a globally
defined, closed 2-form which agrees with the symplectic form on the leaves of
the generalized complex structure, the twisting class.
We prove that in a
compact, type one, 4n-dimensional generalized complex manifold the Euler
characteristic must be even and equal to the signature modulo four.
The
generalized Calabi--Yau condition places much stronger constrains: a compact
type one generalized Calabi--Yau fibers over the 2-torus and if the structure
has one compact leaf, then this fibration can be chosen to be the fibration by
the symplectic leaves of the generalized complex structure.
If the twisting
class vanishes, one can always deform the structure so that it has a compact
leaf.

We propose a single chain slip-spring model, which is based on the
slip-spring model by Likhtman [A. E. Likhtman, Macromolecules, 38, 6128
(2005)], for fast rheology simulations of entangled polymers on a GPU.
We
modify the original slip-spring model slightly for efficient calculations on a
GPU.
Our model is designed to satisfy the detailed balance condition, which
enables us to analyze its static or linear response properties easily.
We
theoretically analyze several statistical properties of the model, such as the
linear response, which will be useful to analyze simulation data.
We show that
our model can reproduce several rheological properties such as the linear
viscoelasticity or the viscosity growth qualitatively.

In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning framework for anatomy
segmentation and automatic landmark- ing.
Specifically, we focus on the
challenging problem of mandible segmentation from cone-beam computed tomography
(CBCT) scans and identification of 9 anatomical landmarks of the mandible on
the geodesic space.
The overall approach employs three inter-related steps.
In
step 1, we propose a deep neu- ral network architecture with carefully designed
regularization, and network hyper-parameters to perform image segmentation
without the need for data augmentation and complex post- processing refinement.

In step 2, we formulate the landmark localization problem directly on the
geodesic space for sparsely- spaced anatomical landmarks.
In step 3, we propose
to use a long short-term memory (LSTM) network to identify closely- spaced
landmarks, which is rather difficult to obtain using other standard detection
networks.

Deep learning models are sensitive to domain shift phenomena.
A model trained
on images from one domain cannot generalise well when tested on images from a
different domain, despite capturing similar anatomical structures.
It is mainly
because the data distribution between the two domains is different.
Moreover,
creating annotation for every new modality is a tedious and time-consuming
task, which also suffers from high inter- and intra- observer variability.

Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) methods intend to reduce the gap between
source and target domains by leveraging source domain labelled data to generate
labels for the target domain.
However, current state-of-the-art (SOTA) UDA
methods demonstrate degraded performance when there is insufficient data in
source and target domains.

Minimal paths are regarded as a powerful and efficient tool for boundary
detection and image segmentation due to its global optimality and the
well-established numerical solutions such as fast marching method.
In this
paper, we introduce a flexible interactive image segmentation model based on
the Eikonal partial differential equation (PDE) framework in conjunction with
region-based homogeneity enhancement.
A key ingredient in the introduced model
is the construction of local geodesic metrics, which are capable of integrating
anisotropic and asymmetric edge features, implicit region-based homogeneity
features and/or curvature regularization.
The incorporation of the region-based
homogeneity features into the metrics considered relies on an implicit
representation of these features, which is one of the contributions of this
work.
Moreover, we also introduce a way to build simple closed contours as the
concatenation of two disjoint open curves.
Experimental results prove that the
proposed model indeed outperforms state-of-the-art minimal paths-based image
segmentation approaches.

text:
Few-shot segmentation (FSS) methods perform image segmentation for a
particular object class in a target (query) image, using a small set of
(support) image-mask pairs.
Recent deep neural network based FSS methods
leverage high-dimensional feature similarity between the foreground features of
the support images and the query image features.
In this work, we demonstrate
gaps in the utilization of this similarity information in existing methods, and
present a framework - SimPropNet, to bridge those gaps.
We propose to jointly
predict the support and query masks to force the support features to share
characteristics with the query features.
We also propose to utilize
similarities in the background regions of the query and support images using a
novel foreground-background attentive fusion mechanism.
Our method achieves
state-of-the-art results for one-shot and five-shot segmentation on the
PASCAL-5i dataset.

This paper presents a novel unsupervised segmentation method for 3D medical
images.
Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have brought significant advances
in image segmentation.
However, most of the recent methods rely on supervised
learning, which requires large amounts of manually annotated data.
Thus, it is
challenging for these methods to cope with the growing amount of medical
images.
This paper proposes a unified approach to unsupervised deep
representation learning and clustering for segmentation.
Our proposed method
consists of two phases.

text:
It has been widely recognized that the success of deep learning in image
segmentation relies overwhelmingly on a myriad amount of densely annotated
training data, which, however, are difficult to obtain due to the tremendous
labor and expertise required, particularly for annotating 3D medical images.

Although self-supervised learning (SSL) has shown great potential to address
this issue, most SSL approaches focus only on image-level global consistency,
but ignore the local consistency which plays a pivotal role in capturing
structural information for dense prediction tasks such as segmentation.
In this
paper, we propose a PriorGuided Local (PGL) self-supervised model that learns
the region-wise local consistency in the latent feature space.
Specifically, we
use the spatial transformations, which produce different augmented views of the
same image, as a prior to deduce the location relation between two views, which
is then used to align the feature maps of the same local region but being
extracted on two views.
Next, we construct a local consistency loss to minimize
the voxel-wise discrepancy between the aligned feature maps.
Thus, our PGL
model learns the distinctive representations of local regions, and hence is
able to retain structural information.

structural information for dense prediction tasks such as segmentation.
In this
paper, we propose a PriorGuided Local (PGL) self-supervised model that learns
the region-wise local consistency in the latent feature space.
Specifically, we
use the spatial transformations, which produce different augmented views of the
same image, as a prior to deduce the location relation between two views, which
is then used to align the feature maps of the same local region but being
extracted on two views.
Next, we construct a local consistency loss to minimize
the voxel-wise discrepancy between the aligned feature maps.
Thus, our PGL
model learns the distinctive representations of local regions, and hence is
able to retain structural information.

This paper introduces Progressively Diffused Networks (PDNs) for unifying
multi-scale context modeling with deep feature learning, by taking semantic
image segmentation as an exemplar application.
Prior neural networks, such as
ResNet, tend to enhance representational power by increasing the depth of
architectures and driving the training objective across layers.
However, we
argue that spatial dependencies in different layers, which generally represent
the rich contexts among data elements, are also critical to building deep and
discriminative representations.
To this end, our PDNs enables to progressively
broadcast information over the learned feature maps by inserting a stack of
information diffusion layers, each of which exploits multi-dimensional
convolutional LSTMs (Long-Short-Term Memory Structures).
In each LSTM unit, a
special type of atrous filters are designed to capture the short range and long
range dependencies from various neighbors to a certain site of the feature map
and pass the accumulated information to the next layer.
From the extensive
experiments on semantic image segmentation benchmarks (e.g., ImageNet Parsing,
PASCAL VOC2012 and PASCAL-Part), our framework demonstrates the effectiveness
to substantially improve the performances over the popular existing neural
network models, and achieves state-of-the-art on ImageNet Parsing for large
scale semantic segmentation.

Deep neural networks have been a prevailing technique in the field of medical
image processing.
However, the most popular convolutional neural networks
(CNNs) based methods for medical image segmentation are imperfect because they
model long-range dependencies by stacking layers or enlarging filters.

Transformers and the self-attention mechanism are recently proposed to
effectively learn long-range dependencies by modeling all pairs of word-to-word
attention regardless of their positions.
The idea has also been extended to the
computer vision field by creating and treating image patches as embeddings.

Considering the computation complexity for whole image self-attention, current
transformer-based models settle for a rigid partitioning scheme that
potentially loses informative relations.
Besides, current medical transformers
model global context on full resolution images, leading to unnecessary
computation costs.

We present ObSuRF, a method which turns a single image of a scene into a 3D
model represented as a set of Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs), with each NeRF
corresponding to a different object.
A single forward pass of an encoder
network outputs a set of latent vectors describing the objects in the scene.

These vectors are used independently to condition a NeRF decoder, defining the
geometry and appearance of each object.
We make learning more computationally
efficient by deriving a novel loss, which allows training NeRFs on RGB-D inputs
without explicit ray marching.
After confirming that the model performs equal
or better than state of the art on three 2D image segmentation benchmarks, we
apply it to two multi-object 3D datasets: A multiview version of CLEVR, and a
novel dataset in which scenes are populated by ShapeNet models.
We find that
after training ObSuRF on RGB-D views of training scenes, it is capable of not
only recovering the 3D geometry of a scene depicted in a single input image,
but also to segment it into objects, despite receiving no supervision in that
regard.

text:
Non-invasive detection of cardiovascular disorders from radiology scans
requires quantitative image analysis of the heart and its substructures.
There
are well-established measurements that radiologists use for diseases assessment
such as ejection fraction, volume of four chambers, and myocardium mass.
These
measurements are derived as outcomes of precise segmentation of the heart and
its substructures.
The aim of this paper is to provide such measurements
through an accurate image segmentation algorithm that automatically delineates
seven substructures of the heart from MRI and/or CT scans.
Our proposed method
is based on multi-planar deep convolutional neural networks (CNN) with an
adaptive fusion strategy where we automatically utilize complementary
information from different planes of the 3D scans for improved delineations.

For CT and MRI, we have separately designed three CNNs (the same architectural
configuration) for three planes, and have trained the networks from scratch for
voxel-wise labeling for the following cardiac structures: myocardium of left
ventricle (Myo), left atrium (LA), left ventricle (LV), right atrium (RA),
right ventricle (RV), ascending aorta (Ao), and main pulmonary artery (PA).

The graph Laplacian is a standard tool in data science, machine learning, and
image processing.
The corresponding matrix inherits the complex structure of
the underlying network and is in certain applications densely populated.
This
makes computations, in particular matrix-vector products, with the graph
Laplacian a hard task.
A typical application is the computation of a number of
its eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
Standard methods become infeasible as the
number of nodes in the graph is too large.

Multi-modal learning is typically performed with network architectures
containing modality-specific layers and shared layers, utilizing co-registered
images of different modalities.
We propose a novel learning scheme for unpaired
cross-modality image segmentation, with a highly compact architecture achieving
superior segmentation accuracy.
In our method, we heavily reuse network
parameters, by sharing all convolutional kernels across CT and MRI, and only
employ modality-specific internal normalization layers which compute respective
statistics.
To effectively train such a highly compact model, we introduce a
novel loss term inspired by knowledge distillation, by explicitly constraining
the KL-divergence of our derived prediction distributions between modalities.

We have extensively validated our approach on two multi-class segmentation
problems: i) cardiac structure segmentation, and ii) abdominal organ
segmentation.
Different network settings, i.e., 2D dilated network and 3D
U-net, are utilized to investigate our method's general efficacy.

We present in this paper an image segmentation approach that combines a fuzzy
semantic region classification and a context based region-growing.
Input image
is first over-segmented.
Then, prior domain knowledge is used to perform a
fuzzy classification of these regions to provide a fuzzy semantic labeling.

This allows the proposed approach to operate at high level instead of using
low-level features and consequently to remedy to the problem of the semantic
gap.
Each over-segmented region is represented by a vector giving its
corresponding membership degrees to the different thematic labels and the whole
image is therefore represented by a Regions Partition Matrix.
The segmentation
is achieved on this matrix instead of the image pixels through two main phases:
focusing and propagation.

The Mahalanobis distance is commonly used in multi-object trackers for
measurement-to-track association.
Starting with the original definition of the
Mahalanobis distance we review its use in association.
Given that there is no
principle in multi-object tracking that sets the Mahalanobis distance apart as
a distinguished statistical distance we revisit the global association
hypotheses of multiple hypothesis tracking as the most general association
setting.
Those association hypotheses induce a distance-like quantity for
assignment which we refer to as association log-likelihood distance.
We compare
the ability of the Mahalanobis distance to the association log-likelihood
distance to yield correct association relations in Monte-Carlo simulations.
It
turns out that on average the distance based on association log-likelihood
performs better than the Mahalanobis distance, confirming that the maximization
of global association hypotheses is a more fundamental approach to association
than the minimization of a certain statistical distance measure.

We tackle biomedical image segmentation in the scenario of only a few labeled
brain MR images.
This is an important and challenging task in medical
applications, where manual annotations are time-consuming.
Current multi-atlas
based segmentation methods use image registration to warp segments from labeled
images onto a new scan.
In a different paradigm, supervised learning-based
segmentation strategies have gained popularity.
These method consistently use
relatively large sets of labeled training data, and their behavior in the
regime of a few labeled biomedical images has not been thoroughly evaluated.
In
this work, we provide two important results for segmentation in the scenario
where few labeled images are available.

text:
Image segmentation refers to the process to divide an image into
nonoverlapping meaningful regions according to human perception, which has
become a classic topic since the early ages of computer vision.
A lot of
research has been conducted and has resulted in many applications.
However,
while many segmentation algorithms exist, yet there are only a few sparse and
outdated summarizations available, an overview of the recent achievements and
issues is lacking.
We aim to provide a comprehensive review of the recent
progress in this field.
Covering 180 publications, we give an overview of broad
areas of segmentation topics including not only the classic bottom-up
approaches, but also the recent development in superpixel, interactive methods,
object proposals, semantic image parsing and image cosegmentation.
In addition,
we also review the existing influential datasets and evaluation metrics.

Co-occurrent visual pattern makes aggregating contextual information a common
paradigm to enhance the pixel representation for semantic image segmentation.

The existing approaches focus on modeling the context from the perspective of
the whole image, i.e., aggregating the image-level contextual information.

Despite impressive, these methods weaken the significance of the pixel
representations of the same category, i.e., the semantic-level contextual
information.
To address this, this paper proposes to augment the pixel
representations by aggregating the image-level and semantic-level contextual
information, respectively.
First, an image-level context module is designed to
capture the contextual information for each pixel in the whole image.
Second,
we aggregate the representations of the same category for each pixel where the
category regions are learned under the supervision of the ground-truth
segmentation.

Confusing classes that are ubiquitous in real world often degrade performance
for many vision related applications like object detection, classification, and
segmentation.
The confusion errors are not only caused by similar visual
patterns but also amplified by various factors during the training of our
designed models, such as reduced feature resolution in the encoding process or
imbalanced data distributions.
A large amount of deep learning based network
structures has been proposed in recent years to deal with these individual
factors and improve network performance.
However, to our knowledge, no existing
work in semantic image segmentation is designed to tackle confusion errors
explicitly.
In this paper, we present a novel and general network structure
that reduces confusion errors in more direct manner and apply the network for
semantic segmentation.
There are two major contributions in our network
structure: 1) We ensemble subnets with heterogeneous output spaces based on the
discriminative confusing groups.

The Active Contour Model (ACM) is a standard image analysis technique whose
numerous variants have attracted an enormous amount of research attention
across multiple fields.
Incorrectly, however, the ACM's
differential-equation-based formulation and prototypical dependence on user
initialization have been regarded as being largely incompatible with the
recently popular deep learning approaches to image segmentation.
This paper
introduces the first tight unification of these two paradigms.
In particular,
we devise Deep Convolutional Active Contours (DCAC), a truly end-to-end
trainable image segmentation framework comprising a Convolutional Neural
Network (CNN) and an ACM with learnable parameters.
The ACM's Eulerian energy
functional includes per-pixel parameter maps predicted by the backbone CNN,
which also initializes the ACM.
Importantly, both the CNN and ACM components
are fully implemented in TensorFlow, and the entire DCAC architecture is
end-to-end automatically differentiable and backpropagation trainable without
user intervention.
